items.title: Early Detection and Surveillance of the SARS-CoV-2 Variant BA.3.2 — Worldwide, November 2024–February 2026
items.summary: The paper examined the emergence and early spread of the SARS-CoV-2 variant BA.3.2, which was first identified in South Africa and subsequently detected across multiple countries. Researchers employed a multimodal genomic surveillance strategy incorporating traveler-based surveillance, clinical specimen testing, airplane wastewater sampling, and community wastewater monitoring to track the variant's introduction and circulation within the United States and internationally. BA.3.2 carries a large number of substitutions and deletions in the spike protein relative to the antigens used in current COVID-19 vaccines, raising concern that it may reduce protection conferred by prior infection or vaccination. Surveillance detected the variant in traveler swabs, clinical patient samples, and wastewater samples spanning numerous states, with international reporting from more than twenty countries. The authors conclude that continued genomic surveillance is essential to monitor the evolution of SARS-CoV-2 and assess the public health implications of this variant.
items.venue: MMWR Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report
items.citation: Mila Shakya, Kevin C. Ma, Laura J. Hughes et al.. Early Detection and Surveillance of the SARS-CoV-2 Variant BA.3.2 — Worldwide, November 2024–February 2026. MMWR Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report. 2026

items.title: Metagenomic Sequencing for Wastewater-Based Surveillance: Modeling and Experimental Approaches for Determining Limit of Detection
items.summary: This paper investigated the performance characteristics of metagenomic next-generation sequencing as a tool for wastewater-based surveillance, with a particular focus on establishing limits of detection. The researchers developed a computational model of a local wastewater system and conducted two types of experiments: laboratory-spiked experiments in which a test organism was introduced into real-world wastewater samples under controlled conditions, and system-spiked experiments in which the organism was introduced at an actual source location within a real wastewater system. The study found that detection performance varies depending on the sequencing method chosen and the data analysis pipeline applied. Importantly, the findings highlight that site-specific method characterization is necessary when deploying metagenomic sequencing for surveillance, because differences in wastewater system configuration, background microbial communities, and sequencing inhibitors can meaningfully affect results. The work addresses a key gap in understanding why metagenomic sequencing, despite its potential for broad pathogen detection beyond predefined targets, has not yet been widely adopted for routine wastewater surveillance.
items.citation: Xiao A, Besse K, Connors D et al.. Metagenomic Sequencing for Wastewater-Based Surveillance: Modeling and Experimental Approaches for Determining Limit of Detection. 2026

items.title: Wastewater Metagenomics for Antimicrobial Resistance and Pathogen Surveillance: A Bibliometric Analysis.
items.summary: This study examined the global research landscape at the intersection of wastewater metagenomics, antimicrobial resistance, and pathogen surveillance using a bibliometric approach. The researchers retrieved over a thousand publications from a major scientific database and applied network analysis software to map publication trends, country contributions, keyword evolution, and literature co-citation patterns across roughly fifteen years. Publication output grew dramatically over the study period, with the majority of output concentrated in the most recent years, reflecting accelerated interest following the COVID-19 pandemic and the rise of wastewater-based epidemiological surveillance. Thematic analysis revealed a progression from basic detection of antibiotic resistance genes in wastewater treatment systems toward broader concerns about dissemination mechanisms and One Health frameworks, while co-citation analysis indicated that integration between environmental monitoring and public health literature remains limited. The authors conclude that key priorities for the field include standardizing analytical methods, incorporating artificial intelligence for resistome analysis, improving participation from underrepresented regions, and operationalizing One Health surveillance to translate wastewater monitoring data into actionable public health interventions.
items.citation: Zheng Y, Ma N, Zhao B et al.. Wastewater Metagenomics for Antimicrobial Resistance and Pathogen Surveillance: A Bibliometric Analysis.. Microorganisms. 2026

items.title: Clade-specific multiplex digital PCR assay for monkeypox virus detection in spike-in wastewater samples.
items.summary: The paper developed and validated a multiplex digital PCR assay for detecting and quantifying monkeypox virus in wastewater samples, with the ability to distinguish between major viral clades and subclades. This capability is epidemiologically important because different clades vary in transmissibility and mortality, and wastewater-based surveillance offers population-level monitoring independent of individual clinical testing. The four-plex assay was evaluated for linearity, analytical sensitivity, and specificity using spike-in wastewater samples, demonstrating low detection limits across all targets. The authors conclude that the assay is suitable for both clinical and wastewater surveillance applications, offering a tool for tracking monkeypox virus dynamics at the clade level.
items.citation: Pitton M, Gan C, Schmidhalter P et al.. Clade-specific multiplex digital PCR assay for monkeypox virus detection in spike-in wastewater samples.. Access microbiology. 2026

items.title: Validation of molecular detection of <i>Candida auris</i> from wastewater.
items.summary: The paper studied whether an existing quantitative PCR assay developed for clinical *Candida auris* colonization screening could be adapted to detect this multidrug-resistant fungal pathogen in wastewater samples. The researchers validated the qPCR workflow using a wastewater matrix, assessing amplification efficiency, sensitivity, and reproducibility. The assay demonstrated high PCR efficiency, a very low limit of detection, and strong reproducibility across tests. These findings indicate that the clinical colonization assay can be reliably repurposed for wastewater surveillance, offering a more cost-effective approach to monitoring *C. auris* prevalence across entire healthcare systems without relying solely on individual patient screening.
items.citation: Rodríguez Stewart RM, Litvintseva AP, Chavez J et al.. Validation of molecular detection of <i>Candida auris</i> from wastewater.. Microbiology spectrum. 2026

items.title: Inferring variant-specific effective reproduction numbers from combined case and sequencing data
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of accurately estimating the transmission dynamics of co-circulating SARS-CoV-2 variants. The authors developed a method that jointly analyzes confirmed case counts alongside genetic sequencing data to estimate variant-specific effective reproduction numbers and variant frequencies simultaneously, rather than relying on sequence frequency data alone. The approach also allows for inferring structured relationships across time series, enabling estimation of fixed growth advantages for specific variants across different geographic locations. Applying this framework to data from United States states over more than a year of the pandemic, they estimated effective reproduction numbers for multiple variants of concern and interest and identified consistent growth advantages of particular variants across locations. The work demonstrates that combining case and sequencing data yields richer epidemiological insights than either data source alone.
items.citation: Marlin D Figgins, Trevor Bedford. Inferring variant-specific effective reproduction numbers from combined case and sequencing data. eLife. 2026

items.title: The WHO priority list of antibiotic-resistant bacteria: challenges and opportunities for next-generation antimicrobial development
items.summary: This narrative review examines the global crisis of antimicrobial resistance as framed by the World Health Organization's priority lists of antibiotic-resistant bacteria, which were established to direct research and drug development efforts. The authors synthesize current understanding of the molecular mechanisms by which these pathogens evade existing antibiotics, including reduced membrane permeability, efflux pump overexpression, enzymatic inactivation, target modification, biofilm formation, and horizontal gene transfer. The review critically evaluates why conventional antibiotic discovery pipelines have largely failed and assesses emerging therapeutic strategies such as artificial intelligence-assisted drug discovery, phage therapy, antimicrobial peptides, CRISPR-based systems, and natural product-derived compounds, while addressing practical challenges including toxicity, delivery, dosing, resistance emergence, and regulatory barriers. The authors also emphasize the importance of antimicrobial stewardship, surveillance systems, and a One Health framework that integrates human, animal, and environmental health sectors. Their overarching conclusion is that overcoming resistance in priority pathogens will require coordinated, multidisciplinary approaches spanning molecular biology, pharmacology, clinical translation, and public health policy.
items.citation: Emad M. Abdallah, Abdulrahman Mohammed Alhudhaibi, Mahmoud M. Dahab et al.. The WHO priority list of antibiotic-resistant bacteria: challenges and opportunities for next-generation antimicrobial development. Frontiers in Pharmacology. 2026

items.title: Mobile Genetic Elements as Central Drivers of Antimicrobial Resistance: Molecular Mechanisms, Evolutionary Ecology, One Health Implications and Control Strategies
items.summary: This review examines the role of mobile genetic elements in driving the global spread of antimicrobial resistance across bacterial species and ecosystems. The authors conducted a critical synthesis of recent genomic, epidemiological, and ecological studies, including case studies of clinically significant resistance outbreaks, to evaluate the types, mechanisms, and ecological drivers of mobile genetic element-mediated resistance gene dissemination. The review finds that plasmids, integrons, transposons, insertion sequences, integrative and conjugative elements, and prophages collectively act as hubs for the capture, recombination, and stabilization of antibiotic resistance genes, enabling the emergence of multidrug-resistant and extensively drug-resistant pathogens. Ecological pressures such as antibiotics, heavy metals, and biocides further promote mobile genetic element activity, and One Health transmission pathways connect human, animal, and environmental reservoirs of resistance. The authors argue that linking these molecular insights to applied strategies — including genomic surveillance, mobile genetic element-targeted inhibitors, phage therapy, and CRISPR-based interventions — is essential for designing effective responses to the antimicrobial resistance crisis.
items.citation: Hemayet Hossain, Md. Hasan Ali, Tanvir Ahmad et al.. Mobile Genetic Elements as Central Drivers of Antimicrobial Resistance: Molecular Mechanisms, Evolutionary Ecology, One Health Implications and Control Strategies. Antibiotics. 2026

items.title: Postbiotics and phage synergy in precision oral microbiome engineering: systems biology strategies targeting Streptococcus mutans in dental caries
items.summary: This review examines the potential of postbiotics, defined as non-viable microbial products and metabolic derivatives, as targeted strategies for managing dental caries by modulating the oral microbiome. The authors focus on how postbiotic compounds such as organic acids, bacteriocins, and exopolysaccharides can reduce the acidogenic activity and biofilm integrity of Streptococcus mutans while preserving commensal microbial communities and influencing host mucosal immunity. The review synthesizes current knowledge on combining postbiotics with bacteriophage-based therapies, nanoformulation delivery systems, and bioadhesive matrices to improve site-specific efficacy against oral dysbiosis. It further highlights how multi-omics approaches, systems biology modeling, and artificial intelligence tools could enable personalized caries interventions tailored to individual microbial signatures, including modulation of viral–bacterial interactions and horizontal gene transfer that contribute to antimicrobial resistance. The authors conclude that realizing the clinical potential of these precision strategies will require resolving translational challenges related to formulation stability, safety, regulatory approval, and comprehensive profiling of the oral virome.
items.citation: Guhanraj Radhamanalan. Postbiotics and phage synergy in precision oral microbiome engineering: systems biology strategies targeting Streptococcus mutans in dental caries. Frontiers in Molecular Biosciences. 2026

items.title: Enterococcus Species: Multifaceted Probiotic Potential and Safety Considerations
items.summary: This paper examines the dual nature of *Enterococcus* species as both potentially beneficial microorganisms and safety concerns in human health and food systems. The authors conducted a comprehensive review of the existing literature on enterococci as commensal gut bacteria found across diverse hosts, environments, and food sources. The review covers their probiotic applications, including pathogen control, microbiome modulation, food fermentation enhancement, and production of bioactive compounds such as bacteriocins with antimicrobial properties. At the same time, the paper addresses serious safety concerns, particularly the association of certain enterococci with healthcare-associated infections and their role in spreading antimicrobial resistance. The authors conclude that while enterococci hold considerable promise as probiotics, antibiotic alternatives, and protective cultures, rigorous safety evaluations are essential before their broader deployment in agrifood and healthcare contexts.
items.citation: Ojonugwa Precious John, Kayode Olayinka Afolabi, Anayochukwu Chibuike Ngene et al.. Enterococcus Species: Multifaceted Probiotic Potential and Safety Considerations. Microorganisms. 2026

items.title: Interaction corrections to topological density three-point functions in two-dimensional Fermi liquids: a coadjoint orbit perspective
items.summary: This paper investigates how electron-electron interactions modify density three-point correlation functions in two-dimensional Fermi liquids, which are known to encode topological information about the Fermi sea geometry in the non-interacting case. The authors employ the coadjoint-orbit effective field theory framework, which reformulates fermionic loop calculations as tree-level diagrams in a bosonized language and allows systematic inclusion of generalized Landau interactions. By working to linear order in the generalized Landau interaction parameter, they demonstrate that a contribution proportional to the band curvature at the Fermi momentum emerges, altering the nonanalytic structure of the density three-point function beyond what is seen in either the free fermion case or the interacting Galilean-invariant system. This finding implies that interactions can, in principle, modify or obscure the topological information that the density three-point correlator was thought to reliably detect in non-interacting systems.
items.citation: Akshay Pal, Andrew Lucas, Umang Mehta. Interaction corrections to topological density three-point functions in two-dimensional Fermi liquids: a coadjoint orbit perspective. arXiv. 2026

items.title: How Long-Range Tails Reshape Non-Hermitian Spectra
items.summary: This paper investigates how exponentially decaying long-range hoppings, which are commonly truncated in tight-binding models, affect non-Hermitian systems under open boundary conditions. The authors demonstrate that even infinitesimally small long-range hopping tails can nonperturbatively reconstruct both the spectrum and eigenstates of short-range non-Hermitian systems, meaning the standard truncation approximation can fail catastrophically in this context. The underlying mechanism arises from a competition between the decay length of the long-range hoppings and the localization length of non-Hermitian skin modes, producing a sharp transition as the hopping decay rate is varied. To describe the reconstructed spectra, the authors introduce a squeezed generalized Brillouin zone framework in one dimension and a squeezed amoeba formulation in two or higher dimensions. They additionally show that long-range hoppings can qualitatively alter the Green's function in ways that are experimentally detectable.
items.citation: Ding Gu, Zhanpeng Fu, Yu-Min Hu et al.. How Long-Range Tails Reshape Non-Hermitian Spectra. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Advancing Interaction-Sensitive Feature Selection: Novel Relief-Based Algorithms, Expanded Comparisons, and Recommendations for Biomedical Data Mining
items.summary: This paper examined Relief-based algorithms (RBAs), a class of filter-based feature selection methods that can detect feature interactions while remaining computationally efficient, with a focus on their application to high-dimensional biomedical and genomic data. The researchers refactored and expanded the scikit-rebate Python package to include existing and newly proposed RBA variants implementing alternative strategies for neighbor selection and feature scoring, then conducted systematic benchmark comparisons across simulated genomic datasets varying in sample size, feature count, heritability, and association type. The refactoring effort produced substantial reductions in algorithm runtimes, and the newly introduced variants were among the strongest performers overall. RBAs using "far" scoring excelled at detecting two-way interactions but were less sensitive to main effects, while several algorithms including the newly introduced MultiSWRFDB demonstrated strong performance across both main effects and higher-order epistatic interactions. The study concludes that robust RBAs capable of retaining both main effects and feature interactions are valuable tools for preserving predictive signals prior to downstream biomedical modeling.
items.citation: Kia Kazemi-Nia, Harsh Bandhey, Philip J. Freda et al.. Advancing Interaction-Sensitive Feature Selection: Novel Relief-Based Algorithms, Expanded Comparisons, and Recommendations for Biomedical Data Mining. arXiv. 2026

items.title: ExoMOD II. A Statistical Model of Transit Timing Variations in Kepler Multi-Planet Systems
items.summary: This paper uses a forward-modeling population framework called ExoMOD, calibrated on Kepler photometric data, to statistically predict transit timing variations (TTVs) arising from gravitational interactions among planets in close-in multi-planet systems, then compares these predictions against TTVs actually measured in the Kepler dataset. The study finds that planet-planet interactions are insufficient to explain the observed short-period TTV signals, implying that most such signals must originate from some other physical mechanism. For long-period TTVs, which are more plausibly attributable to genuine gravitational perturbations between planets, the analysis reveals that singly-transiting planets harbor TTV-inducing companions nearly as frequently as doubly-transiting systems, arguing against orbital architectures dominated by intrinsic single-planet systems. Systems with higher observed multiplicities show elevated rates of long-period TTVs and low orbital gap complexity, suggesting their architectures preserve a record of formation conditions. The work positions this statistical TTV framework as a tool for creating a tighter feedback loop between observational data and theories of planetary system formation.
items.citation: David Nesvorny, Daniel A. Yahalomi, David Kipping et al.. ExoMOD II. A Statistical Model of Transit Timing Variations in Kepler Multi-Planet Systems. arXiv. 2026

items.title: ExoMOD I. A Forward Model for the Orbital Architecture of Kepler Multi-Planet Systems
items.summary: This paper develops a forward model to characterize the orbital architecture of close-in planetary systems observed by the Kepler telescope, addressing the inherent ambiguity introduced by the transit method's geometric bias toward edge-on orbits. The authors parameterize orbital excitation using Angular Momentum Deficit and model distributions of planet radii, masses, and orbital periods, fitting the model to Kepler's catalog using a nested sampling algorithm. They find that the orbital period distributions of systems with single detected planets differ statistically from those with multiple detected planets, potentially due to Kepler's observational baseline, and that high-multiplicity systems show correlated period ratios consistent with retained memory of formation conditions. The gap complexity metric proves useful for constraining orbital excitation distributions, and observed radius monotonicity trends are attributed largely to non-detections of smaller planets. The study concludes that a typical FGK dwarf in the Kepler field hosts on average roughly two to three planets within the studied radius and period ranges, with approximately half of detected planetary systems having at least one inner or intermediate-period planet missed by Kepler.
items.citation: David Nesvorny, Daniel A. Yahalomi, David Kipping et al.. ExoMOD I. A Forward Model for the Orbital Architecture of Kepler Multi-Planet Systems. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Analysis of Polynomial Threshold Functions on Random Regular Graphs: Computational Complexity of Detecting Noisy Random Lift
items.summary: The paper studies the computational complexity of a hypothesis testing problem: distinguishing a noisy random lift of a base regular graph from a uniformly random regular graph. To tackle this, the authors analyze low-degree polynomial threshold functions on random regular graphs, providing the first such analysis for this detection problem. A key technical contribution along the way is a new characterization of the distribution of short cycle counts in noisy random lifts up to logarithmic lengths, which generalizes several prior results on cycle count distributions in random regular graphs and random lifts. The findings contribute to understanding the statistical and computational limits of detecting structured random graph models within the framework of low-degree polynomial tests.
items.citation: Xifan Yu. Analysis of Polynomial Threshold Functions on Random Regular Graphs: Computational Complexity of Detecting Noisy Random Lift. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Research progress on nucleic acid amplification–based detection technologies for phytopathogenic fungi
items.summary: This review examines the landscape of nucleic acid amplification-based technologies developed for detecting phytopathogenic fungi, which are responsible for the vast majority of plant disease infections and cause substantial annual losses in global crop yields. The authors surveyed both thermal cycling methods, including conventional PCR, real-time quantitative PCR, and droplet digital PCR, and isothermal amplification platforms such as loop-mediated isothermal amplification and recombinase polymerase amplification. The review also covers next-generation hybrid approaches that couple isothermal amplification with CRISPR/Cas systems, such as RPA-CRISPR and LAMP-CRISPR assays. By evaluating the principles, strengths, and limitations of each technology, the authors conclude that isothermal and CRISPR-assisted platforms are particularly well-suited for field-deployable diagnostics with minimal instrumentation requirements, and that integrated workflows using these methods can support early diagnosis and precision management of fungal plant diseases.
items.citation: Baoyu Wang, Mei Liu, Hui Wang et al.. Research progress on nucleic acid amplification–based detection technologies for phytopathogenic fungi. Applied Microbiology and Biotechnology. 2026

items.title: Rapid and Sensitive Detection of <i>Schistosoma mansoni</i> in the Intermediate Snail Hosts Using Loop-Mediated Isothermal Amplification (LAMP) Diagnostics.
items.summary: The paper developed and evaluated a loop-mediated isothermal amplification assay targeting the mitochondrial NADH dehydrogenase subunit 1 gene of *Schistosoma mansoni* to improve detection of the parasite in its intermediate snail hosts. The assay was optimized under straightforward isothermal conditions and tested against both laboratory-infected *Biomphalaria* snails and field-collected snails from two sub-Saharan African countries, with performance compared to microscopy, conventional PCR, and real-time PCR. In laboratory settings the assay achieved complete specificity and high sensitivity, outperforming traditional microscopy and performing comparably to real-time PCR, while in field surveys it detected a higher proportion of infected snails than conventional PCR and identified infections entirely missed by parasitological methods. The authors conclude that this LAMP assay is a sensitive, specific, and practically deployable diagnostic tool suitable for routine surveillance of schistosomiasis transmission in snail populations.
items.citation: Li HM, Qin ZQ, Lv S et al.. Rapid and Sensitive Detection of <i>Schistosoma mansoni</i> in the Intermediate Snail Hosts Using Loop-Mediated Isothermal Amplification (LAMP) Diagnostics.. Tropical medicine and infectious disease. 2026

items.title: Development of a Novel <i>Pseudoperonospora cubensis</i>-Specific LAMP Assay for Rapid Field Detection and Surveillance of Cucurbit Downy Mildew.
items.citation: Waliullah S, Anwar MT, Ali E. Development of a Novel <i>Pseudoperonospora cubensis</i>-Specific LAMP Assay for Rapid Field Detection and Surveillance of Cucurbit Downy Mildew.. Journal of fungi (Basel, Switzerland). 2026

items.title: Broad-Temperature Polymerase in Nucleic Acid Amplification-Based Diagnostics: From Thermal Precision to Dynamic Conditions.
items.summary: This paper investigated nucleic acid amplification across a wide temperature range as an alternative to conventional methods requiring precise thermal control. The researchers developed a LAMP-based amplification approach using a Bst polymerase with strong strand displacement activity and broad thermostability, enabling DNA synthesis across a temperature spectrum from approximately the lower end of isothermal LAMP conditions to temperatures typical of PCR thermocycling. They demonstrated that amplification could be initiated at both high and low starting temperatures and sustained even under dynamic, fluctuating temperature profiles. The system was validated for detecting SARS-CoV-2 and *M. tuberculosis* genomic material, confirming its diagnostic utility. The authors propose this broad-temperature amplification platform as a promising tool for point-of-care and field diagnostics where maintaining strict thermal conditions is impractical.
items.citation: Hamidizadeh M, Bier FF. Broad-Temperature Polymerase in Nucleic Acid Amplification-Based Diagnostics: From Thermal Precision to Dynamic Conditions.. ACS sensors. 2026

items.title: Quantitative Loop-Mediated Isothermal Amplification (qLAMP) for the Rapid Discrimination of Normal and Cancerous Tissue Models: An Arduino-Based Portable Cancer Detection System Assisted by a pH Microelectrode.
items.summary: This paper investigated whether a portable, low-cost point-of-care system based on loop-mediated isothermal amplification could distinguish cancerous from normal tissue models through quantitative monitoring of gene expression. The researchers developed an Arduino-based device that tracks the trajectory of the LAMP reaction during its early phase, deriving a rate-of-amplification metric called the m-P3 value, and applied it to measure expression of four cancer-relevant genes across three-dimensional tissue spheroids derived from breast cancer, prostate cancer, and normal fibroblast cell lines. Using principal component analysis and clustering of the resulting m-P3 value sets, they demonstrated that the system could statistically discriminate between the different cell line-derived tissue models, with findings corroborated by quantitative PCR and immunostaining assays. The study establishes a proof-of-concept for using quantitative LAMP in a portable diagnostic platform capable of identifying or differentiating cancer tissues based on their gene expression profiles. The authors suggest the approach could be extended to other diseases characterized by altered gene expression in tissues or bodily fluids.
items.citation: Bravo-González S, Reyes-Cortés LM, Pérez-Alvarez KA et al.. Quantitative Loop-Mediated Isothermal Amplification (qLAMP) for the Rapid Discrimination of Normal and Cancerous Tissue Models: An Arduino-Based Portable Cancer Detection System Assisted by a pH Microelectrode.. Biosensors. 2026
