items.title: The analysis of natural gemstones and their synthetic counterparts using analytical spectroscopy methods
items.summary: This study examined whether analytical spectroscopy methods, specifically Raman spectroscopy, could reliably distinguish natural gemstones from their laboratory-grown synthetic counterparts across four major commercial stones: ruby, sapphire, emerald, and spinel. The researchers evaluated both a laboratory Raman spectrometer equipped with two different laser wavelengths and a portable Raman system, comparing their effectiveness as identification tools for gemstones produced by various manufacturing methods. The laboratory instrument successfully differentiated natural from synthetic gemstones and could determine geographic origin for stones of the same color, while emerald analysis required the shorter wavelength laser specifically. The portable system could distinguish between different stone types but lacked the sensitivity needed to differentiate natural from synthetic specimens. Raman spectroscopy was found to be a reliable and practical approach overall, given its non-destructive nature, minimal sample requirements, and reproducible results consistent with reference literature values.
items.venue: Edinburgh Napier Research Repository (Edinburgh Napier University)
items.citation: Raabell Shah. The analysis of natural gemstones and their synthetic counterparts using analytical spectroscopy methods. Edinburgh Napier Research Repository (Edinburgh Napier University). 2026

items.title: Porous material engineering through synthesis for smart sensor systems
items.summary: This review paper examines porous materials as a class of functional materials for next-generation sensor platforms, focusing on how their high surface areas, tunable pore structures, and chemical functionalization enable improved analyte detection. The authors systematically survey representative porous material categories, including metal oxides, polymers, and carbon-based systems, and analyze their synthesis strategies such as sol-gel processes, template-assisted methods, three-dimensional printing, and light-material interactions. Fundamental sensing mechanisms are discussed across electrical, electrochemical, and optical transduction pathways, connecting porous architecture design to enhanced sensitivity, selectivity, and lower detection limits. Applications reviewed span environmental monitoring, biomedical diagnostics, and smart packaging, where porous material-based sensors are reported to show faster response times, better analyte discrimination, and greater operational stability. The review synthesizes design principles and fabrication methodologies intended to guide future research and support practical deployment of advanced sensing technologies.
items.citation: Se Jin Choi, Sang Yoon Park, Kang Hyeon Kim et al.. Porous material engineering through synthesis for smart sensor systems. Microsystems & Nanoengineering. 2026

items.title: Viral metagenomics of synanthropic urban bats: A surveillance strategy for uncovering potentially zoonotic viruses
items.summary: Bats harbor a wide range of viruses with zoonotic potential, yet systematic surveillance of bat populations remains limited, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. This study developed a framework that integrates viral metagenomics into an existing passive rabies surveillance program in Brazil, using an algorithm to select representative bat specimens from thousands collected across a large state and subjecting paired tissue samples to nanopore sequencing. The approach detected nearly a hundred viral contigs spanning multiple viral families of public health concern, including coronaviruses, arenaviruses, and paramyxoviruses. Strikingly, the framework uncovered a previously unknown filovirus in bats from the Americas, demonstrating its capacity to identify novel pathogens relevant to epidemic preparedness. The method was further validated by multisectoral One Health experts as a scalable and cost-effective model suitable for national expansion and adaptable to resource-limited settings.
items.citation: Juliana Amorim Conselheiro, Filipe Romero Rebello Moreira, Gisely Toledo Barone et al.. Viral metagenomics of synanthropic urban bats: A surveillance strategy for uncovering potentially zoonotic viruses. One Health. 2026

items.title: Advances in low-cost electrochemical sensors for healthcare monitoring and diagnostics
items.summary: This review examines recent progress in low-cost electrochemical sensors designed for healthcare diagnostics and point-of-care testing, particularly in resource-limited settings. The authors surveyed advances in sensor design, materials selection, and fabrication methods, focusing on strategies that reduce costs while maintaining analytical performance. Key approaches identified include the use of carbon-based materials, conductive polymers, and plant-derived bioactive molecules as electrode components, alongside scalable manufacturing techniques such as screen printing and three-dimensional printing to produce disposable, portable devices. The review also covers the integration of these sensors with digital platforms for real-time monitoring and their application in detecting biomarkers relevant to chronic and infectious diseases including diabetes and cardiovascular conditions. The authors conclude that while challenges around sensor stability, specificity, and commercialization remain, affordable electrochemical sensors hold strong potential to broaden diagnostic accessibility and improve patient outcomes.
items.venue: Advances in Industrial and Engineering Chemistry
items.citation: B. Anuthra, Jasmine Ratan, Priyanka Gupta et al.. Advances in low-cost electrochemical sensors for healthcare monitoring and diagnostics. Advances in Industrial and Engineering Chemistry. 2026

items.title: Exact quantification of nonlocal magic
items.summary: This paper addresses a fundamental open question in quantum resource theory: how much "magic" (nonstabilizerness), the resource enabling universal quantum computation beyond Clifford circuits, is genuinely nonlocal — residing in the correlations between two parties rather than in their individual local degrees of freedom? The authors solve this problem exactly for the stabilizer fidelity by showing that the nonlocal magic of any pure multiqubit state equals the distance of its entanglement spectrum from the closest spectrum of Bell pairs. They further establish an unexpected connection to entanglement embezzlement, proving that a family of states can universally embezzle entanglement under local operations and classical communication if and only if its nonlocal magic diverges. A key finding is that the relevant property is not the total amount of entanglement but how the entanglement spectrum distributes its weight across factor-of-two windows of rank, which explains why critical chains and random-singlet states — both exhibiting identical logarithmic entanglement scaling — carry unbounded and vanishing nonlocal magic, respectively. The results make nonlocal magic an operationally meaningful and practically accessible quantity, computable via tensor-network methods and measurable experimentally through entanglement spectroscopy.
items.citation: Piotr Sierant. Exact quantification of nonlocal magic. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Hierarchical organization governs nonlinear mechanical reversibility in $ι$-carrageenan gels
items.summary: This study investigated how the molecular and mesoscale organization of ι-carrageenan gels controls their mechanical behavior under deformation, a question that had remained poorly understood despite the widespread use of these thermoreversible polysaccharide networks. The researchers characterized gels formed in potassium chloride solutions across a range of temperatures using both linear and nonlinear oscillatory rheology alongside normal-force measurements. They found that deeper quenches produce stiffer gels exhibiting pronounced strain stiffening before yielding, accompanied by negative normal forces that reveal the buildup of internal stresses. Strikingly, large deformations irreversibly suppressed strain stiffening while leaving the small-strain elastic modulus intact, indicating a partial mechanical reversibility that distinguishes two structural levels. The authors interpret this behavior through a hierarchical network model in which a robust intermolecular network governs linear elasticity while a more fragile mesoscale organization enables cooperative chain alignment and stress amplification, underscoring that nonlinear mechanics in such gels arise from reversible hierarchical structures rather than molecular connectivity alone.
items.citation: Thomas Gibaud, Loïc Hilliou. Hierarchical organization governs nonlinear mechanical reversibility in $ι$-carrageenan gels. arXiv. 2026

items.title: COVER: Identifiable Evaluation of Coalition Routing
items.summary: This paper addresses a methodological problem in evaluating multi-agent routing systems, where changing a team's composition confounds attempts to isolate the effect of routing decisions from downstream processing changes. The authors introduce an evaluation framework called COVER that establishes a fixed public information boundary, a frozen downstream processing stack, and a predeclared set of legal team compositions before any outcomes are generated, enabling identification of routing effects separate from other system changes. The approach distinguishes between prospective evaluations, which are binding and assumption-free for pairwise policy comparisons, and retrospective analyses, which lack the same inferential standing. Experiments across multiple benchmarks and task domains show that the framework can detect genuine routing improvements, but also exposes cases where apparent gains disappear or fail to meet predeclared performance criteria once the methodology is properly applied. The authors present COVER as an auditable measurement methodology that reveals selection headroom honestly rather than manufacturing spurious routing wins.
items.citation: Raghul Sugumar, Amrit Gopinath. COVER: Identifiable Evaluation of Coalition Routing. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Acquire, Repair, Preserve: A Diagnosis-Guided Post-Training Recipe for Small-Model Dialogue Game Agents
items.summary: This paper investigates how small language models can be improved as agents in interactive dialogue games, where success requires maintaining state across conversational turns, interpreting feedback, and selecting valid actions under dynamic constraints. The authors analyzed failure modes of a small open-weight model in a dialogue game challenge and found that errors fell into distinct categories, including repeated guesses, malformed actions, and violations of recently received feedback. To address these failures, they developed a three-stage post-training recipe: broad game participation through supervised fine-tuning, targeted repair of mechanically verifiable errors using turn-local preference pairs within a specific game family, and preservation of general capabilities outside the dialogue game domain. The approach substantially improved performance on both public and closed in-domain evaluations while approximately maintaining baseline aggregate performance on static benchmarks. The results indicate that supervised fine-tuning contributes the majority of capability gains, that turn-local preference learning transfers primarily within the targeted game family rather than broadly, and that out-of-domain dialogue game performance remains limited.
items.citation: Nan Li. Acquire, Repair, Preserve: A Diagnosis-Guided Post-Training Recipe for Small-Model Dialogue Game Agents. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Follow-up of SN 2025wny V: Lens Modelling and Cosmography of a Strongly Lensed Superluminous Supernova at $z = 2.015$ using Space Data
items.summary: This paper presents a lensing and cosmographic analysis of a strongly lensed Type I superluminous supernova multiply imaged by two foreground galaxies, making it a rare and valuable system for cosmology. Using imaging from the Hubble Space Telescope and the James Webb Space Telescope, the researchers modeled the lens system with elliptical power-law mass distributions and an external shear component, incorporating both the supernova image positions and the surface-brightness distribution of the lensed host galaxy. The analysis accounted for microlensing by stars in the lens galaxies and found total magnifications spanning a broad range. By combining the lens models with spectroscopically and photometrically measured time delays, the study derived constraints on the Hubble constant that fall between approximately 67 and 71 kilometers per second per megaparsec depending on the assumed lens mass parameterization, though these values remain sensitive to the adopted priors, density slope assumptions, and potential contributions from the large-scale environment. The authors conclude that future stellar kinematic measurements and better characterization of the lens environment will enhance the system's power as an independent cosmological probe.
items.citation: Edvard Mörtsell, Joel Johansson, Ariel Goobar et al.. Follow-up of SN 2025wny V: Lens Modelling and Cosmography of a Strongly Lensed Superluminous Supernova at $z = 2.015$ using Space Data. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Kerr nonlinearity and three-wave mixing in superconducting resonators hosting Al-InAs weak links
items.summary: This paper investigates superconducting microwave resonators that incorporate weak links made from aluminum-capped indium arsenide nanowires as a platform for engineered quantum nonlinearities. The researchers characterized how the Kerr (quartic) nonlinearity depends on magnetic flux and gate voltage, demonstrating that it can be tuned to zero using either control parameter. They also experimentally demonstrated three-wave mixing, confirming the presence of a cubic nonlinearity in this semiconductor-superconductor hybrid architecture. An effective theoretical model based on Andreev bound states qualitatively reproduced the observed behavior. The results establish these hybrid devices as a promising and tunable platform for parametric amplification, bosonic mode control, and engineered microwave mode interactions.
items.citation: Vittorio Buccheri, Ivo P. C. Cools, Nermin Trnjanin et al.. Kerr nonlinearity and three-wave mixing in superconducting resonators hosting Al-InAs weak links. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Comprehensive Review on Candidemia: Epidemiology, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Future Directions
items.summary: This review examines candidemia, a major cause of hospital-acquired bloodstream infections characterized by high mortality and significant healthcare burden. The authors synthesize current knowledge spanning epidemiology, species distribution, and infection origins, alongside an evaluation of existing diagnostic methods and their limitations. The review critically assesses emerging diagnostic technologies alongside therapeutic strategies, including empiric and targeted antifungal regimens, management of mixed infections, and the growing problem of antifungal resistance, with particular attention to the potential of combination therapy. Advances in antifungal drug development are highlighted, including agents in clinical trials and those targeting novel fungal pathways. Looking forward, the review identifies artificial intelligence-assisted diagnostics, vaccine-based prophylaxis, and synergistic treatment approaches as promising directions for improving candidemia management.
items.citation: Haojie Dong, Minghui Song, Jingfang Sun et al.. Comprehensive Review on Candidemia: Epidemiology, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Future Directions. iFungi. 2026

items.title: Bedside identification of subphenotypes in acute respiratory failure (PHIND): a multicentre, observational cohort study
items.summary: This prospective multicentre observational study investigated whether inflammatory subphenotypes of acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) could be rapidly identified at the bedside and whether these subphenotypes would show meaningfully different clinical outcomes. Researchers enrolled adults with ARDS or acute hypoxaemic respiratory failure across intensive care units in the UK and Ireland, measuring plasma interleukin-6, soluble TNF receptor-1, and bicarbonate using a near-patient immunoanalyser with approximately one-hour turnaround, then classified patients into hyperinflammatory or hypoinflammatory subphenotypes using a validated logistic regression model. The hyperinflammatory subphenotype was identified in roughly one in five patients and carried substantially higher sixty-day mortality compared to the hypoinflammatory group, with the association remaining significant after adjustment for covariates. The study demonstrates that real-time bedside subphenotyping of ARDS is feasible and recapitulates the distinct outcomes previously described only through retrospective analyses, including differences in sepsis prevalence and metabolic acidosis. The authors argue these findings support the pursuit of precision medicine in ARDS and highlight the need for prospective interventional trials stratified by inflammatory subphenotype.
items.citation: Kiran Reddy, Pratik Sinha, David Antcliffe et al.. Bedside identification of subphenotypes in acute respiratory failure (PHIND): a multicentre, observational cohort study. The Lancet Respiratory Medicine. 2026

items.title: Mechanism-informed diagnostic accuracy of blood biomarkers for sepsis-associated encephalopathy: a systematic review and Bayesian diagnostic network meta-analysis.
items.summary: This systematic review investigated the diagnostic accuracy of blood biomarkers for sepsis-associated encephalopathy, a serious form of acute brain dysfunction occurring in sepsis patients. The authors conducted a PRISMA-compliant systematic review and Bayesian diagnostic network meta-analysis, searching multiple international databases and synthesizing evidence from studies with extractable diagnostic accuracy data, while stratifying findings by reference standard type and biomarker sampling timing relative to an anchor event. Blood-brain barrier and glial markers such as GFAP and S100β showed more balanced diagnostic discrimination than classic neuronal injury markers, while upstream immune and alarmin candidates ranked highest in Bayesian comparative analysis, suggesting a biologically coherent immune-to-neuronal cascade underlying the condition. However, several top-ranked biomarkers were supported by only single studies, thresholds and sampling contexts varied considerably across studies, and few studies examined whether biomarkers provide diagnostic value beyond established clinical predictors such as illness severity scores. The authors conclude that findings are hypothesis-generating rather than practice-changing, and call for prospective head-to-head validation studies using standardized phenotyping and anchor-based sampling to determine whether mechanism-staged biomarker panels offer incremental diagnostic utility.
items.citation: Zhang Q, Zhu R, Li Y et al.. Mechanism-informed diagnostic accuracy of blood biomarkers for sepsis-associated encephalopathy: a systematic review and Bayesian diagnostic network meta-analysis.. Frontiers in molecular neuroscience. 2026

items.title: Plasma and urinary sTREM-1 as biomarkers of sepsis-associated acute kidney injury in critically Ill children.
items.summary: This prospective observational cohort study investigated whether plasma and urinary levels of soluble triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells-1 (sTREM-1) could serve as early diagnostic biomarkers for sepsis-associated acute kidney injury in critically ill children admitted to a pediatric intensive care unit. Researchers measured sTREM-1 levels at the time of sepsis diagnosis and again at the time of acute kidney injury diagnosis in those who developed it, using established pediatric scoring criteria to define both conditions. Both plasma and urinary sTREM-1 levels were significantly elevated in children who subsequently developed sepsis-associated acute kidney injury compared to those who did not, with plasma sTREM-1 demonstrating better diagnostic accuracy than urinary sTREM-1 based on receiver operating characteristic analysis. Notably, both biomarkers rose further following acute kidney injury diagnosis, and urinary sTREM-1 also showed prognostic value for mortality in affected children. The authors conclude that sTREM-1 measurement at sepsis diagnosis may facilitate earlier risk stratification for acute kidney injury, potentially preceding detection by conventional creatinine- and urine output-based criteria.
items.citation: Magdy SM, El-Gawaad TA, Hussein FA et al.. Plasma and urinary sTREM-1 as biomarkers of sepsis-associated acute kidney injury in critically Ill children.. European journal of pediatrics. 2026

items.title: Diagnostic value of cystatin C in acute kidney injury among patients with sepsis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the diagnostic utility of cystatin C for the early detection of acute kidney injury in patients with sepsis. The researchers systematically searched electronic databases, assessed study quality using the QUADAS-2 tool, and performed a random-effects meta-analysis across seventeen eligible studies, constructing a summary receiver operating characteristic curve to quantify overall diagnostic performance. Cystatin C demonstrated good diagnostic accuracy for sepsis-associated acute kidney injury, with an area under the curve, sensitivity, and specificity all indicating strong performance. Subgroup analyses revealed that studies employing Sepsis 3.0 diagnostic criteria showed higher specificity and diagnostic odds ratios with less heterogeneity, and combining cystatin C with other biomarkers further enhanced diagnostic accuracy. The authors conclude that cystatin C is a promising early biomarker for this condition and supports its potential use in clinical practice, despite acknowledging residual heterogeneity among included studies.
items.citation: Cheng L, Zhang B, Hu X et al.. Diagnostic value of cystatin C in acute kidney injury among patients with sepsis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.. Frontiers in medicine. 2026

items.title: Pancreatic Stone Protein as an Emerging Biomarker in Paediatric Nosocomial and Postoperative Sepsis: An Integrative Review of Diagnostic and Prognostic Performance.
items.summary: This narrative review examined the diagnostic and prognostic value of pancreatic stone protein (PSP) as a biomarker for detecting sepsis and nosocomial infections in paediatric patients, a context where distinguishing true infection from postoperative sterile inflammation remains clinically difficult. The authors conducted a structured literature search across two major databases, screening studies published over a recent multi-year period and ultimately synthesising findings from over fifty studies meeting their inclusion criteria. The review found that PSP levels rise substantially in children with sepsis compared to those with non-infectious systemic inflammation, and that elevated PSP is associated with bacteraemia, organ dysfunction, and mortality. In multiple paediatric cohorts, PSP demonstrated diagnostic accuracy comparable to or superior to conventional markers such as C-reactive protein and procalcitonin, with particularly strong sensitivity and specificity reported in neonatal and other high-risk populations. The authors conclude that PSP is a promising early biomarker for paediatric sepsis but note that inter-study variability necessitates larger, prospective multicentre trials and integration of PSP into multimarker diagnostic frameworks before routine clinical adoption.
items.citation: Ramírez Quintana A, Gaman EL, Badea M et al.. Pancreatic Stone Protein as an Emerging Biomarker in Paediatric Nosocomial and Postoperative Sepsis: An Integrative Review of Diagnostic and Prognostic Performance.. International journal of molecular sciences. 2026

items.title: Early diagnostic accuracy of immature platelet fraction for sepsis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of the immature platelet fraction—a marker of bone marrow thrombopoietic activity—for the early identification of sepsis. The authors searched two major databases and identified a small number of studies meeting their inclusion criteria, performing pooled analyses of sensitivity, specificity, and diagnostic odds ratio, along with a subgroup analysis focused on adult populations. The meta-analysis found that the immature platelet fraction demonstrated only moderate diagnostic accuracy, with pooled sensitivity and specificity both around seventy percent and moderate heterogeneity across the included studies. The authors conclude that while the immature platelet fraction may serve as a complementary biomarker for sepsis, the limited number of available studies and methodological variability require cautious interpretation of these findings. They call for further standardized prospective research to clarify its clinical utility.
items.citation: Wiranata S, Manuaba IBAP, Supadmanaba IGP et al.. Early diagnostic accuracy of immature platelet fraction for sepsis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.. Hematology, transfusion and cell therapy. 2026

items.title: Diagnostic performance of interleukin-27 and C-reactive protein in neonatal sepsis: an updated systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated and compared the diagnostic accuracy of interleukin-27 (IL-27) and C-reactive protein (CRP) as biomarkers for neonatal sepsis, given that prior individual studies had produced inconsistent findings. The researchers searched major medical databases for controlled studies published over nearly three decades, following PRISMA guidelines, and pooled diagnostic performance data using standard meta-analytic tools including sensitivity, specificity, and summary receiver operating characteristic curves. The analysis, based on a set of controlled studies encompassing several hundred neonates, found that IL-27 achieved higher pooled sensitivity and specificity than CRP, with a notably greater area under the curve. These results indicate that IL-27 outperforms CRP in accurately identifying neonatal sepsis. The authors conclude that IL-27 may serve as a more reliable clinical biomarker for the early and accurate diagnosis of neonatal sepsis.
items.citation: Liu W, Zhang Y, Liu W et al.. Diagnostic performance of interleukin-27 and C-reactive protein in neonatal sepsis: an updated systematic review and meta-analysis.. Frontiers in pediatrics. 2026

items.title: Surviving Sepsis Campaign: International Guidelines for Management of Sepsis and Septic Shock 2026
items.summary: This paper presents the 2026 Surviving Sepsis Campaign international clinical practice guidelines for the management of sepsis and septic shock in adults. The guideline development committee, representing broad geographic and professional diversity including representation from low- and middle-income countries, systematically reviewed evidence across six clinical domains encompassing screening and early management, infection control, hemodynamics, respiratory support, adjunctive therapies, and goals of care. Evidence synthesis followed the GRADE methodology, with recommendations classified as strong or conditional based on the balance of desirable and undesirable effects, certainty of evidence, patient values, resource considerations, and equity. The guidelines incorporate principles of antimicrobial stewardship alongside recommendations for early identification and treatment, and extend their scope to include prehospital and immediate post-hospital settings. The resulting recommendations are intended to provide actionable, evidence-based guidance to clinicians and health systems to improve outcomes for the tens of millions of patients affected by sepsis annually.
items.citation: Hallie C. Prescott, Massimo Antonelli, Waleed Alhazzani et al.. Surviving Sepsis Campaign: International Guidelines for Management of Sepsis and Septic Shock 2026. Critical Care Medicine. 2026

items.title: Surviving Sepsis Campaign: international guidelines for management of sepsis and septic shock 2026
items.summary: The abstract provided is too thin to summarize meaningfully, containing only background epidemiological context about sepsis and a brief rationale for early treatment, without describing the specific recommendations, methods, or findings of the 2026 guidelines themselves.
items.citation: Hallie C. Prescott, Massimo Antonelli, Waleed Alhazzanic et al.. Surviving Sepsis Campaign: international guidelines for management of sepsis and septic shock 2026. Intensive Care Medicine. 2026

items.title: A systematic literature review on the effects of exercise on human Toll-like receptor expression
items.summary: This systematic review examined how different forms of exercise influence the expression of Toll-like receptors, a family of immune cell receptors central to inflammatory signalling that has been implicated in the link between physical inactivity, chronic low-grade inflammation, and non-communicable diseases. The authors conducted a comprehensive search of multiple databases, ultimately including studies that investigated exercise as an isolated intervention in humans, categorising findings by exercise modality and duration into acute and chronic resistance, aerobic, and combined exercise types. Acute resistance exercise generally appeared to upregulate TLR expression, whereas acute aerobic exercise tended toward neutral or downregulatory effects, particularly in healthy individuals. Chronic resistance and combined training programmes predominantly resulted in unchanged or decreased TLR levels, while chronic aerobic training produced mixed results with most measurements showing no significant change in expression. The authors conclude that exercise does interact with TLR signalling in a manner dependent on exercise characteristics, but highlight that substantial heterogeneity in study designs limits firm conclusions and that further research is needed to clarify the underlying mechanisms and pathophysiological implications.
items.citation: Kasper Favere, Matthias Bosman, Peter Delputte et al.. A systematic literature review on the effects of exercise on human Toll-like receptor expression. PubMed. 2026

items.title: Explainable AI in healthcare: a systematic review of XAI use cases in imaging, diagnostics, and rehabilitation
items.summary: This systematic review examined how explainable artificial intelligence methods are being applied across healthcare domains, specifically medical imaging, diagnostics, and rehabilitation. The authors searched major academic databases following established reporting guidelines, screening over a thousand records and ultimately synthesizing findings from several dozen empirical studies that employed XAI techniques alongside machine learning models. The review found a clear alignment between XAI methods and their application contexts, with gradient-based heatmap approaches such as Grad-CAM predominating in imaging tasks where spatial localization matters, while feature-attribution methods such as SHAP and LIME were favored for diagnostic and rehabilitation applications requiring case-level or global explanations. Many studies combined two or more XAI methods to cross-validate interpretations, reflecting a growing recognition that no single explainer is sufficient. The authors conclude that while current practice shows encouraging consistency in matching methods to modalities, broader adoption of standardized reporting, rigorous faithfulness assessments, and external validation will be necessary before these approaches can support trustworthy clinical deployment.
items.citation: Apoorva Aravindkumar, Marimuthu Ramadoss, Saqhibuddeen Ahmed Fakhruddin Ahmed et al.. Explainable AI in healthcare: a systematic review of XAI use cases in imaging, diagnostics, and rehabilitation. Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence. 2026

items.title: Renormalization-guided inverse blocking for lattice field generation: construction and validation
items.summary: This paper introduces a lattice field generation algorithm that inverts a renormalization-group blocking transformation to efficiently produce large-volume field configurations. The blocking transformation is optimized using a "perfect blocking" condition so that the coarser lattice follows a simple effective action, and it is decomposed into an invertible smoothing step followed by decimation. A conditional normalizing flow reconstructs the short-distance degrees of freedom lost during decimation, while a brief rethermalization corrects residual mismatches between the generated and target distributions. By applying this procedure recursively, the method enables a cascade upscaling strategy in which a small initial ensemble seeds progressively larger lattices without retraining. Testing in two-dimensional scalar field theory at criticality confirms stable upscaling across several orders of magnitude in lattice volume, with rethermalization tests showing that short-distance mismatches relax quickly while relevant thermal-direction mismatches relax more slowly, consistent with renormalization-group expectations.
items.citation: Anna Hasenfratz, Ethan T. Neil, Letizia Parato et al.. Renormalization-guided inverse blocking for lattice field generation: construction and validation. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Exact quantification of nonlocal magic
items.summary: This paper addresses the question of how much of a quantum state's "magic" (nonstabilizerness) arises from correlations between parties rather than from local degrees of freedom, a quantity termed nonlocal magic. The authors solve the previously intractable optimization problem of minimizing over all local bases by proving that, for the stabilizer fidelity, the nonlocal magic of any pure multiqubit state equals the distance of its entanglement spectrum from the closest spectrum of Bell pairs. They further establish a surprising connection to entanglement embezzlement, showing that a family of states can universally embezzle entanglement under local operations and classical communication if and only if its nonlocal magic diverges. Crucially, the relevant property is not the total amount of entanglement but how the entanglement spectrum distributes weight across factor-of-two windows of rank, which explains why critical chains and random-singlet states—despite sharing identical logarithmic entanglement scaling—carry unbounded and vanishing nonlocal magic, respectively. The authors argue that nonlocal magic is an operationally meaningful measure of quantum correlations that is accessible via tensor-network methods and entanglement spectroscopy experiments.
items.citation: Piotr Sierant. Exact quantification of nonlocal magic. arXiv. 2026

items.title: QUEST: A Query and Extraction System for Topics in Asylum Law Application Decisions
items.summary: The paper addresses the challenge of automatically identifying credibility-related factors in asylum application appeal decisions, which are long and legally complex documents where determining whether credibility influenced an original rejection is crucial for processing appeals. The authors developed QUEST, a system that frames this challenge as an information retrieval task, combining synthetic query generation, topic extraction, and relevance assessment to locate credibility indicators within two datasets of Danish asylum appeal materials. Beyond standard retrieval evaluation metrics, they introduced a novel domain-specific evaluation approach that assesses system performance specifically with respect to credibility factors rather than general topical relevance. Their findings show that evaluating system performance through this credibility-based lens reveals greater difficulty than standard metrics suggest, highlighting the inherent complexity of automatically extracting legally meaningful credibility assessments from asylum appeal documents.
items.citation: Maria Vlachou, Anna Murphy Høgenhaug, Mohammad N. S. Jahromi et al.. QUEST: A Query and Extraction System for Topics in Asylum Law Application Decisions. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Offline-Verifiable Accountability for Cross-Organization Agent Messaging: A Preserved Evidence-Bundle Approach
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of verifying accountability for cross-organization agent workflows when live systems are unavailable, untrusted, or controlled by a single party. The authors propose a preserved evidence-bundle model in which each workflow event carries policy-required evidence covering sender authentication, log commitments, witness-backed checkpoints, append-only continuity, delegation authorization, and optional receiver-signed receipts. A policy-controlled offline verifier then assesses whether a given bundle satisfies the selected evidence requirements without inferring delivery or receipt from transport behavior alone. Evaluation over a substantial set of complete workflows and preserved bundles showed that the verifier correctly rejected all corrupted or policy-insufficient bundles with no false acceptances, while checkpoint-context anchoring imposed the highest latency and delegation evidence required additional verification steps. The work advances evidence-based audit and dispute resolution by giving reviewers an offline, verifier-centered basis for assessing evidence sufficiency independent of any live platform.
items.citation: Adil Alshammari, Hayretdin Bahsi. Offline-Verifiable Accountability for Cross-Organization Agent Messaging: A Preserved Evidence-Bundle Approach. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Analysis of Polynomial Threshold Functions on Random Regular Graphs: Computational Complexity of Detecting Noisy Random Lift
items.summary: The paper investigates the computational problem of distinguishing a noisy random lift of a base regular graph from a uniformly random regular graph, using polynomial threshold functions as the analytical tool. The authors develop the first rigorous analysis of low-degree polynomial threshold functions in this hypothesis testing setting. As part of this work, they derive new results characterizing the distribution of short cycle counts in noisy random lifts up to logarithmic cycle lengths, which extends and generalizes several previously known results for random regular graphs and random lifts. The findings contribute to understanding the computational complexity of this detection problem by establishing what low-degree methods can and cannot achieve in this context.
items.citation: Xifan Yu. Analysis of Polynomial Threshold Functions on Random Regular Graphs: Computational Complexity of Detecting Noisy Random Lift. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Understanding Venture Capital Syndication in Information Technology Sectors: A Network Formation Perspective
items.summary: This paper examines how venture capital syndication networks form and evolve within United States information technology sectors, focusing on the mechanisms that drive co-investment relationships among investors. Using a comprehensive dyadic panel dataset spanning several decades across hardware, software, and hybrid subsectors, the researchers tested seven theorized mechanisms—including prior collaboration, shared partners, geographic proximity, and organizational similarity—using dyadic logit models and exponential random graph modeling. Prior collaboration emerged as the most consistent predictor of co-investment link formation across all subsectors, while shared partners, geographic proximity, and organizational-type similarity were also positively associated with new co-investment ties. Network closure and geographic homophily were further confirmed through whole-network modeling of a large software investor network. Together, the findings demonstrate that relational persistence, triadic closure, and homophily jointly shape the structural patterns of venture syndication networks in information technology finance.
items.citation: Liheng Tan, Zhengkai Tu, Prasanna Karhade. Understanding Venture Capital Syndication in Information Technology Sectors: A Network Formation Perspective. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Integrated evaluation of rapid diagnostic testing, genotypic-phenotypic resistance profiling, and AI-Assisted prediction models for antimicrobial stewardship and clinical outcomes in a resource-limited setting.
items.summary: This prospective observational study investigated whether combining rapid diagnostic testing, molecular resistance gene detection, and an artificial intelligence prediction model could improve antibiotic prescribing and patient outcomes compared to conventional susceptibility testing alone. The study enrolled adult patients with suspected bacterial infections at a hospital in Pakistan, measuring outcomes including time to effective therapy, antibiotic appropriateness, hospital length of stay, and mortality. Rapid diagnostics dramatically shortened the time to pathogen identification and to initiation of effective therapy compared to conventional methods, while appropriate antibiotic use increased substantially and broad-spectrum antibiotic use declined. The integrated approach was associated with meaningfully shorter hospital stays and lower mortality, and the AI model showed strong discriminative ability for predicting antimicrobial resistance. The authors conclude that this combined diagnostic strategy holds promise as a scalable and cost-effective tool for combating antimicrobial resistance, particularly in resource-limited healthcare settings.
items.citation: Hammad M, Arif R, Fardoos S et al.. Integrated evaluation of rapid diagnostic testing, genotypic-phenotypic resistance profiling, and AI-Assisted prediction models for antimicrobial stewardship and clinical outcomes in a resource-limited setting.. PloS one. 2026

items.title: Rapid diagnostics innovations for urinary tract infections using molecular biology, artificial intelligence and antimicrobial resistance surveillance: a comprehensive review.
items.summary: This review examines the current landscape and emerging innovations in diagnostic approaches for urinary tract infections, which present substantial clinical challenges due to high recurrence rates, microbial diversity, biofilm formation, and rapidly spreading antimicrobial resistance. The authors identify critical limitations of traditional culture-based diagnostics, particularly their slow turnaround times and inability to adequately resolve virulence and resistance factors, which drive inappropriate empirical antibiotic prescribing. The review surveys a range of advanced molecular diagnostic technologies, including nucleic acid amplification methods, biosensor-based platforms, microfluidic lab-on-chip systems, and omics-based approaches, with particular attention to their integration with artificial intelligence and machine learning for rapid, pathogen-specific detection and antibiotic susceptibility testing. The authors highlight how these combined technologies can improve diagnostic precision, guide targeted antimicrobial therapy, and support broader antimicrobial resistance surveillance and stewardship efforts. Challenges surrounding medical ethics, regulatory frameworks, and practical implementation are also addressed, with the authors arguing that next-generation AI-assisted diagnostics represent a transformative approach to managing antibiotic resistance in urinary tract infection care.
items.citation: Goyal S, Sharma P, Aggarwal D et al.. Rapid diagnostics innovations for urinary tract infections using molecular biology, artificial intelligence and antimicrobial resistance surveillance: a comprehensive review.. Molecular biology reports. 2026

items.title: Evaluation of an adapted relative growth method by MALDI-TOF MS for rapid determination of the susceptibility of <i>Escherichia coli</i> to levofloxacin.
items.summary: This study addressed the critical problem of slow antimicrobial susceptibility testing, which delays targeted treatment of bacterial infections, by developing a rapid diagnostic platform for determining *Escherichia coli* susceptibility to levofloxacin. The researchers created a framework called AI MedLab MS that combines dynamic MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry spectral analysis with a robust dynamic relative growth algorithm and machine learning to track how bacterial mass spectral profiles evolve over time during antibiotic exposure, rather than relying on single static measurements. A key innovation was analyzing the overall bacterial population rather than individual colonies, enabling detection of resistant subpopulations that could otherwise be missed. The platform was developed using clinical *E. coli* isolates and validated prospectively on an independent cohort, delivering susceptibility results within two hours. Validation demonstrated strong overall classification accuracy and particularly high precision for identifying resistant isolates, supporting the platform's potential clinical utility for rapid antimicrobial stewardship decision-making.
items.citation: Liu Y, Xie N, Hu W et al.. Evaluation of an adapted relative growth method by MALDI-TOF MS for rapid determination of the susceptibility of <i>Escherichia coli</i> to levofloxacin.. Microbiology spectrum. 2026

items.title: ERS/ESCMID state-of-the-science statement on the role of rapid diagnostic tests for the diagnosis and management of community-acquired lower respiratory tract infections.
items.summary: This paper presents a state-of-the-science statement from two major European respiratory and infectious disease societies examining the role of rapid diagnostic tests in managing community-acquired lower respiratory tract infections. Developed within the framework of a European Union–funded initiative aimed at combatting antimicrobial resistance, the work systematically reviews existing literature and current clinical practice on how these tests can support antibiotic stewardship. The statement evaluates the diagnostic accuracy of rapid tests for identifying causative pathogens, assesses the utility of biomarkers and clinical algorithms in guiding treatment decisions, and considers how the introduction of rapid diagnostics has altered our understanding of infection aetiology. It also addresses the downstream impact of incorporating rapid diagnostic tests into stewardship protocols on clinical outcomes. The overarching aim is to demonstrate how optimising antibiotic use through better diagnostics can reduce excess morbidity from respiratory infections and help curb the emergence of multidrug resistance.
items.citation: Polverino E, De Nardo P, Gentilotti E et al.. ERS/ESCMID state-of-the-science statement on the role of rapid diagnostic tests for the diagnosis and management of community-acquired lower respiratory tract infections.. The European respiratory journal. 2026

items.title: Preliminary Single-Center Evaluation of the Alifax Molecular Mouse Sepsis Panel for Rapid Detection of Bloodstream Pathogens.
items.summary: This study evaluated the diagnostic performance of the Alifax Molecular Mouse sepsis panel for rapidly detecting bloodstream pathogens and antimicrobial resistance genes directly from positive blood culture broths. In a prospective single-center study, positive blood culture specimens were analyzed using the panel's cartridges targeting Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria and major resistance genes, with results compared against both a conventional microbiological workflow (including MALDI-TOF identification and automated susceptibility testing) and the FilmArray BCID2 panel. The Molecular Mouse panel demonstrated moderate-to-good agreement with the routine protocol for both bacterial identification and resistance gene detection, and showed comparable agreement with the FilmArray BCID2. Notably, the panel generated clinically actionable results within approximately one hour, representing a substantial reduction in turnaround time compared to the conventional workflow, which requires one to two days. The authors conclude that the panel shows promise as a rapid adjunct to routine microbiological workflows for managing bloodstream infections.
items.citation: Han JH, Kim JK, Kim JO et al.. Preliminary Single-Center Evaluation of the Alifax Molecular Mouse Sepsis Panel for Rapid Detection of Bloodstream Pathogens.. Diagnostics (Basel, Switzerland). 2026

items.title: Antibiotic resistance in <i>Pseudomonas aeruginosa</i>: mechanisms, diagnostic challenges, and omics-based diagnostic solutions.
items.summary: This paper reviews the antibiotic resistance landscape of *Pseudomonas aeruginosa*, a multidrug-resistant opportunistic pathogen that poses severe threats to immunocompromised patients and contributes substantially to the global antimicrobial resistance burden. The authors examine the diverse intrinsic and adaptive mechanisms by which the organism evades antibiotics, including efflux pump overexpression, porin modification, enzymatic inactivation, target site alterations, and phenotypic adaptations such as biofilm and persister cell formation, as well as its capacity for horizontal gene transfer. The paper also critically assesses the limitations of conventional culture-based diagnostics, particularly their inability to rapidly detect heteroresistance and biofilm-associated tolerance. In response, the authors survey recent advances in omics-based approaches—spanning genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, and others—alongside microfluidic platforms and machine learning-driven artificial intelligence as more rapid and precise diagnostic alternatives. The authors conclude that integrating multiple omics technologies with advanced diagnostic platforms represents a promising strategy for comprehensive resistance profiling, though standardized protocols, clinical validation, and cost-effective implementation remain essential prerequisites for translating these approaches into clinical practice.
items.citation: Rahman MS, Wakeman CA. Antibiotic resistance in <i>Pseudomonas aeruginosa</i>: mechanisms, diagnostic challenges, and omics-based diagnostic solutions.. Frontiers in microbiology. 2026

items.title: Executive Summary: Surviving Sepsis Campaign: International Guidelines for Management of Sepsis and Septic Shock 2026
items.summary: The 2026 Surviving Sepsis Campaign guidelines represent an updated, comprehensive international guidance document for the identification and management of sepsis and septic shock in adult patients, developed using GRADE methodology with evidence synthesized through mid-2025. The guidelines encompass a total of one hundred twenty-nine statements spanning screening, infection management, hemodynamic support, respiratory care, adjunctive therapies, and long-term outcomes, with the majority being conditional recommendations. Notable new guidance includes suggestions for prehospital sepsis screening and antibiotic administration in patients with anticipated prolonged transport times, age-stratified mean arterial pressure targets favoring permissive hypotension in older patients, selective digestive tract decontamination in low-resistance settings, and active fluid removal following the acute resuscitation phase. Key changes from the prior iteration include a shift away from routine empiric antifungal therapy, updated flexibility permitting either invasive or noninvasive blood pressure monitoring, and a preference for crystalloids alone over supplemental albumin for fluid resuscitation in most patients. Several recommendations saw upgrades in strength or certainty of evidence, notably prolonged beta-lactam infusion and antimicrobial de-escalation, while others such as corticosteroid use and norepinephrine as first-line vasopressor were downgraded in strength or certainty based on updated evidence synthesis.
items.citation: Hallie C. Prescott, Massimo Antonelli, Waleed Alhazzani et al.. Executive Summary: Surviving Sepsis Campaign: International Guidelines for Management of Sepsis and Septic Shock 2026. Critical Care Medicine. 2026

items.title: Accelerating scientific discovery with Co-Scientist
items.summary: Co-Scientist is a multi-agent AI system built on Gemini that is designed to augment scientific discovery by generating, critiquing, and refining novel research hypotheses conditioned on user-defined research objectives and existing scientific evidence. The system features an asynchronous task execution framework for flexible compute scaling and a tournament evolution process through which hypotheses improve iteratively, with automated evaluations confirming that hypothesis quality increases as test-time compute scales. Although the system is general-purpose, its validation focused on three biomedical domains: drug repurposing, novel target discovery, and elucidating mechanisms of antimicrobial resistance. Notably, Co-Scientist identified new drug-repurposing candidates and synergistic combination therapies for acute myeloid leukaemia that were subsequently confirmed through in vitro experiments. These results are presented as evidence that such AI systems can meaningfully accelerate the hypothesis-generation stage of the scientific process.
items.citation: Juraj Gottweis, Wei‐Hung Weng, Alexander Daryin et al.. Accelerating scientific discovery with Co-Scientist. Nature. 2026

items.title: Smart wearable and implantable biosensors for continuous health monitoring: materials, biocompatibility, and AI integration
items.summary: This review examines the current landscape of smart wearable and implantable biosensors designed for continuous, real-time health monitoring in personalized and preventive medicine. The paper surveys advances in flexible, stretchable, and biocompatible materials that allow these devices to integrate seamlessly with the body over extended periods, alongside multimodal sensing approaches that simultaneously track multiple biophysical and biochemical signals. The review also addresses how artificial intelligence is being incorporated to improve signal processing and generate predictive health insights from the data collected. Despite these advances, the authors identify persistent challenges including motion artifacts, limited energy autonomy, data privacy concerns, and difficulties in clinical interpretability. The paper synthesizes findings across materials science, device architecture, and AI-assisted strategies to provide a comprehensive overview of the field's progress and remaining obstacles.
items.citation: Thirumalaisamy Suryaprabha, Chunghyeon Choi, Yanfang Wu et al.. Smart wearable and implantable biosensors for continuous health monitoring: materials, biocompatibility, and AI integration. npj Flexible Electronics. 2026

items.title: Biosensing technologies for foodborne pathogen detection and healthcare: principles, emerging materials, and intelligent platforms
items.summary: This review examines the current state and future directions of biosensing technologies designed to detect priority foodborne pathogens, including *Escherichia coli*, *Salmonella*, and *Listeria monocytogenes*, which remain persistent threats to global public health. The authors surveyed advances across electrochemical, optical, and microfluidic sensing modalities, with particular attention to how functional nanomaterials, aptamers, nanozymes, and surface engineering strategies have improved sensor sensitivity and specificity in complex food matrices. A central theme is the integration of artificial intelligence and machine learning with these platforms, enabling real-time analytics, intelligent pattern recognition, and high-throughput multiplexing that transform conventional detection tools into smart diagnostic devices. The review critically identifies persistent challenges such as matrix interference, bioreceptor instability, manufacturing scalability, and the absence of regulatory standardization, while proposing mitigation strategies including ratiometric sensing, microfluidic pre-treatment, explainable AI, and printable electronics. Looking forward, the authors advocate for self-powered biosensors, modular pathogen panel hubs, blockchain integration, and standardized validation pipelines as pathways toward robust, regulation-ready platforms for next-generation food safety monitoring.
items.citation: Purshottam J. Assudani, Balakrishnan . P., Anny Leema A et al.. Biosensing technologies for foodborne pathogen detection and healthcare: principles, emerging materials, and intelligent platforms. Microchimica Acta. 2026

items.title: Nanoparticles-based phototherapy systems: molecular mechanisms and clinical applications
items.summary: This review examines nanoparticle-based phototherapy systems, exploring how integrating nanoparticles with light-activated treatment modalities enhances therapeutic precision across a broad range of diseases. The authors survey the core components, classification schemes, and delivery platforms—including gold nanoparticles, liposomes, and dendrimers—that underpin photodynamic and photothermal therapies, with particular attention to how these constructs improve light absorption, targeting, and reactive oxygen species generation or localized heating. At the molecular level, the review dissects how light-triggered interventions induce oxidative stress, activate apoptotic and autophagic cascades, and modulate immune responses, with relevance not only to cancer but also to cardiovascular, neurodegenerative, metabolic, and autoimmune conditions. The authors also critically assess regulatory-approved agents and recent clinical trial findings, identifying key barriers to clinical translation such as nanoparticle optimization, effective light delivery, and regulatory challenges. Overall, the review positions nanoparticle-based phototherapy as a transformative, noninvasive strategy with broad therapeutic potential, provided that molecular insights and clinical advancements can be successfully integrated.
items.citation: Deepak S. Chauhan, Rajendra Prasad, Mukesh Dhanka et al.. Nanoparticles-based phototherapy systems: molecular mechanisms and clinical applications. Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy. 2026

items.title: A Similarity Theorem and Its Breakdown in Atomic Black Hole Accretion
items.summary: This paper investigates the mathematical structure underlying gas accretion onto a point mass embedded in atomic gas, demonstrating the existence of an exact similarity symmetry that holds even under time dependence, two-body atomic microphysics, and a broad class of radiation and feedback prescriptions. The symmetry is a joint rescaling of the black hole mass and ambient density that enlarges all spatial and temporal scales while leaving dimensionless flow profiles, optical depths, Eddington ratios, and variability patterns unchanged, and the authors prove this rescaling is unique within its class. A key dimensionless parameter is introduced, representing the fractional mass gained per Bondi time, which is shown to equal the expansion speed of the Bondi radius in units of the ambient sound speed, so that a value of unity corresponds to sonic dilation of the accretion radius. The paper demonstrates that any power-law retained accretion rate drives the system to this sonic threshold after a finite mass increase, after which the similarity-based description breaks down, and canonical hyper-Eddington accretion scenarios are found to have already crossed this boundary. The theorem unifies radiating Bondi and feedback-regulated accretion scalings into a common framework while precisely identifying the regime where a quasi-static, fixed-mass continuation of the solution loses validity.
items.citation: Marcus DuPont. A Similarity Theorem and Its Breakdown in Atomic Black Hole Accretion. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Exact quantification of nonlocal magic
items.summary: This paper addresses the question of how much "magic" (nonstabilizerness) — the resource enabling universal quantum computation beyond Clifford circuits — resides specifically in the correlations between two parties sharing a quantum state, rather than in their local degrees of freedom. The authors solve the longstanding optimization problem of minimizing magic over all local bases by deriving an exact formula for the nonlocal magic of pure multiqubit states in terms of stabilizer fidelity: it equals the distance of the state's entanglement spectrum from the closest spectrum of Bell pairs. They discover an unexpected connection to entanglement embezzlement, showing that a family of states can universally embezzle entanglement under local operations and classical communication if and only if its nonlocal magic diverges. Strikingly, the relevant property is not the total amount of entanglement but how the entanglement spectrum distributes weight across factor-of-two windows of rank, which explains why critical chains and random-singlet states — both exhibiting identical logarithmic entanglement scaling — carry unbounded and vanishing nonlocal magic, respectively. The authors argue that nonlocal magic is thus an operationally meaningful characteristic of quantum correlations, accessible via tensor-network simulations and entanglement spectroscopy experiments.
items.citation: Piotr Sierant. Exact quantification of nonlocal magic. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Automated Dislocation Detection in Electron Channelling Contrast Imaging: A Comparative Study of Rule-Based, Neural Network, and Deep Learning Approaches
items.summary: This paper investigated the automation of threading dislocation detection in semiconductor materials imaged via electron channelling contrast imaging (ECCI), a process that is traditionally slow due to reliance on manual analysis. The researchers benchmarked three automated detection pipelines — a classical rule-based computer vision approach, a convolutional neural network multi-stage classifier, and a single-stage YOLOv8 deep learning architecture — against a statistical ground truth derived from gallium nitride micrographs. The rule-based approach proved unreliable due to its need for extensive per-image tuning, and the CNN method achieved moderate accuracy but struggled with efficiency in high-density dislocation regions. YOLOv8 substantially outperformed the other methods, achieving near-complete counting accuracy, precision, and recall across thousands of dislocations with rapid inference times, after two domain-specific adaptations were implemented: an adaptive Gaussian tile-sizing algorithm to address scale sensitivity, and a substantially lowered confidence threshold that better reflected physical signal strength rather than classification ambiguity. The study demonstrates that a scale-adaptive, single-stage deep learning approach is practically viable for high-throughput quantitative defect characterisation in semiconductors.
items.citation: A. Holmes, C. Trager-Cowan, J. Bruckbauer et al.. Automated Dislocation Detection in Electron Channelling Contrast Imaging: A Comparative Study of Rule-Based, Neural Network, and Deep Learning Approaches. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Casimir-electrostatic pull-in in nanoelectromechanical actuators: Differentiable design sensitivities and the damping-dependent collapse boundary
items.summary: This paper investigates the pull-in instability of nanoelectromechanical actuators operating at sub-100-nanometer gaps, where electrostatic and Casimir (quantum vacuum) forces compete to destabilize the device. The authors address a longstanding gap in understanding: while the quasi-static fold bounding safe operation has been known analytically for decades, the dynamical pull-in threshold reached from rest, its dependence on mechanical damping, and the design sensitivities of either boundary were not available in closed form. To overcome numerical difficulties near the collapse singularity, the authors trained a physics-informed neural network using a coordinate transformation that maps the pull-in pole to infinity, enabling accurate differentiation of the surrogate model to extract voltage sensitivities and solve inverse design problems. They analytically prove that the dynamic pull-in boundary is bracketed by two closed-form curves, is nondecreasing with the damping ratio, and merges with the quasi-static fold once the damping ratio exceeds a specific threshold, with the gap closure following a precise power-law scaling. They also find that thermal corrections to the Casimir force at these length scales are negligible, falling far below even the classical-limit bound.
items.citation: N. S. Akintsov, A. P. Nevecheria, S. N. Andreev et al.. Casimir-electrostatic pull-in in nanoelectromechanical actuators: Differentiable design sensitivities and the damping-dependent collapse boundary. arXiv. 2026

items.title: COVER: Identifiable Evaluation of Coalition Routing
items.summary: This paper addresses a fundamental identification problem in evaluating multi-agent systems: when a team composition changes, it is impossible to attribute performance differences to routing decisions alone using end-to-end accuracy gaps. The authors introduce an evaluation framework called COVER that fixes a public information boundary, a downstream processing stack, and a finite legal team family before outcomes are generated, enabling identifiable measurement of routing effects separate from other system components. The framework distinguishes between pre-specified prospective controls and retrospective comparators, and defines oracle regret as the benchmark for assessing routing quality within a constrained setup. Empirical validation across multiple benchmarks and a tool-use environment demonstrates that the framework can reveal genuine selection headroom—cases where better routing would improve outcomes—while also exposing when apparent gains are artifacts of retrospective design choices rather than true routing improvements. The authors present COVER as an auditable measurement methodology that can expose routing shortcomings without falsely manufacturing routing wins.
items.citation: Raghul Sugumar, Amrit Gopinath. COVER: Identifiable Evaluation of Coalition Routing. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Acquire, Repair, Preserve: A Diagnosis-Guided Post-Training Recipe for Small-Model Dialogue Game Agents
items.summary: This paper investigates how small language models can be improved as agents in interactive dialogue games, where a model must maintain state across conversational turns, interpret feedback, and select valid actions under evolving constraints. The authors diagnosed failures of a small open-weight model in the LM Playschool Challenge, identifying not just broad knowledge gaps but also local decision errors such as repeated guesses, malformed actions, and violations of recently observed feedback. Based on these diagnostics, they developed a three-stage training recipe: supervised fine-tuning to acquire broad game participation, targeted preference learning using turn-local pairs to repair mechanically detectable failures within a specific dialogue-game family, and deliberate preservation of general capabilities outside the target domain. Their approach produced substantial improvements in both in-domain and public evaluation scores while approximately maintaining baseline performance on static benchmarks, though out-of-domain generalization remained limited. The results indicate that broad supervised fine-tuning contributes most of the capability gains, while targeted turn-level supervision offers additional benefit primarily when failure modes can be precisely identified and tend to transfer within rather than across game families.
items.citation: Nan Li. Acquire, Repair, Preserve: A Diagnosis-Guided Post-Training Recipe for Small-Model Dialogue Game Agents. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Advancing non-faradaic impedance biosensors: sensitivity enhancement strategies using microfluidics, multiscale labeling, and CMOS technology
items.summary: This review examines non-Faradaic impedance biosensors, which detect biological targets by measuring changes in electrical properties without requiring electrochemical reactions, making them simpler to operate than Faradaic counterparts but historically limited in sensitivity. The authors analyze three complementary strategies for overcoming this sensitivity bottleneck: enhancement using micro- and nanoparticle labeling, microfluidic integration to improve mass transport of analytes to sensor surfaces, and on-chip integration using complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor technology for high spatiotemporal resolution. By reviewing recent advances in each approach and their combined application, the paper documents dramatic improvements in detection capability, reaching femtomolar sensitivity for proteins and single-bacterium detection. The review also evaluates the strengths and limitations of each strategy and discusses how their synergistic combination could be further developed. The authors position this synthesis as a roadmap for deploying next-generation non-Faradaic biosensing platforms across healthcare diagnostics, environmental monitoring, and biomedical research.
items.citation: Nam-Seog Kim, Jungkyu Kim. Advancing non-faradaic impedance biosensors: sensitivity enhancement strategies using microfluidics, multiscale labeling, and CMOS technology. Microsystems & Nanoengineering. 2026

items.title: AI-Assisted Molecular Biosensors: Design Strategies for Wearable and Real-Time Monitoring
items.summary: This review examines the integration of artificial intelligence into molecular biosensor design, with a particular focus on wearable and real-time monitoring applications. The paper surveys how AI-driven approaches contribute across the full biosensor development pipeline, from biomarker discovery and receptor engineering to the optimization of plasmonic and nanophotonic sensing structures through forward prediction and inverse design. AI is shown to enhance the performance of optical, electrochemical, and microfluidic biosensing platforms by enabling automatic feature extraction, noise reduction, dimensionality reduction, and multimodal data fusion. These capabilities are highlighted as especially critical for wearable biosensors, where weak signals, motion artifacts, and variable physiological conditions demand robust and reliable real-time operation. The review synthesizes current advances in intelligent biosensing strategies and algorithms while outlining remaining challenges and future opportunities in the field.
items.citation: Sishi Zhu, Jie Zhang, Xuming He et al.. AI-Assisted Molecular Biosensors: Design Strategies for Wearable and Real-Time Monitoring. International Journal of Molecular Sciences. 2026

items.title: Fabrication of photoresist SU-8 pyrolyzed carbon electrodes and their integration in a microfluidic hematocrit detection system.
items.summary: This paper addressed limitations in fabricating pyrolyzed carbon microelectrodes from the photoresist SU-8 for use in microfluidic biosensing applications, particularly for hematocrit determination. The researchers developed a three-step pyrolysis protocol to overcome adhesion problems, geometric distortion, and limited surface area that plague conventional two-step approaches, and integrated the resulting low-aspect-ratio planar electrodes into a PDMS microfluidic device that measured current responses of red blood cells in saline under an applied voltage. Surface characterization revealed that the carbon electrodes exhibited substantially greater roughness and thickness compared to platinum electrodes, yielding a notable increase in electroactive surface area that reduced charge-transfer and concentration overpotentials. The device demonstrated precision and accuracy for hematocrit detection comparable to previously reported platinum-based systems, confirming functional equivalence without requiring noble metals or complex surface coatings. The work establishes a reproducible, scalable fabrication route for high-performance carbon microelectrodes suited to low-cost integrated diagnostic devices.
items.citation: Lee HY, Rogers JA, Kendrick C et al.. Fabrication of photoresist SU-8 pyrolyzed carbon electrodes and their integration in a microfluidic hematocrit detection system.. Biomedical microdevices. 2026

items.title: Zinc finger protein arrays in an epoxy-functionalized, pump-free microfluidic device for amplification-free, colorimetric detection of double-stranded DNA.
items.summary: This study developed a microfluidic biosensor platform for rapid, direct detection of pathogenic bacterial DNA without the need for amplification or DNA denaturation. The approach combines engineered zinc finger proteins, which bind specific double-stranded DNA sequences, with a sequence-enabled β-lactamase reassembly system that produces a colorimetric readout upon target recognition. The zinc finger proteins were covalently attached to epoxy-functionalized surfaces within a pump-free, capillary-driven microfluidic device, and were designed to target the *stx2* gene of *E. coli* O157. The device generated a visible color change from yellow to red upon target binding, achieved picomolar sensitivity, and demonstrated high specificity against non-cognate DNA sequences, with the entire assay completing in approximately ten minutes at ambient temperature. The authors conclude that this platform offers a practical, low-cost, instrument-free framework for translating programmable protein-DNA recognition into point-of-care pathogen detection.
items.citation: Bhuiyan SAM, Shumway R, Trinkle C et al.. Zinc finger protein arrays in an epoxy-functionalized, pump-free microfluidic device for amplification-free, colorimetric detection of double-stranded DNA.. The Analyst. 2026

items.title: Artificial Intelligence-Empowered Single-Cell Phenotyping for Rapid, Automated Pathogen Diagnostics.
items.summary: This paper developed an integrated diagnostic platform combining microfluidic technology with artificial intelligence to perform rapid bacterial identification and antimicrobial susceptibility testing at the single-cell level. The system uses a microfluidic device to expose individual bacterial cells to controlled antibiotic concentrations while capturing time-lapse phase-contrast microscopy images, which are then analyzed by a U-Net-based deep learning model that automatically segments and quantifies bacterial drug responses. The AI model demonstrated high accuracy in detecting individual Escherichia coli cells with negligible false-positive predictions, and the full platform determined dose-dependent growth inhibition profiles and minimum inhibitory concentrations for two antibiotics within two hours, compared to the one to two days required by conventional methods. Results were consistent with standard broth microdilution testing, validating the platform's accuracy. The system was also evaluated for automated species identification of both gram-negative and gram-positive bacteria in blood matrices, suggesting broader applicability for rapid clinical pathogen diagnostics.
items.citation: Khadka S, Raahat B, Tragoudas S et al.. Artificial Intelligence-Empowered Single-Cell Phenotyping for Rapid, Automated Pathogen Diagnostics.. Advanced science (Weinheim, Baden-Wurttemberg, Germany). 2026

items.title: Smart wearable and implantable biosensors for continuous health monitoring: materials, biocompatibility, and AI integration
items.summary: This review examines the current state of smart wearable and implantable biosensors designed for continuous, real-time monitoring of biophysical and biochemical signals in the context of personalized and preventive healthcare. items.title: Comprehensive Review on Candidemia: Epidemiology, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Future Directions
items.summary: This review paper examines candidemia, a serious bloodstream infection caused by *Candida* species that represents a major source of hospital-acquired infections with high mortality and significant healthcare burden. The authors conducted a comprehensive literature synthesis covering the epidemiology, species distribution, and origins of candidemia, alongside an evaluation of current diagnostic methods and their limitations. The review critically assesses emerging diagnostic technologies and therapeutic strategies, including empiric and targeted antifungal regimens, management of mixed infections, host-drug interactions, and the growing challenge of antifungal resistance. Combination therapy and novel antifungal agents currently in clinical development, particularly those targeting new fungal pathways, are highlighted as promising avenues to address resistance. The authors also explore future directions including the application of artificial intelligence to diagnostics, vaccine-based prophylaxis, and synergistic treatment approaches, with the goal of guiding clinicians and researchers in managing this evolving clinical challenge.
items.citation: Haojie Dong, Minghui Song, Jingfang Sun et al.. Comprehensive Review on Candidemia: Epidemiology, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Future Directions. iFungi. 2026
