items.title: Hardware-Efficient Error Mitigation and Shot-Efficient Sampling on IBM Quantum Hardware
items.summary: This paper experimentally investigates error mitigation techniques and finite-shot sampling strategies on superconducting quantum hardware under realistic execution constraints. The study combines multiple methods — including calibration-aware qubit selection, zero-noise extrapolation, dynamical decoupling, readout-error mitigation, and optimized shot allocation — running experiments across ideal simulation, noise-model simulation, and physical device execution to isolate different sources of error. The researchers examined how mitigation performance varies with circuit depth, noise scale, qubit connectivity, and measurement budget, assessing accuracy through metrics such as expectation-value error, mean-squared error, and mitigation gain. A key finding is that the benefit of error mitigation is not universal: there are regimes where finite-shot fluctuations offset the advantages gained from additional mitigation overhead. The work provides a hardware-aware characterization of when error mitigation genuinely improves expectation-value estimation on current quantum processors, implemented using contemporary Qiskit and IBM Quantum Runtime workflows for reproducibility.
items.citation: Sumit Chongder. Hardware-Efficient Error Mitigation and Shot-Efficient Sampling on IBM Quantum Hardware. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Targeted Power System Frequency Attack via the Selection of Maliciously Controlled Inverters
items.summary: This paper investigates how an adversary could strategically compromise a subset of inverter-based resources to destabilize targeted generators in a power system through a frequency attack. The attack is designed by engineering an unstable oscillatory mode whose eigenvector concentrates energy at the target generators while minimizing signatures at the compromised devices, making the attack both effective and harder to detect. The authors formalize this adversarial selection problem as a mixed-integer quadratically constrained program and develop two heuristic algorithms based on a ranking metric to make the otherwise combinatorially intractable problem computationally feasible. Validation on modified large-scale test systems through nonlinear dynamic simulations shows that the proposed heuristics recover optimal attacking device sets in most evaluated scenarios while substantially reducing computation time. The study also examines how the choice of eigenvalue targets, generator targets, and the number of compromised devices collectively influence the severity of the attack.
items.citation: Xiangyu Zou, Betelihem Ashebo, Daniel K. Molzahn. Targeted Power System Frequency Attack via the Selection of Maliciously Controlled Inverters. arXiv. 2026

items.summary: This paper investigates the pull-in instability of nanoelectromechanical actuators operating at sub-100-nanometer gaps, where competing electrostatic and Casimir (quantum vacuum) forces determine when the device collapses. The authors developed a physics-informed neural network trained using a rapidity coordinate transformation that maps the pull-in singularity to infinity, avoiding the numerical failures that occur when conventional integration methods cross the collapse threshold. By differentiating the trained surrogate, they obtained design sensitivities of the pull-in voltage that match known closed-form results with very high accuracy, and demonstrated the method's utility for inverting device specifications to target operating parameters. For the dynamically initiated pull-in boundary starting from rest—which has no closed-form solution when damping is finite—the authors proved analytical bounds on this boundary, established that it is nondecreasing in the damping ratio, and showed that it merges with the quasi-static fold above a critical damping ratio, with the gap closing according to a specific power-law scaling. They also characterize how the collapse timescale transitions from logarithmic to inverse square-root growth at the merger point, and find that thermal corrections to the Casimir force at these length scales are negligible relative to even the classical-limit bound.

items.title: COVER: Identifiable Evaluation of Coalition Routing
items.summary: This paper addresses a methodological problem in evaluating multi-agent systems: when a system changes its team composition, it also changes its outputs, making it impossible to attribute performance differences to routing alone using end-to-end accuracy gaps. The authors introduce an evaluation framework called COVER that fixes a public information boundary, a downstream processing stack, and a finite set of legal team configurations before outcomes are generated, enabling identifiable measurement of routing effects. The framework distinguishes between pre-specified prospective controls and retrospective comparators, and requires that the union of distinct teams selected by competing policies be executed to support fair pairwise policy contrasts. Controlled experiments on multi-hop question answering benchmarks and a tool-use sandbox demonstrate that the framework can expose genuine selection headroom—cases where better routing improves performance—while also revealing when apparent routing wins are artifacts of retrospective analysis or confounded stacks. The authors emphasize that COVER is an auditable measurement methodology rather than a claim of universal routing superiority, and that raw answer accuracy can be uninformative about routing effects when stack interactions are present.

items.title: Multirate State Space Models for End-to-End Processing of Pulse Density Modulated Speech Signals
items.summary: The paper investigates processing pulse-density-modulated audio signals directly with deep neural networks based on state-space models, bypassing the conventional conversion to pulse-code-modulated audio that imposes computational overhead on resource-constrained edge devices. The authors identified two key properties of state-space models — their continuous-time parametrization and long-term memory — that make them well-suited for handling PDM signals across variable sampling rates without anti-aliasing. Building on these properties, they proposed a novel end-to-end architecture that encodes raw PDM input into a latent representation that is invariant to both modulation strategy and sampling rate. The architecture achieves competitive speech classification and enhancement performance compared to state-of-the-art methods operating on conventional PCM data at standard PDM sampling rates, while also performing robustly at low-power sampling rates. A particularly notable finding is that the state-space model's output can be downsampled by an extremely large factor, dramatically reducing the computational burden on subsequent processing layers.
items.citation: Ludovic Boulanger, Sean U. N. Wood. Multirate State Space Models for End-to-End Processing of Pulse Density Modulated Speech Signals. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Advancements in biosensor Technologies for Pathogen Detection: Innovations and comparison with conventional diagnostic approaches.
items.summary: This review examines biosensor technologies developed for the detection of pathogens across clinical, food safety, and environmental monitoring contexts, comparing them against established conventional diagnostic approaches. The authors surveyed the literature on electrochemical, optical, nanoparticle, microfluidic, and paper-based biosensor platforms, discussing their underlying sensing principles, design strategies, and respective advantages and limitations alongside methods such as culture-based assays, ELISA, and PCR. Conventional methods, while analytically well-validated, are constrained by lengthy processing times, complex instrumentation, and the requirement for trained personnel, limiting their suitability for rapid or on-site deployment. Biosensors were found to offer compelling advantages including portability, high sensitivity, multiplexing capability, and point-of-care applicability, with advances in nanomaterials, biorecognition strategies, and signal-transduction mechanisms further enhancing their detection potential. Nevertheless, the authors identify persistent challenges in sensor stability, reproducibility, fabrication scalability, and rigorous validation as key barriers that must be addressed before widespread practical implementation can be realized.
items.citation: Singhal P, Misra S, Prakash A et al.. Advancements in biosensor Technologies for Pathogen Detection: Innovations and comparison with conventional diagnostic approaches.. Journal of microbiological methods. 2026

items.title: Development of a NiCoFe-LDH/Ketjenblack-enhanced electrochemical antibacterial peptide biosensor for Aeromonas hydrophila detection in seawater samples.
items.summary: This paper describes the development of an electrochemical biosensor for the rapid detection of Aeromonas hydrophila, a bacterial pathogen significant in aquaculture settings. The biosensor was constructed by modifying a screen-printed carbon electrode with a nanocomposite of ternary nickel-cobalt-iron layered double hydroxide combined with Ketjenblack carbon, synthesized via a one-pot precipitation method, and functionalized with an antibacterial peptide as the biorecognition element. The nanocomposite material demonstrated a high-activity nanosheet architecture facilitating fast electron transfer, which was confirmed through multiple physicochemical and electrochemical characterization techniques. Under optimized conditions, the sensor achieved detection across a broad bacterial concentration range within thirty minutes at room temperature, with a very low limit of detection, high reproducibility, minimal cross-reactivity with other bacterial species, and strong performance when tested in spiked seawater samples. The authors claim this represents the first electrochemical antibacterial peptide-based biosensor for A. hydrophila validated in seawater, highlighting its potential utility for on-site aquaculture monitoring.
items.citation: Kızılkurtlu AA, Arancı K, Gülyüz S et al.. Development of a NiCoFe-LDH/Ketjenblack-enhanced electrochemical antibacterial peptide biosensor for Aeromonas hydrophila detection in seawater samples.. Mikrochimica acta. 2026

items.title: Self-Cleaning Electrochemical Biosensor Based on MCOF@Ag for Simultaneous Pathogen Detection and Photocatalytic Inactivation.
items.summary: This paper developed a dual-function electrochemical biosensor capable of both detecting and eliminating bacterial pathogens using a single electrode material. The researchers synthesized silver nanoparticle-decorated metal-covalent organic framework composites with a nanoflower-like structure, then functionalized the resulting electrode with aptamers specific to Staphylococcus aureus to enable selective bacterial capture and electrochemical quantification. The biosensor achieved highly sensitive detection of the target bacterium across a broad concentration range with a very low detection limit. Beyond detection, the material's photocatalytic activity under visible light allowed it to inactivate nearly all captured bacteria within minutes through reactive oxygen species generation, after which the electrode could be regeneratively cleaned and reused. The study demonstrates that a single metal-covalent organic framework-based electrode can integrate ultrasensitive pathogen detection with photocatalytic inactivation and self-cleaning regeneration, offering a promising platform for infectious disease monitoring and control.
items.citation: Bai Y, Xiao L, Cai L et al.. Self-Cleaning Electrochemical Biosensor Based on MCOF@Ag for Simultaneous Pathogen Detection and Photocatalytic Inactivation.. Analytical chemistry. 2026

items.title: Paper-Based Biosensor Using Dual-Recognition Molecules for Detection of <i>Staphylococcus aureus</i> in Milk.
items.summary: This paper developed a paper-based biosensor for the rapid detection of *Staphylococcus aureus* in milk, addressing the need for on-site food safety monitoring of a common dairy contaminant. The biosensor employed a dual-recognition strategy combining a milk matrix-adapted aptamer, selected through a SELEX process, with polyclonal antibodies that capture the pathogen via multiple epitopes on the paper substrate. Colloidal gold nanoparticles conjugated to the aptamer served as visual signal reporters, enabling instrument-free detection. The system achieved a low detection limit within a short timeframe, and the combination of aptamer and antibody recognition was shown to synergistically improve both sensitivity and specificity compared to single-recognition approaches. The authors propose this cost-effective platform as a practical solution for dairy safety monitoring in complex food matrices.
items.citation: Hou W, Li X, Li J et al.. Paper-Based Biosensor Using Dual-Recognition Molecules for Detection of <i>Staphylococcus aureus</i> in Milk.. Biosensors. 2026

items.title: A modular APEX biosensor enables sensitive and visualized monitoring of viral protease activity.
items.summary: The paper developed modular biosensors to detect viral protease activity within living cells, aiming to overcome limitations of conventional fluorescence and FRET-based screening methods that suffer from non-specific conformational interference and poor reflection of intracellular inhibitory effects. The researchers engineered two biosensors based on a split ascorbate peroxidase system, where protease-specific cleavage of a recognition sequence triggers reassembly of enzyme fragments, restores catalytic activity, and produces amplified fluorescent signals. Using the coronavirus main protease as a model, one sensor achieved an exceptionally high signal-to-noise ratio for enzyme activity detection, while the other accurately identified potent inhibitors and avoided false positives that plague traditional approaches. By simply swapping the protease recognition sequence, the platform was adapted to detect proteases from multiple viruses including SARS-CoV-2, MERS-CoV, enterovirus 71, Epstein-Barr virus, and hepatitis A virus. The authors conclude that this modular, intracellular screening platform provides a reliable and broadly applicable tool for evaluating antiviral drug candidates against diverse viral protease targets.
items.citation: Li B, Dong B, Chen Y et al.. A modular APEX biosensor enables sensitive and visualized monitoring of viral protease activity.. Virologica Sinica. 2026

items.title: Recent Progress in Nanoparticle-Based Biosensors for Monitoring <i>Shigella</i> spp. in Food Safety: A Critical Review.
items.summary: This review examined recent advances in nanoparticle-based biosensors for detecting *Shigella* species in food safety contexts, motivated by the pathogen's low infectious dose and the limitations of conventional culture-based and molecular diagnostic methods. The authors critically assessed biosensor designs across multiple signal transduction strategies—including optical approaches such as fluorescence, SERS, and LSPR, as well as electrochemical and lateral flow formats—evaluating how nanomaterials contribute to signal amplification and biorecognition. Detection was categorized by biological target, distinguishing between gene-level strategies using virulence markers such as *ipaH* for stable genus-level identification and whole-cell recognition approaches that enable faster detection with less sample preparation. Validation in real food matrices demonstrated acceptable recovery, minimal cross-reactivity, and agreement with reference methods across the biosensor types reviewed. The paper concludes by offering a design-oriented framework that integrates nanomaterial function, biosensor architecture, and performance characteristics to guide biosensor selection for food safety applications.
items.citation: Savas S, Gharibzahedi SMT. Recent Progress in Nanoparticle-Based Biosensors for Monitoring <i>Shigella</i> spp. in Food Safety: A Critical Review.. Biosensors. 2026

items.title: Oxidative Stress in Health and Disease: Mechanisms and Therapeutic Perspectives
items.summary: This review examines the dual role of reactive oxygen species in biological systems, where they act as essential signaling molecules at physiological concentrations but drive disease pathology when produced in excess. The authors synthesize current knowledge on the major types, cellular sources, and molecular mechanisms underlying both beneficial redox signaling and oxidative stress-mediated damage across a range of major disorders, including cancer, diabetes, cardiovascular disease, neurodegeneration, and inflammatory conditions. The review also critically evaluates contemporary and emerging methods for detecting and quantifying reactive oxygen species in clinical and preclinical settings, encompassing biochemical assays, fluorescent probes, biosensors, and advanced imaging approaches. On the basis of this integrated analysis, the authors argue for advancing precision redox medicine through targeted antioxidant-based diagnostic and therapeutic strategies informed by improved detection technologies and a deeper mechanistic understanding of redox-regulated processes.
items.citation: Shehwaz Anwar, Hajed Obaid A. Alharbi, Ali Yousif Babiker et al.. Oxidative Stress in Health and Disease: Mechanisms and Therapeutic Perspectives. International Journal of Molecular Sciences. 2026

items.title: The extracellular matrix in inflammation and cancer
items.summary: This review examines the role of the extracellular matrix in regulating immune cell behavior within inflammatory and tumor microenvironments. The authors systematically surveyed key ECM constituents—including fibrous proteins, glycosaminoglycans, proteoglycans, and glycoproteins—along with the molecular mediators, such as matrix metalloproteinases and inflammatory cytokines like TNF, interleukin, and TGF-β, that drive ECM remodeling in cancer. The review describes how dysregulated ECM components interact with immune cell receptors to suppress specific immune subsets, promote T cell exhaustion and macrophage polarization, and activate intracellular signaling pathways that cancer cells exploit to support progression and metastasis. The authors also explore how cytokine-driven ECM remodeling shapes a stromal environment conducive to tumor survival. Finally, the review highlights therapeutic strategies aimed at targeting ECM-mediated immunosuppression in solid tumors as a means of enhancing cancer immunotherapy efficacy.
items.citation: Wanting Zhang, Yuhang Xiang, Chen Lu et al.. The extracellular matrix in inflammation and cancer. Molecular Biomedicine. 2026

items.title: Interaction corrections to topological density three-point functions in two-dimensional Fermi liquids: a coadjoint orbit perspective
items.summary: This paper investigates how electron-electron interactions modify density three-point correlation functions in two-dimensional Fermi liquids, which are known to encode topological information about the Fermi sea in the noninteracting limit. The authors employ the coadjoint-orbit effective field theory framework, which reformulates fermionic loop calculations as tree-level diagrams in a bosonized language and allows systematic inclusion of generalized Landau interaction parameters. They find that even at linear order in the Landau interaction, a contribution proportional to the band curvature at the Fermi momentum arises, which alters the nonanalytic structure of the free density three-point function. This new nonanalytic structure is distinct from both the noninteracting case and the special case of a Galilean-invariant interacting system, demonstrating that interactions can in principle modify the topology-detecting character of the density three-point correlator. The results imply that the topological information encoded in these correlations is not interaction-independent for systems with general isotropic dispersions.
items.citation: Akshay Pal, Andrew Lucas, Umang Mehta. Interaction corrections to topological density three-point functions in two-dimensional Fermi liquids: a coadjoint orbit perspective. arXiv. 2026

items.title: How Long-Range Tails Reshape Non-Hermitian Spectra
items.summary: This paper investigates how exponentially decaying long-range hoppings—commonly truncated in tight-binding models—affect non-Hermitian systems under open boundary conditions. The authors demonstrate that even an infinitesimally small long-range hopping can nonperturbatively reconstruct both the spectrum and eigenstates of a short-range non-Hermitian system, a dramatic failure of the truncation approximation that has no counterpart in Hermitian physics. The underlying mechanism arises from a competition between the decay length of the long-range hoppings and the localization length of non-Hermitian skin modes, producing a sharp transition as the decay rate is varied. To describe the reconstructed spectra analytically, the authors introduce a squeezed generalized Brillouin zone framework in one dimension and a squeezed amoeba formulation in two or higher dimensions. They further show that long-range hoppings qualitatively reshape the Green's function in ways that are experimentally detectable, highlighting the physical importance of these otherwise seemingly negligible tails.
items.citation: Ding Gu, Zhanpeng Fu, Yu-Min Hu et al.. How Long-Range Tails Reshape Non-Hermitian Spectra. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Advancing Interaction-Sensitive Feature Selection: Novel Relief-Based Algorithms, Expanded Comparisons, and Recommendations for Biomedical Data Mining
items.summary: This paper examined Relief-based algorithms (RBAs), a class of filter-based feature selection methods capable of detecting feature interactions, in the context of high-dimensional biomedical data analysis. The researchers refactored and optimized the scikit-rebate Python package, introducing several existing and newly proposed RBA variants implementing alternative strategies for neighbor selection and feature scoring, then benchmarked all algorithms across diverse simulated genomic datasets varying in sample size, feature count, heritability, and association type. The refactoring alone yielded dramatic reductions in algorithm runtimes, making the methods substantially more practical. Most RBAs effectively detected two-way interactions in noisy data, with algorithms employing "far" scoring excelling at interaction detection though at the cost of sensitivity to main effects, while several algorithms including the newly introduced MultiSWRFDB showed strong performance across both main effects and multi-way epistatic interactions. The study concludes that the newly introduced RBA variants robustly preserve both main effect and epistatic predictive signals, making them well-suited as preprocessing steps for downstream biomedical modeling.
items.citation: Kia Kazemi-Nia, Harsh Bandhey, Philip J. Freda et al.. Advancing Interaction-Sensitive Feature Selection: Novel Relief-Based Algorithms, Expanded Comparisons, and Recommendations for Biomedical Data Mining. arXiv. 2026

items.title: ExoMOD II. A Statistical Model of Transit Timing Variations in Kepler Multi-Planet Systems
items.summary: This paper uses a forward-modeling population framework called ExoMOD, calibrated on Kepler data, to statistically predict Transit Timing Variations (TTVs) in close-in multi-planet systems and compare those predictions against observed TTV signals. The study finds that gravitational interactions between planets are insufficient to explain the observed short-period TTV signals, implying those signals must arise from other, unidentified sources. For long-period TTVs, which are more plausibly caused by planet-planet interactions, the analysis reveals that single transiting planets have TTV-inducing companions nearly as frequently as systems with two transiting planets, ruling out orbital architectures that favor a large population of intrinsically single planets. Systems with higher observed multiplicities show elevated rates of long-period TTVs and low orbital gap complexities, suggesting they preserved a dynamical memory of their formation. The work is presented as a step toward building a more rigorous connection between observational statistics and theories of planetary system formation.
items.citation: David Nesvorny, Daniel A. Yahalomi, David Kipping et al.. ExoMOD II. A Statistical Model of Transit Timing Variations in Kepler Multi-Planet Systems. arXiv. 2026

items.title: ExoMOD I. A Forward Model for the Orbital Architecture of Kepler Multi-Planet Systems
items.summary: This paper develops a forward model to interpret transit observations from the Kepler telescope and characterize the true orbital architecture of close-in multi-planet systems, accounting for the geometric bias that only planets with near edge-on orbits are detectable. The authors parameterize planetary system properties including distributions of planet radii, masses, orbital periods, and orbital excitation via the Angular Momentum Deficit, then fit the model to Kepler's planet catalog using a Bayesian inference framework. Key findings include that single- and multi-planet systems show statistically distinct period distributions, and that high-multiplicity systems appear to retain memory of their formation through correlated period ratios. The study estimates that a typical FGK dwarf hosts roughly two or more planets within the studied radius and period ranges, and concludes that for any detected planetary system, there is approximately an even chance that at least one inner or intermediate-period planet was missed by Kepler. The gap complexity metric proves useful for constraining both the period ratio structure and the orbital excitation distribution of these systems.
items.citation: David Nesvorny, Daniel A. Yahalomi, David Kipping et al.. ExoMOD I. A Forward Model for the Orbital Architecture of Kepler Multi-Planet Systems. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Analysis of Polynomial Threshold Functions on Random Regular Graphs: Computational Complexity of Detecting Noisy Random Lift
items.summary: The paper studies the computational problem of distinguishing a noisy random lift of a base regular graph from a uniformly random regular graph, a natural hypothesis testing task in the theory of random graphs. To analyze this problem, the authors develop the first treatment of low-degree polynomial threshold functions in this setting, a framework commonly used to establish computational hardness or limitations of efficient algorithms. Along the way, they derive new results on the distribution of short cycle counts in noisy random lifts up to logarithmic lengths, which generalize previously known results for random regular graphs and random lifts separately into a unified framework. Their findings collectively characterize the power and limitations of low-degree polynomial methods for detecting structured randomness in this graph model.
items.citation: Xifan Yu. Analysis of Polynomial Threshold Functions on Random Regular Graphs: Computational Complexity of Detecting Noisy Random Lift. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Twenty-Two Months of Syndromic Multiplex-PCR Testing for Acute Infections in a Southern Italian Hospital: Pathogen Epidemiology, Diagnostic Appropriateness and the Cost of Negative Results.
items.summary: This study examined the real-world use and diagnostic yield of syndromic multiplex-PCR panels across four clinical syndromes — meningitis/encephalitis, upper and lower respiratory infections, and gastrointestinal infections — at a southern Italian hospital over nearly two years. Researchers retrospectively analysed thousands of panel determinations, removing duplicate tests from the same patient to ensure each represented a distinct diagnostic episode, and evaluated pathogen distribution, result positivity rates, and the financial implications of negative findings. A striking majority of all determinations returned entirely negative results, with the meningitis/encephalitis and gastrointestinal panels showing the highest negativity rates, indicating substantial over-utilisation in those clinical streams. Key microbiological findings included viral dominance in central nervous system infections, rhinovirus/enterovirus prevalence in respiratory specimens, clustering of antimicrobial resistance markers in Enterobacterales co-infections on the pneumonia panel, and a predominance of diarrhoeagenic Escherichia coli pathotypes in gastrointestinal samples. The authors conclude that panel use should be restricted through clinical gating criteria, tiered testing algorithms, and mandatory reflex sequencing of unsubtypeable influenza A specimens to close surveillance gaps for novel or zoonotic strains.
items.citation: Chirizzi D, Spedicato A, Bianco G et al.. Twenty-Two Months of Syndromic Multiplex-PCR Testing for Acute Infections in a Southern Italian Hospital: Pathogen Epidemiology, Diagnostic Appropriateness and the Cost of Negative Results.. Microorganisms. 2026

items.title: 320 Diagnostic stewardship of a multiplex pneumonia PCR panel leads to cost savings and more appropriate patient care
items.citation: Ronne R, Kracker A, Salgado C. 320 Diagnostic stewardship of a multiplex pneumonia PCR panel leads to cost savings and more appropriate patient care. Antimicrobial stewardship & healthcare epidemiology : ASHE. 2026

items.title: Season-matched comparison of pediatric respiratory pathogen detection patterns before and after the lifting of COVID-19 restrictions in Guangzhou.
items.summary: This study examined how the lifting of COVID-19 non-pharmaceutical interventions affected the detection patterns of pediatric respiratory pathogens in subtropical southern China. Researchers retrospectively analyzed nasopharyngeal swab specimens from children under sixteen presenting with fever or respiratory symptoms at a Guangzhou pediatric medical center, using a consistent twelve-pathogen multiplex PCR panel across both a pre-lifting and a post-lifting period, with a season-matched comparison focused on the same months across two consecutive years to minimize seasonal bias. Following the lifting of restrictions, detection rates of Influenza A, RSV, and human rhinovirus increased substantially compared to the matched prior-year period, while Influenza B and human metapneumovirus declined markedly. The post-lifting cohort also contained a higher proportion of infants and showed greater rates of fever, wheezing, and lower respiratory tract diagnoses, though the authors note these clinical differences may partly reflect changes in healthcare-seeking behavior and admission thresholds rather than true shifts in disease burden. The findings highlight the value of continued multiplex surveillance and age-targeted prevention efforts, while cautioning against direct causal attribution of pathogen shifts to restriction lifting alone given residual confounding by seasonality, SARS-CoV-2 circulation, and behavioral factors.
items.citation: Hua L, Liang W, Li W et al.. Season-matched comparison of pediatric respiratory pathogen detection patterns before and after the lifting of COVID-19 restrictions in Guangzhou.. Frontiers in pediatrics. 2026

items.title: Scenario-Driven Rapid Testing for Top Pathogens in Pediatric Respiratory Infections: Clinical and Economic Value from Emergency Triage to Precision Anti-Infective Management in the PICU.
items.summary: This narrative review examined how rapid diagnostic testing for respiratory pathogens in children can be optimized to improve both clinical and economic outcomes across different care settings. The authors identified a core problem: although a wide range of rapid tests now exist—from antigen assays to metagenomic sequencing—evidence from pediatric emergency trials shows that broad pathogen detection alone does not reliably reduce antibiotic use or healthcare costs. In response, they developed a scenario-driven framework in which "top pathogens" are defined contextually by age group, clinical syndrome, season, and care setting based on criteria such as prevalence, treatment implications, transmissibility, and antimicrobial resistance relevance. The review applies this framework across distinct clinical scenarios, from emergency triage and inpatient ward care to severe pneumonia, intensive care, and outbreak management, and analyzes the economic mechanisms through which appropriately targeted testing can generate value, including reduced unnecessary antimicrobials, timely antiviral initiation, optimized isolation, and shorter hospital stays. The authors conclude that embedding rapid diagnostics within predefined decision pathways guided by diagnostic and antimicrobial stewardship principles, rather than applying broad syndromic panels indiscriminately, offers a practical path toward precision infectious disease management in children.
items.citation: Chen J, Wang H, Li Y et al.. Scenario-Driven Rapid Testing for Top Pathogens in Pediatric Respiratory Infections: Clinical and Economic Value from Emergency Triage to Precision Anti-Infective Management in the PICU.. Pathogens (Basel, Switzerland). 2026

items.title: Distribution Patterns of Non-SARS-CoV-2 Respiratory Pathogens Among Patients With Influenza-Like Illness During the COVID-19 Pandemic: A Cross-Sectional Study From Bangladesh.
items.summary: This cross-sectional study investigated the respiratory pathogens responsible for influenza-like illness in patients who tested negative for SARS-CoV-2 during the COVID-19 pandemic at a tertiary care hospital in Bangladesh. Adults presenting with influenza-like symptoms between July and December 2022 were enrolled and their nasopharyngeal swabs were analyzed using multiplex real-time PCR to detect a broad range of viral and bacterial pathogens. Over a third of participants tested positive for at least one non-SARS-CoV-2 pathogen, with human rhinovirus emerging as the most prevalent viral agent and *Streptococcus pneumoniae* as the dominant bacterial pathogen. Co-infections were present in a minority of patients, with rhinovirus–influenza B and *S. pneumoniae*–*Haemophilus influenzae* pairings showing the strongest, though statistically non-significant after correction, co-detection trends. The authors conclude that broad-spectrum multiplex PCR testing should be incorporated into the clinical evaluation of SARS-CoV-2-negative patients with persistent respiratory symptoms to capture the full etiological burden of respiratory illness.
items.citation: Sultana S, Taher A, Haque N et al.. Distribution Patterns of Non-SARS-CoV-2 Respiratory Pathogens Among Patients With Influenza-Like Illness During the COVID-19 Pandemic: A Cross-Sectional Study From Bangladesh.. Cureus. 2026

items.title: Etiology of severe acute respiratory infections among adults in northern Thailand using multiplex PCR: A post-COVID-19 surveillance study (2023-2024).
items.summary: This study investigated the causes of severe acute respiratory infections among hospitalized adults in northern Thailand during the post-COVID-19 pandemic period. Researchers retrospectively analyzed respiratory samples from adult patients admitted to a regional hospital in Chiang Mai with SARI symptoms, testing specimens using multiplex real-time PCR capable of detecting a broad range of respiratory pathogens. Nearly half of patients tested positive for at least one respiratory pathogen, with adenovirus and rhinovirus emerging as the most commonly identified viruses, and co-infections present in a notable proportion of cases. Seasonal patterns were observed, with influenza A and rhinovirus peaking in January while adenovirus and enterovirus circulated throughout the study period. The findings underscore the importance of continued pathogen-specific surveillance and broader rapid molecular diagnostics in the post-pandemic era, particularly given the high rate of empiric antibiotic use observed among patients whose infections may not have had a bacterial cause.
items.citation: Kham-Kjing N, Kawila R, Tariyo P et al.. Etiology of severe acute respiratory infections among adults in northern Thailand using multiplex PCR: A post-COVID-19 surveillance study (2023-2024).. PloS one. 2026

items.title: Enterococcus Species: Multifaceted Probiotic Potential and Safety Considerations
items.summary: The paper examines the genus *Enterococcus*, commensal bacteria found in the gastrointestinal tracts of humans and animals as well as in food and environmental sources, focusing on their dual role as potentially beneficial microorganisms and sources of safety concern. The authors reviewed how select enterococcal strains are employed as probiotics, antibiotic alternatives, and protective cultures, where they help control pathogens, modulate the microbiome, support food fermentation, and produce bioactive compounds such as bacteriocins with pathogen-inhibitory activity. At the same time, the review highlights that certain species are associated with healthcare-acquired infections and the dissemination of antimicrobial resistance genes, complicating their application. The authors argue that rigorous safety evaluations are essential before enterococci can be broadly adopted in clinical or agrifood contexts. The paper is presented as a comprehensive reference intended to guide future research, regulatory frameworks, and practical applications in both healthcare and food systems.
items.citation: Ojonugwa Precious John, Kayode Olayinka Afolabi, Anayochukwu Chibuike Ngene et al.. Enterococcus Species: Multifaceted Probiotic Potential and Safety Considerations. Microorganisms. 2026

items.title: Genomic analysis of high pathogenicity avian influenza viruses from Antarctica reveals multiple introductions from South America
items.summary: This study investigated the introduction and spread of highly pathogenic avian influenza virus H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b into Antarctica, where it poses a significant threat to polar wildlife. Researchers detected the virus in carcasses of eight species across the South Shetland Islands during two consecutive austral summers, then applied whole-genome sequencing, mutational profiling, and phylogenetic reconstruction to characterize the viral strains. The analyses revealed that the detected viruses descended from multiple distinct introduction events rather than a single source, with one group of strains clustering with H5N1 previously found in marine mammals in South America and another group clustering with strains from South Georgia and the Antarctic Peninsula. These findings demonstrate extensive epidemiological connectivity between South America and Antarctica, with South Georgia appearing to function as an intermediary stepping stone facilitating viral spread into the Antarctic region.
items.citation: Maria Ogrzewalska, Ralph Eric Thijl Vanstreels, Elisa Cavalcante Pereira et al.. Genomic analysis of high pathogenicity avian influenza viruses from Antarctica reveals multiple introductions from South America. Nature Communications. 2026

items.title: Serologic Evidence of Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza A(H5N1) Virus Infection in a Veterinary Professional Exposed to an Infected Domestic Cat — Los Angeles County, California, December 2024–January 2025
items.summary: This report investigated potential human exposure to highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) virus following an outbreak among domestic cats in Los Angeles County linked to consumption of raw animal products. Health authorities monitored all persons exposed to the infected cats and later conducted a serological survey to detect infections that may have been missed by standard diagnostic testing, including among those without symptoms. Although none of the exposed individuals tested positive by PCR, antibody testing revealed serological evidence of H5N1 infection in one asymptomatic veterinary professional who had not used respiratory or eye protection during animal contact and had no other known risk factors. These findings represent evidence of possible cat-to-human transmission of H5N1 virus, a route of spillover that warrants heightened concern. The report emphasizes the importance of consistent use of appropriate personal protective equipment in veterinary settings where exposure to infected animals may occur.
items.venue: MMWR Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report
items.citation: Aisling Vaughan, Allison Joyce, Elizabeth Traub et al.. Serologic Evidence of Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza A(H5N1) Virus Infection in a Veterinary Professional Exposed to an Infected Domestic Cat — Los Angeles County, California, December 2024–January 2025. MMWR Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report. 2026

items.title: Evolution of a truncated nucleocapsid protein enhances SARS-CoV-2 fitness by suppressing antiviral responses
items.citation: Rory P. Mulloy, Danyel Evseev, Noga Sharlin et al.. Evolution of a truncated nucleocapsid protein enhances SARS-CoV-2 fitness by suppressing antiviral responses. PLoS Biology. 2026

items.title: Metagenomic and Targeted Next-Generation Sequencing in Infectious Disease Diagnostics: Current Applications, Challenges, and Future Perspectives
items.summary: This review examines how metagenomic and targeted next-generation sequencing technologies are reshaping the diagnosis and management of infectious diseases in clinical settings. The authors surveyed current applications of both approaches across clinical microbiology, focusing on pathogen detection, antimicrobial resistance profiling, virulence characterization, and outbreak investigation in conditions such as pneumonia, critical illness, and pediatric respiratory infections. The review evaluates the diagnostic performance, strengths, and limitations of these sequencing methods, including obstacles related to sensitivity, specificity, standardization, bioinformatic complexity, and cost. The authors also explore how integrating sequencing-based surveillance with public health tools such as wastewater epidemiology could enable population-level monitoring of healthcare-associated infections and antimicrobial resistance. Finally, the review outlines the steps required to move these genomic approaches from research environments into routine clinical and public health practice.
items.citation: Rong Rong, Yuni Long, Yujing Li et al.. Metagenomic and Targeted Next-Generation Sequencing in Infectious Disease Diagnostics: Current Applications, Challenges, and Future Perspectives. Diagnostics. 2026

items.title: Expert Consensus on the Prevention of Secondary Mucormycosis Following Respiratory Viral Infections
items.summary: This paper addresses the clinical challenge of secondary mucormycosis arising after respiratory viral infections, particularly those caused by SARS-CoV-2 and influenza viruses. A multidisciplinary group of experts was convened to develop a formal consensus document aimed at systematically guiding prevention efforts. The consensus identifies high-risk patient populations and puts forward preventive recommendations organized across four domains: education and training, personal protection, early diagnosis and treatment, and infection control. The document also acknowledges areas where evidence remains insufficient or contested, and it proposes directions for future research to strengthen the evidence base. Overall, the consensus seeks to optimize prevention strategies and raise awareness of mucormycosis as a serious complication following respiratory viral disease.
items.citation: Junyan Qu, Xinyao Liu, Min Quan et al.. Expert Consensus on the Prevention of Secondary Mucormycosis Following Respiratory Viral Infections. iFungi. 2026

items.title: Understanding Venture Capital Syndication in Information Technology Sectors: A Network Formation Perspective
items.summary: This paper investigates how venture capital co-investment networks form and evolve within U.S. information technology sectors by examining the relational mechanisms that drive syndication decisions. Using a comprehensive dyadic dataset spanning nearly six decades across hardware, software, and hybrid subsectors, the researchers tested seven theoretical mechanisms—including prior collaboration, shared partners, geographic proximity, and organizational similarity—through logistic regression models applied to all possible investor pairs. They also estimated an exponential random graph model of the contemporary software investment network among a large set of active investors. The findings consistently show that prior collaboration is the strongest predictor of new co-investment ties, while network closure, geographic homophily, and organizational-type similarity also positively structure link formation, with other factors such as domain overlap and prominence varying by subsector. Together, the results demonstrate that IT venture syndication networks are jointly shaped by relational persistence, social closure, and homophilous preferences rather than any single mechanism.
items.citation: Liheng Tan, Zhengkai Tu, Prasanna Karhade. Understanding Venture Capital Syndication in Information Technology Sectors: A Network Formation Perspective. arXiv. 2026

items.title: PanelShield: Verifiable Closed-Loop Safe Planning for Robotic Industrial Panel Operation
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of safe, manual-guided robotic operation of industrial control panels, which requires not only recognizing controls and generating actions but also strictly adhering to constraints specified in operation manuals and safety regulations. The authors developed PanelShield, a closed-loop planning framework that generates parameterized action sequences grounded in task-relevant manual evidence and enforces safety through dual formal verification using Linear Temporal Logic and a Safety Finite State Machine, catching both cross-step temporal violations and local transition illegality. When a violation is detected, the system produces a structured counterexample identifying the earliest offending step and its cause, enabling targeted repair and re-verification rather than wholesale replanning. The framework was evaluated on a custom multi-level long-horizon benchmark spanning three representative industrial panel types, as well as in real-world robotic experiments, where it substantially outperformed foundation-model-only baselines on safety-constrained tasks while achieving a very low violation rate and modest end-to-end latency. The results demonstrate that formal verification can be practically integrated with foundation-model-based planners to achieve flexible yet auditable and safety-assured robotic manipulation in industrial settings.
items.citation: Guipeng Xin, Jiahe Xu, Chenhui Wan et al.. PanelShield: Verifiable Closed-Loop Safe Planning for Robotic Industrial Panel Operation. arXiv. 2026

items.title: MaCoPlanner: LLM-Assisted Manual-Compiled Task Planning with Proactive Safety Verification for Robotic Industrial Panel Operation
items.summary: MaCoPlanner is a task-planning framework designed to enable robots to operate industrial control panels by reasoning over heterogeneous equipment manuals containing operating procedures, safety rules, and device-state constraints. The system converts these manuals into a typed intermediate representation, retrieves relevant evidence for plan generation, and symbolically simulates candidate plans before execution to check for procedural and state-transition violations, with detected errors returned for targeted repair and unresolvable plans rejected outright. A separate execution interface then grounds verified symbolic actions to physical controls and tracks device state. Evaluation using an independent oracle showed a low final violation rate, with meaningful improvements in task success on both moderately and highly complex tasks compared to a baseline that uses raw manuals directly. Additional experiments on a controller-panel simulator confirmed execution feasibility under representative conditions, though the authors explicitly note the system is not claimed to be ready for industrial deployment.
items.citation: Guipeng Xin, Jiahe Xua, Mohammad Deghat et al.. MaCoPlanner: LLM-Assisted Manual-Compiled Task Planning with Proactive Safety Verification for Robotic Industrial Panel Operation. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Spectral Features Dominate BCG Respiratory-Event Detection: A Large-Scale Patient-Independent Comparison of Feature Groups in Sleep Apnea Patients
items.summary: This study investigated which signal features extracted from ballistocardiographic recordings are most useful for detecting respiratory events associated with sleep apnea, a question previously unresolved in the literature. Researchers recorded data from a large capacitive pressure mat simultaneously with standard respiratory polygraphy in a substantial cohort of patients undergoing in-hospital sleep apnea evaluation, extracting a broad set of features spanning statistical, time-domain, frequency-domain, wavelet, frame-energy, and nonlinear complexity descriptors across multiple spatial channels. Using strict leave-one-patient-out cross-validation to ensure patient-independent generalization, machine learning classifiers achieved very high discriminative performance for distinguishing respiratory-event windows from event-free windows. Feature importance analysis revealed that frequency-domain features, particularly breathing-band spectral power and spectral shape descriptors, dominated discrimination, while time-domain features such as curve-length and area-under-the-curve measures provided the main complementary contribution, and wavelet or nonlinear features played only secondary roles. The findings establish an empirical basis for prioritizing a compact, interpretable subset of features in future unobtrusive BCG-based sleep apnea monitoring systems.
items.citation: Israel Campero Jurado, Zoe Bousraou, Lara Benning et al.. Spectral Features Dominate BCG Respiratory-Event Detection: A Large-Scale Patient-Independent Comparison of Feature Groups in Sleep Apnea Patients. arXiv. 2026

items.title: CP-Aware OFDM-Based OOK Signaling
items.summary: The paper addresses a fundamental incompatibility between cyclic prefix structures and on-off keying signal generation in OFDM-based low-power IoT systems. The researchers proposed a CP-aware waveform design that extends OOK signal generation across the entire CP-OFDM symbol duration, which risks breaking subcarrier orthogonality when the cyclic prefix length is mismatched at the receiver. To manage this, the design requires independent OOK generation with modifications to the existing signal generation block, and introduces a block-wise time shift strategy to reduce CP mismatch effects. Analytical and simulation results indicate that interference imposed on legacy OFDM subcarriers remains controlled under this scheme, while OOK detection performance improves substantially, though practical deployment trade-offs must be weighed.
items.citation: Badr Eddine Ouakouak, Salah Eddine Zegrar, Hüseyin Arslan. CP-Aware OFDM-Based OOK Signaling. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Under-Mattress Temporal Sensing for Next-Day Agitation Risk Scoring in Dementia Wards
items.summary: This paper investigated whether contactless under-mattress physiological signals recorded during the night could predict the risk of agitation in dementia patients on the following day, and whether retaining fine-grained temporal structure improves prediction compared to simple nightly summaries. Using data from a specialized hospital dementia unit, the researchers benchmarked four analytical approaches ranging from conventional handcrafted nightly summary features to full-night sequence modeling and sliding-window multiple-instance learning, evaluated with patient-grouped cross-validation. Full-night sequence modeling achieved the best discrimination performance, and both minute-level temporal pipelines outperformed nightly summaries, though differences relative to three-period handcrafted features were uncertain. Attribution analyses across temporal models consistently highlighted activity, heart rate, and respiratory rate during the core overnight period as the most informative signals. The authors conclude that overnight contactless sensing offers modest but promising next-day agitation risk discrimination, while noting that calibration limitations and the need for external validation preclude immediate use in individual clinical decisions.
items.citation: Zhen Liu, Marta Bono, Robbe Decloedt et al.. Under-Mattress Temporal Sensing for Next-Day Agitation Risk Scoring in Dementia Wards. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Recent advances in lateral flow immunoassay for virus detection: current achievements, challenges and future prospects.
items.summary: This review examines lateral flow immunoassay (LFIA) technology and its role in detecting viral pathogens, reconceptualizing it not merely as a point-of-care tool but as a point-of-need self-testing platform capable of supporting large-scale epidemic surveillance and pandemic preparedness. The authors systematically survey recent advances across three domains: signal generation and transduction strategies employing diverse nanomaterials such as colorimetric, fluorescent, magnetic, surface-enhanced Raman scattering, and photothermal systems; multimodal and multiplex detection approaches aimed at improving sensitivity and throughput; and the integration of machine learning for signal interpretation and system optimization. The review also comprehensively covers LFIA applications in detecting viral antigens, antibodies, and nucleic acids. Current limitations—including sensitivity constraints, target specificity issues, and practical challenges related to cost, usability, and stability—are critically assessed, with future directions proposed around advanced nanomaterials, intelligent data processing, and multi-target detection. Overall, the authors argue that LFIA, particularly colorimetric formats, holds transformative potential as an emergency screening tool and for strengthening decentralized diagnostic capacity in global public health systems.
items.citation: Li L, Liu F, He X et al.. Recent advances in lateral flow immunoassay for virus detection: current achievements, challenges and future prospects.. Talanta. 2026

items.title: Polydopamine nanoparticle-based colorimetric-photothermal dual-mode lateral flow immunoassay for thromboembolism diagnosis.
items.summary: This paper investigated whether polydopamine nanoparticles could serve as superior signal labels in lateral flow immunoassays compared to conventional gold nanoparticles, which are constrained by single-mode colorimetric detection and limited sensitivity. The researchers constructed a dual-mode colorimetric and photothermal lateral flow immunoassay platform exploiting the high molar extinction coefficient and broadband ultraviolet-to-near-infrared absorption of polydopamine nanoparticles, targeting two thromboembolism-related biomarkers, thrombomodulin and α2-plasmin inhibitor-plasmin complex, in clinical serum samples. The photothermal readout mode substantially amplified detection sensitivity beyond what colorimetric reading alone could achieve, and clinical validation using serum samples showed strong agreement with established clinical methods. The authors conclude that polydopamine nanoparticle-based dual-mode lateral flow immunoassay represents a feasible and sensitive strategy for point-of-care thromboembolism diagnosis.
items.citation: Yin J, Qiu Y, Nie Y et al.. Polydopamine nanoparticle-based colorimetric-photothermal dual-mode lateral flow immunoassay for thromboembolism diagnosis.. RSC advances. 2026

items.title: A lateral flow microarray immunoassay to detect USUV NS1-specific antibodies in tissues of deceased blackbirds in the Netherlands.
items.summary: This study investigated whether a lateral flow microarray immunoassay (LMIA) could be used to detect Usutu virus (USUV)-specific antibodies in tissues collected from deceased Eurasian blackbirds, addressing a gap in current surveillance systems that typically rely on serum from live birds. The researchers tested the LMIA against blood clots and extracts from lung and liver tissues taken from blackbird carcasses found in the Netherlands. Detection of USUV non-structural protein 1 (NS1)-specific antibodies was more likely in lung tissue extracts from RT-PCR-confirmed USUV-positive birds, and the assay showed minimal cross-reactivity with the related West Nile virus NS1 antigen. The findings demonstrate that the LMIA can specifically detect USUV NS1 antibodies in deceased bird specimens, opening the possibility of extending serological surveillance to carcasses found in the field. The authors suggest this approach could enable rapid, on-site analysis of both live and deceased blackbirds, improving monitoring of USUV circulation.
items.citation: Godarzi B, Holicki CM, Chandler FD et al.. A lateral flow microarray immunoassay to detect USUV NS1-specific antibodies in tissues of deceased blackbirds in the Netherlands.. Virus research. 2026

items.title: Boronate-mediated antibody orientation: a molecular simulation-guided strategy for ultra-sensitive lateral flow immunoassays.
items.summary: This study addressed the problem of random antibody orientation on lateral flow immunoassay strips, which limits detection sensitivity and reproducibility. The researchers developed a boronate affinity-based strategy that exploits covalent reactions between boronic acid and cis-diol groups on antibody Fc-region glycans to achieve site-specific, oriented immobilization, using molecular dynamics simulations to characterize the binding mechanism and energetics. Simulations revealed that the boronate-antibody configuration achieved the most favorable binding energy and rapid conformational stabilization through a sequential process of electrostatic guidance followed by hydrogen-bond and covalent bond formation. When applied experimentally, the oriented immobilization yielded near-complete antibody conjugation efficiency, greater antigen-binding fragment exposure, and substantially improved affinity compared to conventional passive adsorption. The resulting lateral flow assay for detecting zearalenone in corn achieved a dramatically lower detection limit than traditional colloidal gold assays, with strong agreement to liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry reference measurements, demonstrating a broadly applicable, chemistry-driven framework for next-generation rapid diagnostics.
items.citation: Yang Z, Yan X, Yang Z et al.. Boronate-mediated antibody orientation: a molecular simulation-guided strategy for ultra-sensitive lateral flow immunoassays.. Mikrochimica acta. 2026

items.title: On-site serological screening of Usutu virus in wild birds: Field evaluation of a lateral flow microarray immunoassay using the WHO REASSURED framework.
items.summary: This study evaluated a novel field-deployable serological assay for detecting Usutu virus (USUV) and West Nile virus (WNV) antibodies in wild birds at capture sites in the Netherlands, where both arboviruses pose increasing public health and ecological concern. The researchers used a species-independent Lateral Flow Microarray ImmunoAssay (LMIA) targeting non-structural protein 1 antibodies for both viruses, testing blood samples from wild birds captured at bird-ringing sites and comparing results against the gold-standard Focus Reduction Neutralization Test. The LMIA demonstrated high sensitivity and strong specificity for USUV detection relative to the gold-standard method, and successfully identified seroconversion in a Eurasian blackbird, which was independently confirmed. Performance of the assay was also evaluated using the WHO REASSURED framework, scoring well against criteria designed to assess diagnostics for point-of-care use in resource-limited settings. The authors conclude that the LMIA is a feasible, rapid, multi-analyte, and equipment-light tool for on-site arbovirus surveillance in wild birds, though broader validation is still recommended before widespread deployment.
items.citation: Godarzi B, Holicki CM, Chandler FD et al.. On-site serological screening of Usutu virus in wild birds: Field evaluation of a lateral flow microarray immunoassay using the WHO REASSURED framework.. Journal of virological methods. 2026

items.title: Large-scale synthesis of phenylboronic acid-functionalized gold nanoparticles enables an oriented antibody interface for sensitive point-of-care diagnostics.
items.summary: This paper investigated how antibody orientation on gold nanoparticles affects the sensitivity of lateral flow immunoassays and sought to overcome the limitations of conventional citrate-capped nanoparticles, which rely on random antibody adsorption that can obscure antigen-binding sites. The researchers developed a one-pot, room-temperature synthesis method for phenylboronic acid-functionalized gold nanoparticles that could be produced at large scale in a single batch within minutes, without the high-temperature reflux conditions typically required. These nanoparticles enabled oriented antibody immobilization by exploiting boronate-affinity interactions with carbohydrate moieties on antibody Fc fragments, thereby directing antigen-binding sites away from the nanoparticle surface. When tested in a lateral flow assay for fecal occult blood detection, the phenylboronic acid-functionalized nanoparticles achieved dramatically improved sensitivity compared to conventional citrate-capped nanoparticle probes, demonstrating strong potential for clinical point-of-care diagnostic applications.
items.citation: Xu J, Li Q, Lu B et al.. Large-scale synthesis of phenylboronic acid-functionalized gold nanoparticles enables an oriented antibody interface for sensitive point-of-care diagnostics.. Colloids and surfaces. B, Biointerfaces. 2026

items.title: Biosensing technologies for foodborne pathogen detection and healthcare: principles, emerging materials, and intelligent platforms
items.summary: This review examines the current state and future direction of biosensing technologies designed to detect priority foodborne pathogens, including *Escherichia coli*, *Salmonella*, and *Listeria monocytogenes*, which continue to threaten global public health. The authors survey electrochemical, optical, and microfluidic sensing platforms, evaluating how advances in functional nanomaterials, aptamers, nanozymes, and surface engineering have improved sensor sensitivity, specificity, and performance in complex food matrices. A central theme is the integration of artificial intelligence and machine learning into these platforms, enabling real-time analytics, intelligent pattern recognition, and high-throughput multiplexing that transform conventional detection systems into smart diagnostic devices. The review critically assesses practical challenges such as matrix interference, bioreceptor instability, scalability limitations, and the absence of regulatory standardization, while proposing mitigation strategies including ratiometric sensing, microfluidic pre-treatment, explainable AI, and printable electronics. Looking ahead, the authors advocate for self-powered biosensors, modular pathogen panel hubs, blockchain integration, and standardized validation pipelines as pathways toward robust, regulation-ready platforms for next-generation food safety monitoring.
items.citation: Purshottam J. Assudani, Balakrishnan . P., Anny Leema A et al.. Biosensing technologies for foodborne pathogen detection and healthcare: principles, emerging materials, and intelligent platforms. Microchimica Acta. 2026

items.title: Oxidative Stress in Health and Disease: Mechanisms and Therapeutic Perspectives
items.summary: This review examines the dual role of reactive oxygen species in biological systems, where they act as essential signaling molecules at physiological concentrations but drive disease when produced in excess or dysregulated. The paper synthesizes current knowledge on the major types, sources, and physiological functions of reactive oxygen species, as well as the molecular pathways through which oxidative stress causes cellular damage and signaling dysregulation. Methods for detecting and quantifying oxidative stress in clinical and preclinical settings are critically evaluated, including biochemical assays, fluorescent probes, biosensors, and advanced imaging approaches. The review also surveys how oxidative stress contributes to the pathophysiology of cancer, diabetes, cardiovascular disease, neurodegenerative conditions, and inflammatory disorders. The authors conclude by outlining future directions in precision redox medicine, emphasizing targeted antioxidant-based diagnostic and therapeutic strategies informed by improved detection technologies and deeper mechanistic understanding of redox biology.
items.citation: Shehwaz Anwar, Hajed Obaid A. Alharbi, Ali Yousif Babiker et al.. Oxidative Stress in Health and Disease: Mechanisms and Therapeutic Perspectives. International Journal of Molecular Sciences. 2026

items.title: Rethinking Extracellular Vesicle Signaling
items.summary: This paper examines how extracellular vesicles communicate between cells, challenging the prevailing view that their signaling primarily depends on cellular uptake and release of internal cargo into recipient cells. The authors propose two alternative signaling modes based on surface binding alone: a "bind-and-stay" mechanism, in which vesicles remain attached to a cell and signal from the surface, and a "bind-and-leave" mechanism, in which vesicles transiently bind one cell and then move on to interact with additional cells. This latter mode directly challenges the conventional assumption that a single vesicle signals to only a single recipient cell, suggesting instead that one vesicle can sequentially trigger downstream responses in multiple cells. The paper also outlines experimental approaches that could be used to investigate these surface-binding interactions more rigorously. The authors argue that a more complete understanding of these signaling modes has implications for both fundamental cell biology and the development of extracellular vesicle-based therapeutics.
items.citation: Wojciech Chrzanowski, Joy Wolfram. Rethinking Extracellular Vesicle Signaling. Advanced Materials. 2026

items.title: Mechanistic advances in microbial nanobiotechnology and their applications in sustainable agriculture, environment and biomedicine
items.summary: This review examines the field of microbial nanobiotechnology, which combines microbiology and nanotechnology to develop sustainable solutions across medicine, agriculture, and environmental management. The authors survey how microorganisms such as bacteria, fungi, and algae can biosynthesize nanoparticles through biochemical pathways that are environmentally benign and cost-effective, yielding particles with controllable size, shape, and functional properties. These biogenic nanoparticles show promise in biomedical contexts including targeted drug delivery, imaging, and antimicrobial treatments, as well as in environmental remediation such as wastewater treatment and pollution control. The review also highlights how tools like genetic engineering and synthetic biology are advancing nanoparticle synthesis and characterization, while noting that scalability, biosafety, regulatory concerns, and ethical implications remain substantial barriers to commercial translation. The authors conclude that addressing these challenges through multidisciplinary collaboration is essential for the field to fulfill its potential in tackling global health, environmental, and industrial problems.
items.citation: Mir Sajad Rabani, Meenakshi Shrivastav, Mudasir Fayaz et al.. Mechanistic advances in microbial nanobiotechnology and their applications in sustainable agriculture, environment and biomedicine. Discover Nano. 2026

items.title: Ultrasensitive Enzyme-Free Detection of Proteins on Magnetic Beads
items.summary: This paper studied the development of an enzyme-free platform for ultrasensitive protein biomarker detection aimed at improving accessibility in resource-limited settings. The researchers created a system called efMOSAIC that uses hybridization chain reaction-based signal amplifiers on magnetic beads, eliminating the need for enzymes that typically require cold chain infrastructure and specialized laboratory conditions. The platform achieves detection limits comparable to established single-molecule digital assays while supporting multiplexed biomarker detection from human plasma samples, including cytokines relevant to clinical workflows. A key finding was that the signal amplifier reagents remain stable when stored at room temperature for up to six months, removing a major logistical barrier for deployment in low- and middle-income countries or point-of-care settings. The authors argue that this combination of ultrasensitive performance, simplified workflows, and temperature-stable reagents positions efMOSAIC as a transformative tool for expanding access to advanced protein diagnostics globally.
items.venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society
items.citation: Karan Malhotra, Louise L. Hansen, Samuel Han et al.. Ultrasensitive Enzyme-Free Detection of Proteins on Magnetic Beads. Journal of the American Chemical Society. 2026

items.title: Histoplasmosis: a missing piece in the global efforts to end HIV deaths
items.citation: Alessandro C Pasqualotto, Thuy Vi Le, Tarsila Vieceli et al.. Histoplasmosis: a missing piece in the global efforts to end HIV deaths. The Lancet HIV. 2026

items.title: Bounds for inertialess dynamo
items.summary: This paper derives rigorous necessary conditions for dynamo action in rotating convection within a magnetohydrodynamic framework, examining both a rapidly rotating inviscid plane layer and a viscous system at arbitrary rotation rates. Unlike classical kinematic dynamo bounds, the analysis couples magnetic field evolution to an inertialess force balance, meaning the flow and magnetic field are not treated independently. The authors establish that the buoyancy-driven component of the flow must satisfy certain norm inequalities involving the magnetic Reynolds number, with a refined anisotropic constraint obtained through a poloidal-toroidal decomposition. For the viscous case, additional necessary conditions are derived for the growth of magnetic enstrophy and combined thermo-magnetic energy. A key result is that a specific scaling relationship between the Rayleigh number and Ekman number is necessary for dynamo action to occur, providing new constraints linking convective forcing to rotational effects in planetary and astrophysical dynamo contexts.
items.citation: Ali Arslan, Hezekiah Grayer. Bounds for inertialess dynamo. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Renormalization-guided cascade upscaling for lattice field generation
items.summary: This paper introduces a machine-learning algorithm for generating lattice field configurations that is guided by renormalization-group principles. The method works by approximately inverting a renormalization-group transformation: long-distance modes are supplied through a perfect blocking construction, while a conditional normalizing flow reconstructs the missing short-distance details, and brief rethermalization corrects residual errors. The approach is tested on two-dimensional scalar field theory at criticality, where the algorithm is applied recursively in cascades to reach lattice sizes far larger than those used during training. A key finding is that a normalizing flow trained on relatively small lattices can be reused at each scale in the cascade to generate physically correct configurations at much larger lattice sizes, demonstrating strong generalization across length scales.
items.citation: Anna Hasenfratz, Ethan T. Neil, Letizia Parato et al.. Renormalization-guided cascade upscaling for lattice field generation. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Renormalization-guided inverse blocking for lattice field generation: construction and validation
items.summary: This paper proposes and validates a new algorithm for generating lattice field configurations by approximately inverting a renormalization-group blocking transformation. The method optimizes the blocking using a "perfect blocking" condition so that the coarse-grained lattice distribution is captured by a simple action, then separates the blocking into an invertible smoothing step and a decimation step, with a conditional normalizing flow used to reconstruct the short-distance degrees of freedom lost during decimation. A brief rethermalization step corrects residual mismatches, and because long-distance modes are supplied by the coarse ensemble, the procedure can be applied recursively to scale up to much larger lattices from a small initial ensemble. Testing in two-dimensional scalar field theory at criticality, the authors demonstrate stable cascade upscaling across several orders of magnitude in lattice volume on local computational resources. Rethermalization tests confirm that short-distance mismatches relax quickly while mismatches in the relevant thermal direction relax much more slowly, and the authors argue the approach has natural extensions toward higher-dimensional, gauge, and fermionic theories.
items.citation: Anna Hasenfratz, Ethan T. Neil, Letizia Parato et al.. Renormalization-guided inverse blocking for lattice field generation: construction and validation. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Quantum Fourier transform for the symmetric group
items.summary: This paper revisits the quantum Fourier transform (QFT) for the symmetric group, a canonical example of a non-abelian QFT that is fundamental to quantum computing. Building on earlier constructions, the authors carefully reanalyze the gate complexity and circuit depth of the existing algorithm. They find that the previously reported complexities require revision, correcting them to specific polynomial bounds in terms of the group size parameter. Additionally, the authors identify a suboptimality in the choice of transversal elements used in the construction and propose a simpler, improved realization of the symmetric group QFT.
items.citation: Carli Bruinsma, Dmitry Grinko, Maris Ozols. Quantum Fourier transform for the symmetric group. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Exact quantification of nonlocal magic
items.summary: This paper addresses a fundamental open question about quantum resources: how much of the "magic" (nonstabilizerness) in a shared quantum state arises from correlations between parties rather than from local properties alone. The authors solved this optimization problem exactly for the stabilizer fidelity, showing that the nonlocal magic of any pure multiqubit state is determined by how far its entanglement spectrum lies from the closest spectrum of Bell pairs. This framework reveals an unexpected connection to entanglement embezzlement: a family of states can universally embezzle entanglement under local operations and classical communication if and only if its nonlocal magic diverges. Crucially, the relevant property is not the total amount of entanglement but rather how the entanglement spectrum distributes its weight across factor-of-two windows of rank, which explains why critical chains and random-singlet states can share identical logarithmic entanglement scaling yet possess unbounded and vanishing nonlocal magic, respectively. The results make nonlocal magic an operationally meaningful measure of quantum correlations that is accessible through tensor-network simulations and entanglement spectroscopy experiments.
items.citation: Piotr Sierant. Exact quantification of nonlocal magic. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Offline-Verifiable Accountability for Cross-Organization Agent Messaging: A Preserved Evidence-Bundle Approach
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of verifying accountability in cross-organization agent-to-agent messaging workflows when live systems are unavailable, controlled by a single party, or not trusted by all participants. The authors developed a preserved evidence-bundle model in which each workflow event carries policy-required cryptographic evidence — including sender authentication, log commitments, witness-backed checkpoints, append-only continuity proofs, delegation authorization, and receiver-signed receipts — alongside a policy-controlled offline verifier that evaluates whether a bundle meets explicitly stated evidentiary requirements. The verifier deliberately avoids inferring delivery or receipt from transport behavior or log inclusion alone, requiring instead that all accepted claims be directly supported by preserved evidence. In a prototype evaluation spanning hundreds of complete workflows and valid preserved bundles, the system rejected all corrupted or policy-insufficient bundles with no false acceptances, while checkpoint-context anchoring was identified as the highest-latency component. The work positions itself as providing an auditor-centered, offline basis for dispute review that does not depend on platform-specific logs or cooperative live services.
items.citation: Adil Alshammari, Hayretdin Bahsi. Offline-Verifiable Accountability for Cross-Organization Agent Messaging: A Preserved Evidence-Bundle Approach. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Feasibility, Acceptability, and Test Performance of Point-of-Care Nucleic Acid Tests for HIV Testing and Viral Load Monitoring in the United States: Prospective Longitudinal Mixed-Methods Study.
items.summary: This study examined the feasibility, acceptability, and diagnostic performance of point-of-care nucleic acid tests for HIV detection and viral load monitoring in clinical and community settings in the United States. The researchers enrolled participants across two sites in Seattle, Washington, including individuals seeking HIV testing, pre-exposure prophylaxis, or post-exposure prophylaxis, as well as people already living with HIV, using qualitative and semiquantitative point-of-care nucleic acid test devices alongside standard laboratory testing for comparison. The study employed a mixed-methods prospective design that included a randomized clinical trial arm, acceptability surveys, in-depth interviews, and time-and-motion observations to comprehensively assess implementation outcomes. Enrollment was completed with several hundred participants across multiple study groups, though the primary analyses evaluating test performance, impact on time to viral suppression, and acceptability are not yet complete and are anticipated in forthcoming publications. The abstract is essentially a protocol and feasibility report, and no performance or outcome results are yet available to summarize.
items.citation: Niemann LA, Violette LR, Cornelius-Hudson A et al.. Feasibility, Acceptability, and Test Performance of Point-of-Care Nucleic Acid Tests for HIV Testing and Viral Load Monitoring in the United States: Prospective Longitudinal Mixed-Methods Study.. JMIR research protocols. 2026

items.title: Brief Report: Association Between Pharmacologic Tenofovir Adherence Measures and Subsequent 24-Week Viral Load Outcomes for People With HIV in South Africa.
items.summary: This study evaluated whether pharmacologic measures of tenofovir adherence could predict future HIV viremia among people with HIV receiving antiretroviral therapy in South Africa.
