Researchers compared three adherence measures — a point-of-care urine tenofovir assay, quantitative urine tenofovir by liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry, and tenofovir-diphosphate concentrations in dried blood spots — and examined their associations with current and subsequent viral load outcomes at twenty-four weeks using logistic regression. Tenofovir-diphosphate in dried blood spots was the only measure significantly associated with viremia at twenty-four weeks, suggesting it reflects longer-term adherence patterns most relevant to future viral suppression. An undetectable point-of-care urine tenofovir result was associated with current viremia, lower CD4 counts, and likely recent treatment initiation, but did not predict future viremia. The findings suggest that dried blood spot tenofovir-diphosphate measurement is the most useful pharmacologic tool for identifying patients at risk of subsequent viremia and guiding targeted adherence interventions.
items.venue: Journal of acquired immune deficiency syndromes (1999)
items.citation: Bodley N, Govender K, Moodley P et al.. Brief Report: Association Between Pharmacologic Tenofovir Adherence Measures and Subsequent 24-Week Viral Load Outcomes for People With HIV in South Africa.. Journal of acquired immune deficiency syndromes (1999). 2026

items.title: Can exercise affect immune function to increase susceptibility to infection?
items.summary: This debate article examines a central and contested question in exercise immunology: whether exercise itself can suppress immune function and increase susceptibility to infection. The authors structured the discussion around opposing arguments concerning whether high-performance athletes face greater infection risk than the general population, whether exercise independently alters immunity beyond confounding factors such as sleep disruption, psychological stress, travel, and nutritional deficits, and whether the biomarkers and study designs used to assess immune health in this context are adequate. There is broad agreement that regular, moderate-intensity exercise of shorter duration benefits immune defense, particularly in older or chronically ill individuals, whereas arduous exercise characteristic of elite athletes and military personnel has long been thought to suppress immunity. However, the extent to which exercise per se, rather than the constellation of stressors accompanying intense training and competition, causally drives increased infection risk remains unresolved. Both sides agree that infection susceptibility is multifactorial, and the article calls for more rigorous empirical research to disentangle the specific contribution of exercise from other shared immune-activating factors in these populations.
items.citation: Richard J. Simpson, Richard J. Simpson, Maree Gleeson et al.. Can exercise affect immune function to increase susceptibility to infection?. PubMed. 2026

items.title: Multi-omics and artificial intelligence for precision drug discovery and potential clinical applications
items.summary: This review paper examines how the integration of multiomics technologies with artificial intelligence is reshaping precision drug discovery and clinical translation. The authors analyze multiomics approaches spanning genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, and metabolomics alongside advanced AI methodologies including deep learning, exploring their combined application across the drug development pipeline. The paper covers specific applications such as target deconvolution, drug repositioning, de novo compound discovery, virtual screening, pharmacokinetic modeling, and safety assessment, with case examples drawn from oncology, neurodegenerative diseases, and cardiovascular conditions. The authors find that this convergence holds substantial promise for accelerating target identification, optimizing lead compounds, and improving clinical trial design, while acknowledging persistent challenges including data harmonization, reproducibility, and algorithmic bias. The review concludes that the fusion of multiomics and AI represents a foundational shift toward more precise, data-driven therapeutic innovation in bench-to-clinic translational medicine.
items.citation: Yuqing Liu, Kun Zhu, Weijun Peng et al.. Multi-omics and artificial intelligence for precision drug discovery and potential clinical applications. Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy. 2026

items.title: Oral Nirmatrelvir–Ritonavir for Covid-19 in Higher-Risk Outpatients
items.summary: These two open-label platform trials examined whether nirmatrelvir–ritonavir reduces hospitalization or death in vaccinated or previously infected higher-risk adults with COVID-19, a population distinct from the unvaccinated high-risk outpatients in whom the drug originally demonstrated benefit. Conducted in the United Kingdom and Canada, the trials randomly assigned community-dwelling adults who tested positive for SARS-CoV-2 and had been symptomatic for five days or fewer to receive either nirmatrelvir–ritonavir plus usual care or usual care alone, with the primary outcome being hospitalization or death within 28 days. Rates of hospitalization or death were very low and nearly identical between treatment and control groups in both trials, and neither trial demonstrated a statistically meaningful probability of superiority for the drug. Although a substudy confirmed that nirmatrelvir–ritonavir reduced viral load by the end of treatment, this virological effect did not translate into a clinical benefit. The authors conclude that nirmatrelvir–ritonavir does not reduce hospitalization or death among vaccinated higher-risk outpatients with SARS-CoV-2 infection.
items.citation: Christopher C. Butler, Andrew Pinto, Victoria Harris et al.. Oral Nirmatrelvir–Ritonavir for Covid-19 in Higher-Risk Outpatients. New England Journal of Medicine. 2026

items.title: 2025 Inborn errors of immunity practice parameter
items.citation: Jordan S. Orange, Javier Chinen, Caroline C. Horner et al.. 2025 Inborn errors of immunity practice parameter. Annals of Allergy Asthma & Immunology. 2026

items.title: CRISPR-Cas systems as next-generation antimicrobials: a systemic review of mechanisms, delivery strategies, and translational challenges
items.summary: This systematic review examined the potential of CRISPR-Cas systems as precision antimicrobials against multidrug-resistant bacteria, which have increasingly rendered conventional antibiotics ineffective. The authors synthesized preclinical and experimental evidence on different CRISPR effectors, including Cas9, Cas12, and Cas13, evaluating their mechanisms of action, delivery platforms, and therapeutic outcomes against resistant bacterial targets. The reviewed studies demonstrated that CRISPR-Cas tools can kill or resensitize resistant bacteria through mechanisms such as chromosomal double-strand break induction, resistance plasmid elimination, and RNA-targeted cleavage, with phage-mediated delivery showing the most consistent efficacy across complex environments and animal models. One CRISPR-enhanced engineered bacteriophage cocktail has progressed to clinical evaluation, representing a meaningful translational milestone. Nevertheless, the review identifies substantial remaining barriers including narrow host range, physiological instability, emergence of escape mutations, and insufficient long-term safety data, concluding that optimized delivery strategies, multiplex targeting, and standardized regulatory frameworks will be necessary for clinical translation.
items.citation: Maha S.I. Wizrah. CRISPR-Cas systems as next-generation antimicrobials: a systemic review of mechanisms, delivery strategies, and translational challenges. Frontiers in Microbiology. 2026

items.title: Chitosan Derivatives: Challenges and Opportunities in the Green and Sustainable Transition Era
items.summary: This review examines the production and chemical modification of chitosan derivatives through the lens of green and sustainable chemistry principles. The authors surveyed the full production pipeline, from chitin isolation across diverse natural sources and deacetylation through to downstream chemical modification of chitosan. The review highlights sustainable methodologies including eco-efficient isolation and purification strategies, continuous-flow processes, and greener synthetic approaches such as click chemistry. The authors argue that interdisciplinary collaboration and a holistic approach to process design are essential for advancing cost-effective, safe, and high-performing chitosan derivatives while minimizing environmental impact.
items.citation: Ana Morais, Rita Lima, Madalena Pinto et al.. Chitosan Derivatives: Challenges and Opportunities in the Green and Sustainable Transition Era. Molecules. 2026

items.title: A Similarity Theorem and Its Breakdown in Atomic Black Hole Accretion
items.summary: This paper establishes and analyzes an exact scaling symmetry in the problem of atomic gas accreting onto a point mass, such as a black hole embedded in an ambient medium. The authors prove that simultaneously rescaling the black hole mass and ambient number density by inverse factors leaves all dimensionless physical quantities—including optical depths, Eddington ratios, and variability patterns—unchanged, and demonstrate this rescaling is unique within its class. They introduce a dimensionless growth parameter that measures how much mass is gained per Bondi time, showing it is equivalent to the expansion speed of the Bondi radius in units of the ambient sound speed, so that a value of unity corresponds to sonic dilation of the accretion sphere. Using this parameter, they identify a finite mass threshold beyond which rapidly accreting systems—including canonical hyper-Eddington accretion scenarios—break the similarity, and show that no nontrivial stationary growing solution can simultaneously preserve the atomic scaling symmetry and self-consistent radiative flux. The theorem thus provides a unified framework connecting radiating Bondi accretion and feedback-regulated scalings while delineating the regime where quasi-static, fixed-mass approximations lose validity.
items.citation: Marcus DuPont. A Similarity Theorem and Its Breakdown in Atomic Black Hole Accretion. arXiv. 2026

items.title: PULSAR: Pooled Unified Late-Interaction Search and Retrieval for Enterprise Visual Document RAG
items.summary: This paper presents PULSAR, a vision-first retrieval system designed for searching visually dense financial documents such as pitch decks and board packs in an enterprise investment context. The system indexes document page images directly using a frozen ColPali-style backbone with a two-stage late-interaction approach, where compact page summaries enable initial retrieval and a finer pooled representation handles exact rescoring, eliminating the need for costly optical character recognition and figure verbalization pipelines. The pooled architecture dramatically reduces vector-search latency and supports far higher query throughput under concurrent load compared to unpooled configurations, while maintaining nearly equivalent retrieval quality as measured by standard ranking metrics. Ingestion costs are substantially lower than the OCR-based baseline the system replaced, and in production deployment the system more than doubles answer-fact recall over that baseline. The work demonstrates that a vision-native, pooled late-interaction design can meet both the latency and freshness demands of high-volume, time-sensitive financial document retrieval at scale.
items.citation: Benjamin Constable, Anup Roy, Vishal Sharma et al.. PULSAR: Pooled Unified Late-Interaction Search and Retrieval for Enterprise Visual Document RAG. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Quadratic Probing Insertions Are $ε^{-(1+o(1))}$
items.summary: Quadratic probing is a classical open-addressing hash table scheme in which collisions are resolved by probing positions at quadratically increasing offsets, yet its theoretical performance has remained poorly understood despite decades of use. The central conjecture holds that at load factor one minus epsilon, the expected insertion time should be on the order of the reciprocal of epsilon, but even establishing any bound expressible purely as a function of that reciprocal had been an open problem since the scheme was introduced. This paper proves that the expected insertion time is epsilon to the power of negative one plus a sub-polynomial correction, thereby settling the complexity of quadratic probing up to sub-polynomial factors and coming within a sub-polynomial gap of the conjectured optimal bound.
items.citation: Yang Hu, William Kuszmaul, Jingxun Liang et al.. Quadratic Probing Insertions Are $ε^{-(1+o(1))}$. arXiv. 2026

items.title: A Single Spin Switches the Steady-State Phase of an Open Quantum System
items.summary: This paper investigates how adding a single spin to a dissipative many-body quantum system can dramatically alter its macroscopic steady-state behavior, challenging the conventional expectation that one-constituent changes produce negligible effects on intensive observables. The authors study a collective spin model with dissipation imbalance and show that the parity of the total spin number determines whether the Dicke ladder samples a zero of the nonlinear-loss amplitude in the jump operator, a structural difference that controls whether certain quantum states are transient or form a recurrent class. Through exact finite-size calculations, they demonstrate that exponential competition between stationary weights amplifies this microscopic connectivity difference, producing a first-order dissipative phase transition that switches the steady state between a phase-averaged ring and a south-polar fixed point, but only along the odd-spin-number sequence. Single-spin loading confirms that rare quantum fluctuations are sufficient to induce this phase switch without any postselection, making the effect physically accessible. The findings identify zeros in jump operators as a general mechanism by which single-constituent changes can exert control over the phase of an open quantum system.
items.citation: Jianwen Jie. A Single Spin Switches the Steady-State Phase of an Open Quantum System. arXiv. 2026

items.title: MaCoPlanner: LLM-Assisted Manual-Compiled Task Planning with Proactive Safety Verification for Robotic Industrial Panel Operation
items.summary: The paper addresses the challenge of robotic operation of industrial control panels, which requires robots to follow complex operating procedures, safety rules, and device-state constraints scattered across heterogeneous equipment manuals. The authors developed MaCoPlanner, a task-planning framework that compiles equipment manuals into a typed intermediate representation, retrieves relevant evidence for plan generation, and symbolically verifies candidate plans against procedural and state-transition constraints before any physical action is taken. Detected constraint violations are localized and fed back for targeted repair, while plans that cannot be resolved within a refinement budget are rejected outright, and a separate execution interface grounds verified symbolic actions to physical controls. The system achieved a notably low final violation rate and substantially improved task success rates compared to a baseline that used raw manuals directly, with gains observed across both moderately and highly complex task levels. Experiments on a controller-panel simulator further demonstrated the feasibility of integrated execution under representative conditions, though the authors explicitly note the system is not claimed to be ready for real industrial deployment.
items.citation: Guipeng Xin, Jiahe Xua, Mohammad Deghat et al.. MaCoPlanner: LLM-Assisted Manual-Compiled Task Planning with Proactive Safety Verification for Robotic Industrial Panel Operation. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Unsteady airfoil aerodynamics in attached flow: From unsteady thin airfoil theory to wind turbine application
items.summary: This paper addresses the formulation and implementation of attached-flow unsteady aerodynamics for wind turbine solvers, focusing on the region of the blade where flow remains predominantly attached and which dominates power production and loading. Starting from classical unsteady thin-airfoil theory, the authors derived circulatory and non-circulatory loads expressed as lift, drag, and moment coefficients compatible with blade-element momentum, lifting-line, and actuator-line methods, using shed-wake memory cast in terms of downwash velocity rather than angle of attack. The work identifies key modeling choices and clarifies how airfoil polar lookup, shed-wake memory, non-circulatory loads, consistent force definitions, and separated-flow dynamics combine into a complete engineering model. Verification through a coned straight-blade benchmark revealed that omitting certain contributions introduces meaningful errors in thrust and power, with lift-direction projection having the largest influence on power and the omission of a mid-chord heaving-acceleration term disrupting non-circulatory normal-force cancellation. A vertical-axis wind turbine case in the zero-onset-flow, ideal thin-airfoil limit confirmed that all circulatory and non-circulatory contributions cancel exactly, yielding zero net rotor torque and validating the theoretical consistency of the formulation.
items.citation: Ang Li, Mac Gaunaa, Georg Raimund Pirrung. Unsteady airfoil aerodynamics in attached flow: From unsteady thin airfoil theory to wind turbine application. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Brief Report: Sustainability of the Effects of Linkage Case Management on Posthospitalization HIV Outcomes: The Daraja Randomized Clinical Trial.
items.summary: The Daraja randomized clinical trial examined whether the benefits of a linkage case management intervention for hospitalized people with HIV would persist beyond its primary endpoint. Researchers followed participants for an additional year after the initial twelve-month assessment, evaluating continuity in HIV care, antiretroviral therapy adherence, and viral load suppression at twenty-four months post-hospital discharge. Intervention participants demonstrated significantly higher rates of all three outcomes compared to those receiving standard care, with differences exceeding ten percentage points across each measure. The intervention's effect on time to HIV clinic linkage and antiretroviral therapy initiation also remained significant at two years, with a notable proportion of control participants still untreated at that point. These findings indicate that linkage case management initiated at hospitalization produces durable improvements in HIV care engagement and viral suppression well beyond the active intervention period.
items.venue: Journal of acquired immune deficiency syndromes (1999)
items.citation: Willkens M, Issarow B, Kisigo GA et al.. Brief Report: Sustainability of the Effects of Linkage Case Management on Posthospitalization HIV Outcomes: The Daraja Randomized Clinical Trial.. Journal of acquired immune deficiency syndromes (1999). 2026

items.title: New to cohort, not new to care: leveraging historical data in HIV clinical cohorts in the United States.
items.summary: This paper examined how to distinguish patients newly entering HIV care from those transferring from prior care within United States clinical cohorts, a distinction important for accurate research on care outcomes. Using data from a large multi-cohort collaboration spanning over two decades, the researchers assessed the availability of five types of historical HIV data at enrollment, including antiretroviral therapy prescriptions, CD4 counts, viral loads, suppressed viral load at enrollment, and AIDS-defining conditions. They developed an algorithm to classify participants as new to care, transfers, re-engaging after a gap, or previously in care with unknown transfer status. The analysis revealed a substantial shift over time, with transfers becoming the dominant enrollment category while those truly new to care declined, and the gap between earliest known HIV history and cohort enrollment grew considerably. The authors recommend that HIV cohorts systematically collect all five data types and apply the proposed algorithm, tailored to their specific context, to improve the accuracy of identifying participants who are genuinely new to HIV care.
items.citation: Haw NJL, Hogan B, Humes E et al.. New to cohort, not new to care: leveraging historical data in HIV clinical cohorts in the United States.. American journal of epidemiology. 2026

items.title: Diagnostic accuracy of point-of-care urine tenofovir test, and associations between metrics of tenofovir use and treatment outcomes in a community ART programme
items.summary: This study evaluated two methods of measuring tenofovir adherence—a point-of-care urine tenofovir assay and dried blood spot tenofovir diphosphate concentrations—in a South African community antiretroviral therapy programme, examining both the diagnostic accuracy of the point-of-care test and the relationship between these adherence metrics and treatment outcomes. Researchers measured tenofovir concentrations using liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry as the reference standard and assessed associations between the adherence measures, concurrent viraemia, and retention in care over sixteen weeks. The point-of-care urine tenofovir assay demonstrated high sensitivity but only moderate specificity compared to the reference method. The vast majority of participants without viraemia had detectable urine tenofovir or high dried blood spot tenofovir diphosphate levels, consistent with good short- and medium-term adherence, though neither adherence measure was associated with retention in care at sixteen weeks.
items.citation: Naidu L, Tlhaku K, Govender K et al.. Diagnostic accuracy of point-of-care urine tenofovir test, and associations between metrics of tenofovir use and treatment outcomes in a community ART programme. 2026

items.title: Diagnostic performance of a field-deployable iiPCR platform and viral load dynamics of MPXV Clade IIb in a cohort with high prevalence of HIV.
items.summary: This study evaluated a field-deployable insulated isothermal PCR platform as an alternative to standard quantitative real-time PCR for diagnosing Mpox virus Clade IIb infection, with particular attention to diagnostic performance across specimen types and in a cohort with high HIV prevalence. Researchers prospectively enrolled confirmed Mpox patients and tested multiple specimen types using both the portable iiPCR system and reference qPCR, while also tracking viral load dynamics over the course of illness and performing phylogenetic characterization. The iiPCR platform achieved analytical sensitivity and qualitative concordance identical to qPCR, with lesion-derived specimens consistently yielding the highest detection rates and lowest cycle threshold values compared to non-lesion specimens. Among people living with HIV who were receiving antiretroviral therapy and had preserved immune function, no differences in diagnostic performance or viral load dynamics were observed relative to HIV-negative individuals. These findings support the potential of the portable iiPCR system as a decentralized diagnostic tool for Mpox, especially when lesion specimens are available.
items.citation: Liu LT, Chen CJ, Lin PC et al.. Diagnostic performance of a field-deployable iiPCR platform and viral load dynamics of MPXV Clade IIb in a cohort with high prevalence of HIV.. Annals of medicine. 2026

items.title: Comparative evaluation of a multi-antigen malaria rapid diagnostic test against qPCR and microscopy in a co-endemic area of Southern Ethiopia.
items.summary: This study evaluated the diagnostic performance of a multi-antigen rapid diagnostic test for malaria in a region of Southern Ethiopia where both *Plasmodium falciparum* and *Plasmodium vivax* co-circulate, a setting complicated by low-density infections and gene deletions that can undermine conventional testing. Researchers enrolled febrile patients from health facilities during peak transmission season and compared the Bioline Malaria multi-Ag RDT, which detects HRP2 and dual pLDH antigens, against expert microscopy and quantitative PCR. The multi-antigen RDT performed well relative to microscopy, showing high sensitivity and specificity with near-perfect agreement, but its sensitivity dropped meaningfully when qPCR served as the reference standard, revealing that submicroscopic infections were frequently missed. Overall, qPCR detected the highest proportion of malaria cases, including more species-specific and mixed infections than either RDT or microscopy. The authors conclude that while the multi-antigen RDT is suitable for routine clinical diagnosis, more sensitive tools are needed for surveillance and elimination efforts in co-endemic settings.
items.citation: Bogale A, Mitiku A, Tefera S et al.. Comparative evaluation of a multi-antigen malaria rapid diagnostic test against qPCR and microscopy in a co-endemic area of Southern Ethiopia.. Scientific reports. 2026

items.title: Characterization of arbovirus infections in patients within Haiti by screening discarded malaria rapid diagnostic test cassettes.
items.summary: This study investigated circulating arboviruses in Haiti during a period when traditional surveillance was disrupted by political instability, using an innovative approach of extracting nucleic acids from discarded malaria rapid diagnostic test cassettes collected from febrile patients. Samples were screened using a series of real-time PCR assays targeting flaviviruses, alphaviruses, and Oropouche virus, followed by next-generation sequencing and phylogenetic analysis on positive samples. The predominant finding was dengue virus serotype three, detected exclusively in samples from a single year, with phylogenetic analysis placing these sequences in close relationship to strains circulating across the Caribbean region during the same period. No evidence of alphavirus or Oropouche virus infections was detected in the subset of samples tested for those pathogens. The study demonstrates that discarded malaria rapid diagnostic tests can serve as a practical and resource-efficient surveillance tool for arboviral diseases in resource-limited or insecure settings where conventional public health infrastructure is compromised.
items.citation: Matulis GA, Smith HP, Hall G et al.. Characterization of arbovirus infections in patients within Haiti by screening discarded malaria rapid diagnostic test cassettes.. PLoS neglected tropical diseases. 2026

items.title: ZigBee Based Low Latency IoT and AI Integrated Framework for Real Time Telehealth Monitoring
items.summary: This paper presents a wireless telehealth monitoring framework that integrates IoT sensors with cloud-based artificial intelligence to enable continuous, real-time health surveillance for elderly and chronically ill patients. The system uses the ZigBee communication protocol to transmit physiological data—including heart rate, body temperature, and blood oxygen levels—from wearable sensors to a centralized processing unit with minimal power consumption and low latency. Multiple machine learning algorithms, including random forest, support vector machine, and logistic regression, were applied to detect health anomalies, with the random forest model achieving the highest performance in terms of accuracy and recall. The framework was validated in a real-world care facility setting, demonstrating suitability for long-term deployment through its low delay and energy efficiency. The authors claim the system addresses key limitations of existing telehealth solutions—such as high latency and excessive false alarms—while offering a scalable, modular architecture that can accommodate additional sensor types to meet diverse patient needs.
items.citation: B. V. Ravi Kumar, Mohammad Shahnawaz Shaikh. ZigBee Based Low Latency IoT and AI Integrated Framework for Real Time Telehealth Monitoring. Emerging Science Journal. 2026

items.title: Cancer workforce—a global crisis: a Lancet Oncology Commission
items.citation: Hedvig Hricak, Zachary J. Ward, Fabio Ynoe Moraes et al.. Cancer workforce—a global crisis: a Lancet Oncology Commission. The Lancet Oncology. 2026

items.title: Biosynthesis of cinchona alkaloids
items.summary: This paper investigated the biosynthetic pathway by which cinchona plants produce their characteristic alkaloids, including the antimalarial drug quinine and the chiral catalyst cinchonidine, whose biosynthetic origins have remained largely unknown. Using a combination of isotopic labelling, gene silencing, single-nucleus RNA sequencing, and comparative transcriptomics, the researchers identified the genes responsible for constructing the distinctive quinoline-quinuclidine scaffold of these compounds, revealing several unexpected enzymatic transformations including an unusual cyclization that produces a previously unreported quaternary amine intermediate. Heterologous expression of the discovered genes in *Nicotiana benthamiana* enabled production of multiple cinchona alkaloid intermediates, and the same system could accept non-native fluorinated and chlorinated tryptamine substrates to generate halogenated analogues. These findings resolve a longstanding mystery in plant biochemistry and open avenues for producing cinchona alkaloids and novel derivatives through metabolic engineering.
items.citation: Blaise Kimbadi Lombe, Tingan Zhou, Gyumin Kang et al.. Biosynthesis of cinchona alkaloids. Nature. 2026

items.title: Safety of a large language model-based clinical decision support system in African primary healthcare
items.summary: This study evaluated the safety and clinical utility of a large language model embedded within electronic medical records to support clinical decision-making at primary care clinics in Kenya. Trained physicians retrospectively reviewed over a thousand patient encounter records generated with the system's assistance, assessing for hallucinations, guideline alignment, and the presence of harmful or beneficial recommendations. The system rarely hallucinated and almost universally aligned with local clinical guidelines, yet clinicians frequently left documentation unmodified, meaning both harmful and helpful suggestions were often carried forward unchanged. Critically, actively harmful recommendations from the model appeared in a meaningful proportion of final clinical documents, while the system's capacity to mitigate pre-existing clinical risk in initial notes was also demonstrated but less frequently realised. The authors conclude that although the tool shows promise for quality improvement in African primary healthcare, the tendency for clinicians to adopt harmful outputs more readily than beneficial ones highlights urgent need for improved usability, locally tailored safety guardrails, and prospective trials to establish patient-level benefit.
items.citation: Ambrose Agweyu, Paul Mwaniki, Wilkister Musau et al.. Safety of a large language model-based clinical decision support system in African primary healthcare. Nature Health. 2026

items.title: Advances in Natural Product Extraction: Established and Emerging Technologies
items.summary: This review examines recent advances in the extraction and isolation of natural products, motivated by the renewed centrality of nature-derived compounds in modern drug discovery. The authors survey a broad range of established and emerging methodologies, including green and designer solvent systems, pressurized and ultrasound-assisted extraction, supercritical fluid techniques, and integrated purification workflows. A particular focus is placed on the growing role of artificial intelligence and machine learning in optimizing solvent selection, extraction conditions, and metabolite dereplication within complex biological matrices. Together, these developments have improved compound recovery, selectivity, and analytical throughput while reducing processing time. The review concludes that combinatorial extraction strategies and AI-driven approaches have collectively expanded the scope of detectable and characterizable metabolites over the recent period surveyed.
items.citation: Carsyn R. Travis, Jared McMaster, Fatima Rivas. Advances in Natural Product Extraction: Established and Emerging Technologies. Molecules. 2026

items.title: Macrophage metabolic exhaustion and PANoptotic cell death drive chronic tissue inflammation in rheumatoid arthritis
items.summary: This study investigated why chronic joint inflammation persists in rheumatoid arthritis despite the presence of macrophages normally associated with tissue repair. The researchers found that patient-derived synovial repair-type macrophages produce the complement protein C1q and simultaneously express its receptor, creating an autocrine signaling loop that drives disease. C1q stimulation induced a state of metabolic exhaustion in these macrophages, characterized by impaired energy production and NAD cleavage by the mitochondrial enzyme SARM1, which converted NAD into cyclic ADP ribose and triggered a form of inflammatory cell death called PANoptosis. In animal experiments, C1q administration worsened synovitis while inhibiting SARM1 provided therapeutic benefit. The findings establish SARM1 as both a marker of metabolically stressed macrophages and a key executor of the pro-inflammatory cell death that sustains autoimmune tissue destruction in rheumatoid arthritis.
items.citation: Tao Huang, Yoshinori Takashima, Jitendra Kumar et al.. Macrophage metabolic exhaustion and PANoptotic cell death drive chronic tissue inflammation in rheumatoid arthritis. Immunity. 2026

items.title: A Similarity Theorem and Its Breakdown in Atomic Black Hole Accretion
items.summary: This paper studies the mathematical structure of gas accretion onto a point mass in an atomic medium, asking whether and when the governing physics admits an exact scaling symmetry. The authors prove that simultaneously rescaling the black hole mass and ambient density by inverse factors leaves all dimensionless physical quantities—including optical depths, Eddington ratios, and variability—unchanged, and demonstrate this rescaling is unique within the class of two-body atomic microphysics and a specified family of radiation and feedback laws. They introduce a dimensionless growth parameter defined as the fractional mass gained per Bondi time, showing it equals the Bondi radius expansion speed in units of the ambient sound speed, so that a value of unity corresponds to sonic dilation of the accretion radius. When the retained accretion rate follows a power-law in black hole mass, the system reaches this sonic boundary after a finite mass increase, and at most a finite number of additional Bondi times remain before the similarity framework loses control; the authors note that canonical hyper-Eddington accretion scenarios have already crossed this threshold. Additionally, they prove that no nontrivial stationary growing solution can simultaneously preserve the atomic similarity and self-consistent radiative flux, thereby unifying radiating Bondi and feedback-regulated accretion scalings within a single theoretical framework while delineating its limits.
items.citation: Marcus DuPont. A Similarity Theorem and Its Breakdown in Atomic Black Hole Accretion. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Renormalization-guided inverse blocking for lattice field generation: construction and validation
items.summary: This paper proposes a new algorithm for generating lattice field configurations by approximately inverting a renormalization-group blocking transformation. The approach optimizes the blocking using a "perfect blocking" condition to ensure the coarse-lattice distribution is well described by a simple action, then separates the blocking into an invertible smoothing step followed by decimation, with a conditional normalizing flow used to reconstruct the short-distance degrees of freedom that decimation removes. A brief rethermalization step corrects residual mismatches, and because the coarse ensemble provides long-distance modes, the same blocking and flow can be applied recursively to generate configurations on progressively larger lattices from a single small-volume ensemble. The method is validated in two-dimensional scalar field theory at criticality, demonstrating stable cascade upscaling across several orders of magnitude in lattice volume on local computational resources, with rethermalization tests confirming that short-distance mismatches relax quickly while infrared mismatches relax slowly as expected. The authors argue that the constituent components of the construction extend naturally toward higher-dimensional theories, including those with gauge and fermionic degrees of freedom.
items.citation: Anna Hasenfratz, Ethan T. Neil, Letizia Parato et al.. Renormalization-guided inverse blocking for lattice field generation: construction and validation. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Exact quantification of nonlocal magic
items.summary: This paper addresses the fundamental question of how much "magic" (nonstabilizerness), the resource enabling universal quantum computation beyond Clifford circuits, resides specifically in the correlations between spatially separated parties rather than in their local degrees of freedom. The authors solve an open optimization problem by deriving an exact formula for the nonlocal magic of pure multiqubit states in terms of stabilizer fidelity, showing it equals the distance of a state's entanglement spectrum from the closest spectrum of Bell pairs. They further establish a surprising connection to entanglement embezzlement, demonstrating that a family of states can universally embezzle entanglement under local operations and classical communication if and only if its nonlocal magic diverges. Notably, the relevant property is not the total amount of entanglement but how the entanglement spectrum is distributed across rank windows, which explains why critical chains and random-singlet phases can have identical logarithmic entanglement scaling yet carry unbounded and vanishing nonlocal magic, respectively. The authors argue that nonlocal magic is an operationally meaningful characterization of quantum correlations that is accessible both to tensor-network methods and to experimental entanglement spectroscopy.
items.citation: Piotr Sierant. Exact quantification of nonlocal magic. arXiv. 2026

items.title: QUEST: A Query and Extraction System for Topics in Asylum Law Application Decisions
items.summary: The paper addresses the challenge of automatically identifying credibility-related factors in legal decisions on asylum applications, which are lengthy, complex documents combining applicant narratives, original decisions, and supporting materials. The authors developed QUEST, an information retrieval system that combines synthetic query generation, topic extraction, and relevance assessment to locate information pertaining to credibility indicators within Danish asylum appeal board materials. Beyond standard retrieval evaluation metrics, they introduced a novel domain-specific evaluation framework that assesses system performance according to credibility-based relevance rather than traditional topical relevance. Their findings show that performance estimation becomes substantially more difficult when using credibility-based assessments, highlighting the particular challenge of automatically extracting credibility factors from asylum legal documents.
items.citation: Maria Vlachou, Anna Murphy Høgenhaug, Mohammad N. S. Jahromi et al.. QUEST: A Query and Extraction System for Topics in Asylum Law Application Decisions. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Offline-Verifiable Accountability for Cross-Organization Agent Messaging: A Preserved Evidence-Bundle Approach
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of verifying accountability for cross-organization agent-to-agent messaging workflows when live systems are unavailable, controlled by a single party, or not trusted by all participants. The authors propose a preserved evidence-bundle model in which each workflow event carries policy-required evidence components, including sender authentication, authenticated log commitments, witness-backed checkpoints, append-only continuity proofs, delegation-aware authorization evidence, and receiver-signed receipts where mandated. A policy-controlled offline verifier evaluates these bundles against explicit policy profiles rather than inferring delivery or receipt from transport behavior alone, ensuring that only claims supported by sufficient evidence are accepted. A prototype evaluation across hundreds of complete workflows and preserved bundles measured offline verification latency across different policy profiles and found that checkpoint-context anchoring imposed the greatest latency, while delegation and workflow-prerequisite checks required additional steps. Notably, all corrupted or policy-insufficient bundles were rejected with no false acceptances, supporting the approach's suitability for evidence-based audit and dispute resolution without dependence on live infrastructure.
items.citation: Adil Alshammari, Hayretdin Bahsi. Offline-Verifiable Accountability for Cross-Organization Agent Messaging: A Preserved Evidence-Bundle Approach. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Analysis of Polynomial Threshold Functions on Random Regular Graphs: Computational Complexity of Detecting Noisy Random Lift
items.summary: The paper studies the computational complexity of a hypothesis testing problem: distinguishing a noisy random lift of a base regular graph from a uniformly random regular graph. To address this, the authors develop the first analysis of low-degree polynomial threshold functions in this setting, a framework commonly used to establish computational lower bounds for statistical problems. A key technical contribution along the way is a new characterization of the distribution of short cycle counts in noisy random lifts up to logarithmic lengths, which generalizes several prior results on random regular graphs and random lifts. The findings extend the reach of polynomial threshold function methods to this graph-theoretic detection problem and provide foundational distributional results that unify and broaden earlier work in the area.
items.citation: Xifan Yu. Analysis of Polynomial Threshold Functions on Random Regular Graphs: Computational Complexity of Detecting Noisy Random Lift. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Advances in tuberculosis diagnostics and biomarkers, 2020-26: scientific evidence, recommendations, gaps, and developmental priorities.
items.summary: This paper reviews major advances in tuberculosis diagnostics and biomarker research over a five-year period, culminating in updated WHO policy guidance that consolidates recommendations for detecting tuberculosis disease and drug resistance into a single framework. Key developments include the expanded role of digital chest radiography with computer-aided detection as a screening and triage tool, and the broadened deployment of decentralised molecular diagnostics, including low-complexity automated and manual nucleic acid amplification tests, near point-of-care platforms, and novel specimen types such as tongue swabs and pooled sputum. Progress in non-sputum specimen testing has improved bacteriological confirmation in children and sputum-scarce populations, while advances in rapid molecular drug-resistance testing and next-generation sequencing have strengthened comprehensive susceptibility testing at reference laboratory level. Urine-based lipoarabinomannan assays offer diagnostic benefit in people with HIV and advanced disease, and host blood transcriptomic signatures show promise for prognosis and triage, alongside emerging proteomic, metabolomic, and other biomarker platforms. Despite these advances, the paper concludes that significant performance, implementation, and equity gaps persist, and no biomarker has yet met WHO target criteria for a point-of-care test capable of reliably distinguishing infection from disease, including subclinical tuberculosis.
items.citation: Walzl G, McHugh TD, Chakaya J et al.. Advances in tuberculosis diagnostics and biomarkers, 2020-26: scientific evidence, recommendations, gaps, and developmental priorities.. The Lancet. Microbe. 2027

items.title: The changing landscape of diagnosing HIV-associated tuberculosis.
items.summary: This narrative review examines how the diagnosis of tuberculosis in people with HIV has evolved from 1990 to the present day. The authors highlight the particular diagnostic challenges posed by this co-infection, including lower bacillary burden in sputum, frequent extrapulmonary or disseminated disease, and nonspecific clinical features that overlap with other opportunistic infections, all of which demand rapid diagnostic approaches. The review traces the limitations of early reliance on smear microscopy, which had reduced sensitivity in people with HIV, and describes how diagnostic algorithms for smear-negative cases led to both under- and overdiagnosis with serious consequences for patient outcomes. The introduction of nucleic acid amplification tests and urine lipoarabinomannan lateral flow assays, alongside the widespread use of antiretroviral therapy, has substantially transformed the diagnostic landscape and contributed to reductions in tuberculosis incidence and mortality. Nevertheless, the authors conclude that existing rapid tests remain imperfect in sensitivity and that only the urine lipoarabinomannan assay meets criteria for affordability and point-of-care suitability, underscoring the continued need for novel, accurate, and accessible diagnostic tools.
items.venue: South African medical journal = Suid-Afrikaanse tydskrif vir geneeskunde
items.citation: Maartens G. The changing landscape of diagnosing HIV-associated tuberculosis.. South African medical journal = Suid-Afrikaanse tydskrif vir geneeskunde. 2026

items.title: Operationalization of rapid molecular test coverage for tuberculosis in different international contexts: a scoping review.
items.summary: This scoping review examined how coverage of rapid molecular testing for tuberculosis has been defined, measured, and operationalized across different international settings. The authors searched multiple major databases spanning over a decade and synthesized findings from studies meeting their inclusion criteria. They found substantial conceptual and methodological heterogeneity in how coverage was defined, ranging from proportions of tested populations to measures of equipment availability and geographic accessibility, with no standardization across countries. Reported coverage values varied enormously, from negligible levels to roughly four-fifths of target populations, with socioeconomic, structural, and financial barriers consistently impeding access. The authors conclude that meaningful global monitoring of rapid molecular test coverage will require governmental commitment, decentralization of testing services, and adoption of uniform measurement criteria aligned with World Health Organization guidance.
items.venue: Revista da Escola de Enfermagem da U S P
items.citation: Silva DHMD, Valença ABM, Ferreira MRL et al.. Operationalization of rapid molecular test coverage for tuberculosis in different international contexts: a scoping review.. Revista da Escola de Enfermagem da U S P. 2026

items.title: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Urine-Based Molecular Testing for Urogenital Tuberculosis.
items.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the diagnostic performance of urine-based molecular testing methods — including Xpert Mycobacterium tuberculosis/rifampicin, multiplex polymerase chain reaction, and loop-mediated isothermal amplification — for detecting urogenital tuberculosis, a condition that is difficult to confirm rapidly using conventional culture. The authors pooled data from diagnostic accuracy studies involving patients with high clinical suspicion of urogenital tuberculosis, assessing sensitivity, specificity, likelihood ratios, and diagnostic odds ratios using a bivariate random-effects model. Urine-based molecular testing demonstrated high specificity and a strong area under the summary receiver operating characteristic curve, indicating good overall discriminative ability, though sensitivity was more modest. A positive test result substantially increased post-test probability of disease, while a negative result meaningfully reduced it, supporting the clinical utility of these assays. The authors conclude that urine-based molecular testing is a valuable adjunctive tool for rapid confirmation of urogenital tuberculosis, best interpreted in conjunction with clinical, imaging, and culture findings.
items.citation: Fang L, Chen X, Chen J et al.. Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Urine-Based Molecular Testing for Urogenital Tuberculosis.. Archivos espanoles de urologia. 2026

items.title: Emerging blood-based diagnostic strategies for tuberculosis.
items.summary: This review examines blood-based diagnostic approaches for tuberculosis, a disease caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis that continues to pose a major global public health burden. The authors focus on serological methods, which have gained increasing attention due to their simplicity, rapid turnaround time, and cost-effectiveness compared to conventional diagnostics such as sputum culture and rapid molecular assays. The review summarizes current biomarkers employed in TB serodiagnosis, discusses how advanced diagnostic technologies can be integrated with these approaches, and highlights their particular utility for diagnosing extrapulmonary TB and for patients who test negative using standard methods. The authors argue that these emerging blood-based strategies hold significant potential to improve TB diagnosis across a range of clinical settings.
items.citation: Yue C, Geng X, Sun X et al.. Emerging blood-based diagnostic strategies for tuberculosis.. Clinical chemistry and laboratory medicine. 2026

items.title: Diagnostic accuracy, operational feasibility, and cost considerations of Truenat MTB Plus and Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra for pulmonary tuberculosis.
items.summary: This study compared two WHO-endorsed nucleic acid amplification tests — Truenat MTB Plus and Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra — for detecting pulmonary tuberculosis and rifampicin resistance among presumptive TB patients in India. Using mycobacterial culture and phenotypic drug susceptibility testing as reference standards, the researchers prospectively tested paired sputum specimens from several hundred patients at a tuberculosis centre in New Delhi. Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra demonstrated higher sensitivity and specificity for both TB detection and rifampicin resistance identification, and produced substantially lower rates of invalid and indeterminate results compared to Truenat MTB Plus. Truenat, however, was considerably less expensive per test and offers practical advantages for decentralized settings, though its higher rates of invalid and indeterminate results increase the operational burden through the need for repeat testing. The authors conclude that a tiered diagnostic approach utilizing both platforms according to their respective strengths could help expand molecular testing access and advance tuberculosis elimination efforts.
items.citation: Sidiq Z, Anand A, Dwivedi KK et al.. Diagnostic accuracy, operational feasibility, and cost considerations of Truenat MTB Plus and Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra for pulmonary tuberculosis.. PloS one. 2026

items.title: Osteoarthritis: molecular pathogenesis and potential therapeutic options
items.summary: This review paper examines the molecular mechanisms underlying osteoarthritis, a chronic joint disorder characterized by pain, inflammation, and bone deterioration, with a focus on identifying new therapeutic targets. The authors comprehensively analyzed nociceptive pathways connecting the knee joint to the central nervous system, pathological changes in bone and cartilage, and the roles of inflammatory cytokines alongside organelle-specific dysfunctions including mitochondrial impairment, lysosomal destabilization, and unresolved endoplasmic reticulum stress. Based on these mechanistic insights, the review delineates emerging pharmacological strategies aimed at simultaneously addressing inflammatory cascades, restoring organelle homeostasis through approaches such as mitophagy enhancement and lysosomal integrity preservation, and reducing pain signaling. The authors also highlight advanced organelle-targeted drug delivery systems intended to improve therapeutic efficacy and stability. Together, these findings are proposed to establish a multimodal therapeutic framework capable of addressing both the structural and clinical manifestations of osteoarthritis.
items.citation: Yi Zhang, Yanqi Han, Ying Sun et al.. Osteoarthritis: molecular pathogenesis and potential therapeutic options. Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy. 2026

items.title: Implementation of the NHS England Lung Cancer Screening Programme over 5 years
items.summary: The paper presents a progress report on the NHS England Lung Cancer Screening Programme, a national initiative that offers low-dose computed tomography to ever-smokers aged 55–74 who meet risk thresholds determined by multivariable models. The programme operates through regionally federated clinical infrastructure guided by national strategic, clinical, and economic frameworks, and was launched in 2019 with the goal of achieving full national coverage by 2030. Over five years, more than two million people were invited and thousands of lung cancers were diagnosed, with nearly two-thirds detected at the earliest tumour stage, representing a substantial increase in early-stage diagnoses particularly in socioeconomically deprived regions. The authors conclude that the programme demonstrates feasibility and scalability in reaching high-risk and underserved populations, though inequalities in participation remain a challenge to be addressed. These findings are presented as evidence supporting broader adoption of lung cancer screening across the UK and internationally, along with practical frameworks for adaptation elsewhere.
items.citation: Richard W. Lee, Arjun Nair, Haval Balata et al.. Implementation of the NHS England Lung Cancer Screening Programme over 5 years. Nature Medicine. 2026

items.title: Nanoparticles-based phototherapy systems: molecular mechanisms and clinical applications
items.summary: This review examines nanoparticle-based phototherapy systems, focusing on how integrating nanoparticles with light-activated treatment modalities enhances therapeutic precision across a range of diseases. The authors survey the core components, classification schemes, and delivery platforms—including gold nanoparticles, liposomes, and dendrimers—that improve light absorption, tumor targeting, reactive oxygen species generation in photodynamic therapy, and localized heating in photothermal therapy. At the molecular level, the review details how light-triggered interventions induce oxidative stress, activate apoptotic and autophagic cascades, and modulate immune responses through altered cytokine profiles and T-cell activity, with relevance not only to cancer but also to cardiovascular, neurodegenerative, metabolic, and autoimmune conditions. The authors critically assess regulatory-approved agents and recent clinical trial findings, identifying key obstacles to broader clinical translation such as nanoparticle optimization, efficient light delivery, and regulatory barriers. Collectively, the review positions nanoparticle-based phototherapy as a transformative, noninvasive therapeutic strategy with broad applicability across chronic and oncological diseases.
items.citation: Deepak S. Chauhan, Rajendra Prasad, Mukesh Dhanka et al.. Nanoparticles-based phototherapy systems: molecular mechanisms and clinical applications. Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy. 2026

items.title: AI-induced never-skilling in medical education
items.citation: Yuhe Ke, Liyuan Jin, Jasmine Chiat Ling Ong et al.. AI-induced never-skilling in medical education. Nature Medicine. 2026

items.title: EULAR recommendations for the management of Behçet’s syndrome: 2025 update
items.summary: This paper presents the updated clinical practice recommendations from a major European rheumatology alliance for managing Behçet's syndrome, a complex multisystem inflammatory disease. A large, multinational task force representing multiple medical specialties, along with patient partners, conducted a systematic literature review and used a Delphi survey process to formulate and vote on updated guidance. The resulting framework comprises five overarching principles and twelve recommendations organized by organ involvement, including one entirely new recommendation and several modified ones. Key therapeutic guidance emphasizes colchicine as first-line treatment for mucocutaneous and joint manifestations, with apremilast or TNFα inhibitors reserved for refractory cases, and more aggressive immunosuppressive regimens for organ-threatening disease. The overarching principles stress the relapsing-remitting nature of the condition, the need for individualized treatment based on disease activity and prognostic factors, and the importance of multidisciplinary care, patient education, and shared decision-making.
items.citation: Gulen Hatemi, Sofia Ramiro, Yeşim Özgüler et al.. EULAR recommendations for the management of Behçet’s syndrome: 2025 update. Annals of the Rheumatic Diseases. 2026

items.title: A systematic literature review on the effects of exercise on human Toll-like receptor expression
items.summary: This systematic review examined how different forms of exercise affect the expression of Toll-like receptors (TLRs), a family of immune pattern recognition receptors implicated in inflammatory signalling and linked to chronic low-grade inflammation associated with sedentary behaviour and non-communicable diseases. The authors searched multiple databases for studies in which exercise served as an isolated intervention in human subjects, ultimately including several dozen articles spanning acute and chronic resistance, aerobic, and combined exercise modalities. Acute resistance exercise tended to upregulate TLR expression, whereas acute aerobic exercise more often produced neutral or downregulatory effects, particularly in healthy individuals. Chronic resistance and combined training programs predominantly left TLR levels unchanged or reduced them, while chronic aerobic training yielded mixed results with most measurements showing no significant change. The authors conclude that exercise does interact with TLR signalling in a modality- and duration-dependent manner, but substantial heterogeneity across study designs limits firm conclusions and underscores the need for more standardised research to clarify the underlying mechanisms and clinical implications.
items.citation: Kasper Favere, Matthias Bosman, Peter Delputte et al.. A systematic literature review on the effects of exercise on human Toll-like receptor expression. PubMed. 2026

items.title: A Similarity Theorem and Its Breakdown in Atomic Black Hole Accretion
items.summary: This paper investigates the mathematical symmetry properties of accreting atomic gas onto a central point mass, such as a black hole, and determines where that symmetry breaks down during rapid growth. The authors prove that a specific rescaling of black hole mass and ambient gas density constitutes an exact similarity transformation that preserves all dimensionless physical quantities—including optical depths, Eddington ratios, and variability—across a broad class of physically motivated radiation and feedback laws, and demonstrate this rescaling is unique within that class. They introduce a dimensionless parameter characterizing the fractional mass gained per Bondi time, showing it equals the expansion speed of the Bondi radius in units of the ambient sound speed, so that a value of unity corresponds to sonic dilation of the accretion radius. For power-law mass retention rates, this sonic threshold is reached after a finite mass increase, and the available remaining time within the similarity regime is strictly bounded; canonical hyper-Eddington accretion scenarios are found to have already crossed this boundary. The authors conclude that the similarity theorem unifies previously separate radiating Bondi and feedback-regulated scaling relations while identifying the precise conditions under which a fixed-mass quasi-steady approximation loses validity.
items.citation: Marcus DuPont. A Similarity Theorem and Its Breakdown in Atomic Black Hole Accretion. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Renormalization-guided inverse blocking for lattice field generation: construction and validation
items.summary: This paper proposes and validates a new algorithm for generating lattice field configurations by approximately inverting a renormalization-group blocking transformation. The method optimizes a blocking transformation under a "perfect blocking" condition so that the coarse-grained lattice distribution is well described by a simple action, then separates the blocking into an invertible smoothing step followed by decimation, with a conditional normalizing flow used to reconstruct the short-distance degrees of freedom lost in decimation. A brief rethermalization step corrects residual mismatches, and because the coarse ensemble provides the long-distance modes, the same learned transformation can be applied recursively to generate configurations on successively larger lattices from a single small-volume ensemble. The method is tested in two-dimensional scalar field theory at criticality, demonstrating stable cascade upscaling across several orders of magnitude in lattice volume using only local computational resources. Rethermalization tests confirm that short-distance mismatches relax quickly while mismatches in the relevant thermal direction relax slowly, and the authors argue the approach naturally extends to higher-dimensional, gauge, and fermionic systems.
items.citation: Anna Hasenfratz, Ethan T. Neil, Letizia Parato et al.. Renormalization-guided inverse blocking for lattice field generation: construction and validation. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Exact quantification of nonlocal magic
items.summary: This paper addresses the question of how much quantum "magic" (nonstabilizerness, the resource enabling universal quantum computation beyond Clifford circuits) is genuinely nonlocal—residing in correlations between parties rather than in their individual local descriptions. The authors solve the previously open optimization problem of minimizing over local bases for the stabilizer fidelity, proving that the nonlocal magic of any pure multiqubit state is determined by the distance of its entanglement spectrum from the closest spectrum of Bell pairs. They also establish an unexpected connection to entanglement embezzlement: a family of states can universally embezzle entanglement under local operations and classical communication if and only if its nonlocal magic diverges. Crucially, the relevant property is not the total amount of entanglement but how the entanglement spectrum distributes weight across factor-of-two windows of rank, which explains why critical chains and random-singlet states—despite sharing the same logarithmic entanglement scaling—carry unbounded and vanishing nonlocal magic, respectively. The results make nonlocal magic an operationally meaningful characteristic of quantum correlations that is accessible through tensor-network methods and entanglement spectroscopy experiments.
items.citation: Piotr Sierant. Exact quantification of nonlocal magic. arXiv. 2026

items.title: QUEST: A Query and Extraction System for Topics in Asylum Law Application Decisions
items.summary: The paper investigates how to automatically identify and extract information related to credibility assessments within asylum application appeal decisions, which are lengthy and complex legal documents. The researchers developed QUEST, a system that combines synthetic query generation, topic extraction, and relevance assessment to frame this identification problem as an information retrieval task, applied to two datasets of Danish asylum appeals. Beyond standard retrieval evaluation metrics, they introduced a novel domain-specific evaluation framework based on credibility-relevant factors rather than traditional notions of document relevance. Their findings reveal that performance estimation becomes substantially more challenging when using credibility-based relevance assessments compared to conventional metrics, highlighting the inherent difficulty of this specialized legal information retrieval task.
items.citation: Maria Vlachou, Anna Murphy Høgenhaug, Mohammad N. S. Jahromi et al.. QUEST: A Query and Extraction System for Topics in Asylum Law Application Decisions. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Offline-Verifiable Accountability for Cross-Organization Agent Messaging: A Preserved Evidence-Bundle Approach
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of verifying accountability in cross-organization agent workflows when live systems are unavailable, untrusted, or controlled by a single party. The authors propose a preserved evidence-bundle model in which each workflow event carries policy-required cryptographic evidence, including sender authentication, log commitments, witness-backed checkpoints, delegation authorization, and receiver-signed receipts. A policy-controlled offline verifier then assesses whether a given bundle satisfies the chosen evidence policy without inferring delivery or receipt from transport behavior alone. Evaluation using a prototype over hundreds of complete workflows and preserved bundles showed that all corrupted or policy-insufficient bundles were correctly rejected with no false acceptances, while latency measurements revealed that checkpoint-context anchoring was the costliest verification step. The work claims to provide an auditable, dispute-ready foundation for cross-organization agent messaging that does not depend on live infrastructure or platform-specific logging.
items.citation: Adil Alshammari, Hayretdin Bahsi. Offline-Verifiable Accountability for Cross-Organization Agent Messaging: A Preserved Evidence-Bundle Approach. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Analysis of Polynomial Threshold Functions on Random Regular Graphs: Computational Complexity of Detecting Noisy Random Lift
items.summary: The paper studies the computational difficulty of a hypothesis testing problem: distinguishing a noisy random lift of a base regular graph from a uniformly random regular graph of the same degree. To analyze this problem, the authors develop the first treatment of low-degree polynomial threshold functions in this setting, a standard framework for understanding the limitations of efficient algorithms. A key technical contribution is a new characterization of the distribution of short cycle counts in noisy random lifts up to logarithmic lengths, which extends prior results on cycle statistics in random regular graphs and random lifts to this more general noisy setting. The findings collectively shed light on the computational complexity of the detection problem by establishing regimes where low-degree methods provably fail to distinguish the two distributions.
items.citation: Xifan Yu. Analysis of Polynomial Threshold Functions on Random Regular Graphs: Computational Complexity of Detecting Noisy Random Lift. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Community peer-led STI/HIV point-of-care testing and knowledge, attitude and practice (KAP) survey in men who have sex with men (MSM) attending an NGO-led clinic in the outskirts of Beirut (Lebanon).
items.summary: This pilot study examined the utility of point-of-care testing for HIV, syphilis, and hepatitis among men who have sex with men attending an NGO-led clinic in Beirut, Lebanon, while also evaluating their sexual health knowledge, attitudes, and practices. Using a cross-sectional design over several months, researchers conducted sexual health consultations alongside an anonymous questionnaire covering demographics, STI knowledge, condom use, chemsex, sexual violence, and perceived HIV-related stigma. The cohort was predominantly young, educated Lebanese men, with a notable proportion living with HIV, and findings revealed that high levels of STI and HIV awareness coexisted with condomless sex and recreational drug use. Perceived community stigma emerged as a significant barrier to testing-seeking behavior. The study concludes that integrating point-of-care testing into sexual health services enables same-day diagnosis, counselling, and linkage to care, representing a valuable approach for reaching MSM populations in contexts of high stigma.
items.citation: Abou Shahla W, Rossoni I, Padovese V. Community peer-led STI/HIV point-of-care testing and knowledge, attitude and practice (KAP) survey in men who have sex with men (MSM) attending an NGO-led clinic in the outskirts of Beirut (Lebanon).. Sexually transmitted infections. 2026

items.title: Point-of-care screening for curable sexually transmitted infections in antenatal care in Zimbabwe: a costing study.
items.summary: This study investigated the cost of integrating point-of-care screening for three curable sexually transmitted infections into antenatal care in Harare, Zimbabwe, compared to the standard syndromic management approach. Researchers implemented screening at primary healthcare clinics and collected detailed economic cost data using staff interviews, time-and-motion studies, and other sources, then modelled implementation in a low-volume routine care setting over a twelve-month period. The prevalence of at least one of the three infections was substantial among pregnant women screened. The largest cost drivers were test kits and personnel, which together accounted for the majority of total intervention costs. The findings highlight that while point-of-care antenatal STI screening is feasible, its incremental cost over syndromic management is considerable, underscoring the need for less expensive point-of-care diagnostic tools to make such programmes more affordable for health systems.
items.citation: Martin K, Bath D, Nyamwanza R et al.. Point-of-care screening for curable sexually transmitted infections in antenatal care in Zimbabwe: a costing study.. Sexually transmitted infections. 2026

items.title: Cost-effectiveness of a decentralised molecular point-of-care testing programme for sexually transmitted infections in remote primary care health services in Australia.
items.summary: This study examined whether a decentralised molecular point-of-care testing programme for sexually transmitted infections is cost-effective compared with standard laboratory-based testing in remote Australian First Nations communities, where the burden of chlamydia, gonorrhoea, and trichomonas is disproportionately high. Using a decision analytic model with a government payer perspective and a ten-year time horizon, the researchers modelled costs and health outcomes for young women and men seeking care at remote primary health services. The primary measure was cost per quality-adjusted life year gained, with sensitivity analyses used to assess uncertainty. The point-of-care programme was found to be cost-effective relative to the accepted willingness-to-pay threshold, and was predicted to substantially reduce rates of pelvic inflammatory disease and preterm or low birthweight births among those with infections. The findings support sustained investment in scaled point-of-care testing in remote primary care settings as a means of improving reproductive health outcomes for First Nations communities.
items.citation: Watts CG, Causer LM, Matthews SJ et al.. Cost-effectiveness of a decentralised molecular point-of-care testing programme for sexually transmitted infections in remote primary care health services in Australia.. Sexually transmitted infections. 2026

items.title: Mechanisms, management and prevention of anorectal sexually transmitted infections.
items.summary: This review examines the epidemiology, pathogenic mechanisms, diagnosis, and prevention of anorectal bacterial sexually transmitted infections, focusing primarily on chlamydia, gonorrhoea, and syphilis. The authors synthesize current understanding of why these infections are frequently asymptomatic, attributing this to bacterial adaptation to rectal tissue and attenuated local immune responses that do not reach symptom thresholds, a phenomenon particularly pronounced among men who have sex with men where anorectal infections often exceed urogenital prevalence. Molecular diagnostics have substantially improved detection, yet challenges remain in distinguishing viable from non-viable organisms, expanding point-of-care testing, and balancing screening with antimicrobial stewardship, especially as gonorrhoea continues to develop antimicrobial resistance. The review highlights doxycycline post-exposure prophylaxis and artificial intelligence applications as promising emerging prevention strategies, while noting that real-world implementation across diverse clinical settings remains limited. The authors identify key knowledge gaps and propose research priorities to strengthen control of these infections globally.
items.citation: Latt PM, Kong FYS, Khosropour CM et al.. Mechanisms, management and prevention of anorectal sexually transmitted infections.. Nature reviews. Gastroenterology & hepatology. 2026

items.title: Cost-Effectiveness of Testing and Screening Strategies for Trichomoniasis among Asymptomatic and Symptomatic Women in U.S. Outpatient Clinical Settings.
items.summary: This study evaluated the cost-effectiveness of various testing and screening strategies for trichomoniasis among both symptomatic and asymptomatic women in U.S. primary care settings. Using a decision tree model applied to a hypothetical cohort of women aged 15–59, researchers examined combinations of wet mount microscopy, rapid antigen testing, and nucleic acid amplification testing, estimating outcomes including quality-adjusted life years and societal economic burden across sequelae such as preterm birth, HIV infection, and cervical cancer. The analysis found that adding nucleic acid amplification testing to wet mount microscopy for symptomatic women improved health outcomes and fell within a commonly accepted cost-effectiveness threshold, whereas adding it to rapid antigen testing for symptomatic women was not cost-effective at that same threshold. Universal nucleic acid amplification testing screening of asymptomatic women was substantially more costly per quality-adjusted life year gained and was not considered cost-effective under standard willingness-to-pay assumptions. The findings suggest that while enhanced testing for symptomatic women can be economically justified, broader screening of asymptomatic populations would require considerably higher willingness-to-pay thresholds to be warranted.
items.venue: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
items.citation: Rong R, Stoecker C, Kissinger PJ et al.. Cost-Effectiveness of Testing and Screening Strategies for Trichomoniasis among Asymptomatic and Symptomatic Women in U.S. Outpatient Clinical Settings.. Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America. 2026

items.title: Compulsive sexual behavior disorder (CSBD) and problematic pornography use (PPU): A comprehensive, interdisciplinary, and expert-informed narrative review with suggested future directions
items.summary: This narrative review examined the current state of scientific and clinical knowledge on Compulsive Sexual Behavior Disorder and Problematic Pornography Use, two widely debated constructs concerning dysregulated sexual behavior. Drawing on contributions from experts across psychology, psychiatry, sexology, addiction science, and neuroscience, the authors synthesized empirical and theoretical literature spanning eleven key thematic areas, including historical context, conceptualization, assessment, epidemiology, co-occurring disorders, etiology, consequences, and treatment. The review also addressed underrepresented groups such as adolescents, women, and LGBTQ+ individuals, as well as the role of cultural factors in shaping these phenomena. The authors identify persistent methodological challenges and classificatory controversies that continue to complicate the field, and they argue that progress depends on greater interdisciplinary collaboration and more rigorous research designs. The work is intended to advance scientific discourse, guide clinical practice, and inform public health policy related to these conditions.
items.citation: Campbell Ince, Stephanie Antons, Sarah Ashton et al.. Compulsive sexual behavior disorder (CSBD) and problematic pornography use (PPU): A comprehensive, interdisciplinary, and expert-informed narrative review with suggested future directions. Journal of Behavioral Addictions. 2026

items.title: An epidemiological approach to sexually transmitted diseases – with special reference to contact tracing and screening
items.summary: This thesis examined epidemiological approaches to controlling sexually transmitted diseases, with particular focus on contact tracing and screening as tools for identifying asymptomatic infected individuals. The research evaluated contact tracing routines, characterized chlamydia-infected populations and their partners, and investigated whether contact tracing data could inform mathematical models of partner choice and disease spread. Key findings included that a gonorrhoea microepidemic was successfully contained through coordinated contact tracing, and that integrating contact tracing into HIV care identified large numbers of previously unknown cases. Chlamydia screening in family planning clinics revealed meaningful prevalence among asymptomatic patients, with infection risk associated with younger age, shorter relationship duration, lack of condom use, and no prior genital infection history, while uptake of testing was lowest in low socioeconomic areas. The study also found that although patients identified through screening differed somewhat from those attending dedicated clinics, the differences were insufficient to warrant distinct partner management strategies, and that partner selection data did not support a purely random mixing model for disease transmission.
items.citation: Kristina Ramstedt. An epidemiological approach to sexually transmitted diseases – with special reference to contact tracing and screening. Acta Dermato Venereologica. 2026

items.title: Multifactorial determinants of health status: insights from the MEDIET4ALL large-scale survey on eco-sociodemographic, psychological, and lifestyle (diet, physical activity, and sleep) factors
items.summary: This large-scale survey study investigated the multifactorial determinants of individual health status, with particular focus on how geo-demographic, socioeconomic, psychological, and lifestyle factors collectively shape outcomes related to non-communicable diseases.
