Researchers administered the MEDIET4ALL e-survey across ten Mediterranean and neighboring countries, recruiting thousands of participants and categorizing their self-reported health as healthy, at-risk, or having known disease, before applying multinomial logistic regression and other statistical models. Body mass index emerged as the strongest negative predictor of health status, with both obesity and underweight substantially elevating the odds of being at risk or having disease, while psychological distress, insomnia, alcohol consumption, and prolonged sitting also worsened outcomes. Conversely, life satisfaction was the strongest protective factor, followed by higher education, better sleep quality, and adherence to the Mediterranean diet and lifestyle, and residing in Mediterranean regions, being female, employed, or in a rural environment was also associated with more favorable health outcomes. The findings underscore the complex interplay among mental health, lifestyle behaviors, and socioeconomic context, and call for multi-level public health interventions addressing physical activity, healthy eating, psychological well-being, and equitable healthcare access.
items.citation: Achraf Ammar, Atef Salem, Mohamed Ali Boujelbane et al.. Multifactorial determinants of health status: insights from the MEDIET4ALL large-scale survey on eco-sociodemographic, psychological, and lifestyle (diet, physical activity, and sleep) factors. Frontiers in Public Health. 2026

items.title: A Novel Index Measure of Housing-Related Risk as a Predictor of Overdose Among Young People Who Inject Drugs and Injection Networks
items.summary: This study examined the relationship between housing instability and overdose risk among young people who inject drugs, addressing limitations of prior research that typically reduced housing instability to a single dimension. Using baseline data from a network-based longitudinal study of young people who inject drugs and their social networks in metropolitan Chicago, the researchers constructed a multi-dimensional housing instability risk index composed of five dichotomous variables and analyzed its association with lifetime overdose count via negative binomial regression. After adjusting for multiple covariates, a significant positive association was found between the housing instability risk score and lifetime overdose count. The findings support the value of a holistic, multi-dimensional approach to measuring housing instability, suggesting that such an index better captures overdose risk than single-dimension measures and should inform the design of interventions targeting this vulnerable population.
items.citation: Kathleen Kristensen, Leslie D. Williams, Charlie Kaplan et al.. A Novel Index Measure of Housing-Related Risk as a Predictor of Overdose Among Young People Who Inject Drugs and Injection Networks. Journal of Urban Health. 2026

items.title: Ultrasensitive Enzyme-Free Detection of Proteins on Magnetic Beads
items.summary: This paper studied the development of an enzyme-free platform for ultrasensitive protein detection on magnetic beads, aimed at making advanced diagnostic assays more accessible in resource-limited settings. The researchers created a system called efMOSAIC, which uses hybridization chain reaction-based signal amplifiers instead of enzymes to achieve digital protein quantification with simple workflows. The platform achieved detection limits comparable to established single-molecule detection technologies such as Simoa, while the reagents remained stable when stored at room temperature for up to six months. The team validated efMOSAIC for detecting cytokines from human plasma and demonstrated its capability for multiplexed biomarker detection. By eliminating the need for enzymes, specialized instrumentation, and cold-chain supply logistics, the authors argue this approach could expand access to ultrasensitive protein diagnostics in low- and middle-income countries and point-of-care settings.
items.venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society
items.citation: Karan Malhotra, Louise L. Hansen, Samuel Han et al.. Ultrasensitive Enzyme-Free Detection of Proteins on Magnetic Beads. Journal of the American Chemical Society. 2026

items.title: Malaria in the 21st Century: Global Disease Burden, Epidemiological Insights, and Strategic Control Approaches
items.summary: This review paper examines the current global burden of malaria, synthesizing epidemiological data and evidence on the disease's distribution, determinants, and control strategies in the twenty-first century. The authors drew primarily on the World Health Organization's World Malaria Report and Global Burden of Disease estimates to characterize regional trends and identify key drivers of ongoing transmission, including socio-economic factors and emerging challenges such as drug resistance, climate change, and funding constraints. The paper covers the full spectrum of malaria transmission routes — including vector-borne, transfusion-related, transplant-related, and congenital pathways — and evaluates intervention approaches across primary, secondary, and tertiary prevention. The authors argue that effective disease control requires multifactorial, locally adapted strategies and that strengthening health education with contextually relevant knowledge is essential to improving outcomes. The review concludes by outlining policy priorities necessary to advance toward the WHO's goal of malaria elimination by the year two thousand and thirty.
items.citation: Basmah F. Alharbi, Mawahib A. Ahmed. Malaria in the 21st Century: Global Disease Burden, Epidemiological Insights, and Strategic Control Approaches. Biology. 2026

items.title: Understanding Venture Capital Syndication in Information Technology Sectors: A Network Formation Perspective
items.summary: This paper investigates how venture capital co-investment relationships form and evolve within U.S. information technology sectors, focusing on the structural mechanisms that drive syndication network development. Using comprehensive dyadic panel data spanning several decades across hardware, software, and hybrid subsectors, the researchers tested multiple relational mechanisms—including prior collaboration, shared partners, geographic proximity, and organizational similarity—using dyadic logit models and exponential random graph modeling. Prior collaboration emerged as the most consistent predictor of new co-investment links across all subsectors, with shared partners, geographic proximity, and organizational-type similarity also positively associated with link formation, while the influence of domain overlap, prominence, and experience varied by subsector. A whole-network model of the software sector confirmed that triadic closure and geographic homophily reinforce network structure, alongside a weaker effect of investor-type homophily. Together, the findings demonstrate that IT venture syndication networks are jointly shaped by relational persistence, network closure, and homophily rather than any single mechanism.
items.citation: Liheng Tan, Zhengkai Tu, Prasanna Karhade. Understanding Venture Capital Syndication in Information Technology Sectors: A Network Formation Perspective. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Distinct Modes of Pulsar Glitch Activity Revealed by the Waiting-Time--Amplitude Morphology
items.summary: This paper investigated the diversity of pulsar glitch behavior by developing an objective, quantitative classification scheme to replace the traditional qualitative "Vela-like" and "Crab-like" labels. The authors compiled a sample of glitches from dozens of pulsars by cross-matching two major glitch databases, then characterized each pulsar's glitch activity using the joint distribution of backward waiting time and fractional glitch amplitude, analyzed through two-dimensional kernel density estimation and highest-density region descriptors. Hierarchical clustering of these geometric descriptors revealed two distinct morphological classes—a Compact class characterized by small, anisotropic distributions consistent with near-complete superfluid reservoir depletion, and an Extended class with broader, more diffuse distributions suggestive of partial, avalanche-like angular momentum releases—with most sources clustering robustly into one group, though two prolific pulsars occupied intermediate positions. Logistic regression identified mean backward waiting time as the strongest predictor distinguishing the two classes, and a parallel analysis using forward waiting times recovered the same two-class structure with somewhat less stability. The authors conclude that this morphological distinction has physical implications, particularly that short-term glitch activity measurements in Extended-class pulsars likely underestimate the true fraction of crustal superfluid involved in glitching.
items.citation: Wen-Tong Liu, Wei-hua Wang, Xia Zhou et al.. Distinct Modes of Pulsar Glitch Activity Revealed by the Waiting-Time--Amplitude Morphology. arXiv. 2026

items.title: CRISPR-Cas12a assay for rapid and specific detection of <i>Shigella flexneri 2a</i> in clinical samples.
items.summary: The paper studied the development and validation of a rapid diagnostic assay for *Shigella flexneri 2a*, the most prevalent serotype causing shigellosis and a significant public health burden in developing countries. The researchers designed a CRISPR-Cas12a-based detection system using two guide RNAs targeting serotype-specific genes, coupled with recombinase polymerase amplification to enable isothermal signal amplification readable by either fluorescence or lateral flow. The assay was analytically and clinically validated against conventional PCR using both purified DNA and a large cohort of clinical stool specimens. The assay achieved a detection limit of ten copies per microliter with complete analytical specificity and no cross-reactivity, while clinical testing demonstrated diagnostic sensitivity and specificity comparable to PCR. The authors conclude that the assay's speed, simplicity, and dual readout options make it a practical tool for point-of-care diagnostics and field-based surveillance in resource-limited settings.
items.citation: Liao J, Su Y, Jiang F. CRISPR-Cas12a assay for rapid and specific detection of <i>Shigella flexneri 2a</i> in clinical samples.. Journal of clinical microbiology. 2026

items.title: An integrated centrifugal microfluidic CRISPR-based diagnostics platform for multiplexed point-of-care testing of respiratory pathogens.
items.summary: The paper developed and validated an integrated microfluidic diagnostic platform called iCARD for rapid, multiplexed detection of respiratory pathogens at the point of care. The system combines centrifugal microfluidics with CRISPR/Cas13a chemistry on a rotating disc pre-loaded with lyophilized reagents, paired with a portable fluorescence analyzer, and uses a novel resin-based method to purify and concentrate nucleic acids directly from throat swabs. The platform enables simultaneous screening of multiple pathogens across several independent samples in a single automated workflow within approximately forty minutes. Analytical testing confirmed single-copy-level sensitivity with no cross-reactivity, and clinical validation against retrospective patient samples demonstrated very high diagnostic sensitivity and perfect specificity. The authors conclude that iCARD represents a robust, accurate, and accessible tool suitable for decentralized molecular diagnostics and epidemiological surveillance.
items.citation: Li L, Wei H, Wei M et al.. An integrated centrifugal microfluidic CRISPR-based diagnostics platform for multiplexed point-of-care testing of respiratory pathogens.. Biosensors & bioelectronics. 2026

items.title: CRISPR RNA Engineering Enables Single Nucleotide Polymorphism Discrimination in Nucleic Acid Detection.
items.summary: This review examines how CRISPR-based diagnostic platforms can be engineered to achieve single nucleotide polymorphism discrimination in nucleic acid detection, addressing the persistent problem of off-target activation that limits clinical reliability. The authors synthesize advances in CRISPR RNA engineering strategies, detailing how structural features such as spacer length, intentional mismatch design, secondary-structure modulation, chemical modification, and strand-displacement gating collectively govern target recognition and cleavage specificity. Computational prediction, high-throughput screening, and hybrid guide architectures are systematically evaluated for their ability to enhance single-nucleotide discrimination, stabilize reaction performance, and enable multiplexed detection for pathogen profiling and mutation identification. The review identifies remaining obstacles including interference from complex clinical matrices, absence of unified evaluation standards, and scalability barriers that impede translation to clinical settings. The authors conclude that integrated crRNA design combined with system-level optimization and standardized benchmarking will be necessary to fulfill the potential of CRISPR diagnostics for ultrasensitive point-of-care testing and precision medicine applications.
items.citation: Sun T, Yuan A, Xie W et al.. CRISPR RNA Engineering Enables Single Nucleotide Polymorphism Discrimination in Nucleic Acid Detection.. Angewandte Chemie (International ed. in English). 2026

items.title: SARS-CoV-2 Point-of-Care Testing Modalities: Integrating Molecular, Immunological, Biosensor, and AI Approaches.
items.summary: This review examined the landscape of point-of-care testing technologies developed for SARS-CoV-2 diagnosis, motivated by the urgent diagnostic demands exposed by the COVID-19 pandemic. The authors conducted a structured literature search across major scientific databases and evaluated multiple testing modalities, including molecular assays such as rapid RT-PCR, LAMP, and CRISPR-based methods, alongside antigen and antibody tests, biosensor platforms, and artificial intelligence-assisted diagnostic approaches. Molecular methods were found to offer high sensitivity and specificity suitable for decentralized use, while antigen tests provide rapid and affordable screening albeit with performance that varies by viral load, symptom timing, and circulating variants. Antibody-based testing proved most useful for retrospective diagnosis and seroprevalence monitoring rather than acute infection detection, and emerging biosensor and AI technologies showed analytical promise but largely remain at prototype or early-validation stages requiring further clinical evidence. The review concludes that no single modality is universally optimal, and that combining complementary approaches alongside advances in multiplex testing, digital connectivity, and variant-resilient detection will strengthen both COVID-19 management and future infectious disease preparedness.
items.citation: Hetta HF, Ahmed R, Haseeb A et al.. SARS-CoV-2 Point-of-Care Testing Modalities: Integrating Molecular, Immunological, Biosensor, and AI Approaches.. Diagnostics (Basel, Switzerland). 2026

items.title: CRISPR-Cas and Infectious Diseases: A Decade of Translational Advances in Molecular Biotechnology.
items.summary: This review examines a decade of translational progress in applying CRISPR-Cas systems to infectious disease diagnostics, therapeutics, and vaccine development. The authors surveyed key platforms and research directions, including rapid pathogen detection tools, CRISPR-based strategies for targeting viral genomes and antimicrobial resistance, and the engineering of live-attenuated and personalized neoantigen vaccines. Their synthesis reveals an uneven maturity across these domains: diagnostic platforms have advanced furthest toward clinical evaluation, live-attenuated vaccine engineering has reached preclinical stages, while therapeutic genome editing and personalized neoantigen vaccines remain largely exploratory. Delivery inefficiency, off-target effects, and regulatory and ethical uncertainties are identified as the principal barriers slowing clinical translation across all application areas. The review concludes that realizing the transformative potential of CRISPR-Cas in infectious disease management will require coordinated technical innovation alongside clear ethical and regulatory frameworks to ensure safe and equitable deployment.
items.citation: Mayuri K, Saravanan KM, Somala CS et al.. CRISPR-Cas and Infectious Diseases: A Decade of Translational Advances in Molecular Biotechnology.. Biochemical genetics. 2026

items.title: PCR and molecular diagnostics: Biotechnologic integration in clinical laboratories.
items.summary: This review paper examines the evolution and clinical integration of polymerase chain reaction technology and related molecular diagnostic tools in laboratory medicine. The authors survey the development of PCR from conventional amplification methods to advanced platforms including quantitative, digital, reverse transcription, and multiplex variants, assessing how each contributes to nucleic acid detection, quantification, and high-throughput analysis. The paper further explores how PCR can be combined with next-generation sequencing, CRISPR-based diagnostics, microarrays, and epigenetic profiling to broaden the characterization of disease states, with particular attention to oncologically relevant biomarkers such as circulating tumor DNA and key mutation targets used in precision oncology. Applications extending to infectious disease diagnosis, antimicrobial resistance surveillance, heritable disorder detection, and minimal residual disease monitoring are also covered, alongside emerging trends in multi-omics data integration and artificial intelligence-assisted analysis. The authors conclude that while challenges related to cost, standardization, technical expertise, and data management persist, continued technological advances are progressively expanding clinician and patient access to these powerful diagnostic capabilities.
items.venue: Clinica chimica acta; international journal of clinical chemistry
items.citation: Saleem MA, Riaz T, Saleem F et al.. PCR and molecular diagnostics: Biotechnologic integration in clinical laboratories.. Clinica chimica acta; international journal of clinical chemistry. 2026

items.title: Biosensing technologies for foodborne pathogen detection and healthcare: principles, emerging materials, and intelligent platforms
items.summary: This review examines the current state and future directions of biosensing technologies designed to detect high-priority foodborne pathogens, including Escherichia coli, Salmonella, and Listeria monocytogenes, which continue to threaten global public health. The authors survey electrochemical, optical, and microfluidic sensing platforms, analyzing how advances in functional nanomaterials, aptamers, nanozymes, and surface engineering strategies have improved sensor sensitivity, specificity, and performance in complex food matrices. A central theme is the integration of artificial intelligence and machine learning into these biosensing systems, enabling intelligent pattern recognition, real-time analytics, and high-throughput multiplexed detection that transform conventional sensors into smart diagnostic devices. The review critically identifies persistent challenges such as matrix interference, bioreceptor instability, manufacturing scalability, and regulatory standardization, while proposing mitigation strategies including ratiometric sensing, microfluidic pre-treatment, explainable AI, and printable electronics. Looking forward, the authors advocate for self-powered biosensors, modular pathogen detection panels, blockchain-enabled data integrity, and standardized validation pipelines as pathways toward regulation-ready platforms for next-generation food safety monitoring.
items.citation: Purshottam J. Assudani, Balakrishnan . P., Anny Leema A et al.. Biosensing technologies for foodborne pathogen detection and healthcare: principles, emerging materials, and intelligent platforms. Microchimica Acta. 2026

items.title: New approach methodologies for drug discovery
items.summary: This review examines the emerging field of new approach methodologies as alternatives to traditional animal-based drug discovery, which has historically suffered from high failure rates. The authors survey recent advances in stem cell-based systems, organoid models, and computational approaches, considering how these tools apply across the full drug-discovery continuum from disease modeling through efficacy testing. The review also discusses the evolving regulatory frameworks from major health agencies that are shaping the adoption of these methods. Key biological, technical, and regulatory bottlenecks limiting broader translational uptake are identified and analyzed. The authors conclude by outlining future human-centric discovery pipelines and the societal considerations necessary for the responsible integration of these methodologies into mainstream drug development.
items.citation: Wenqiang Liu, Paul Pang, Catherine A. Wu et al.. New approach methodologies for drug discovery. Cell. 2026

items.title: Nanoparticles-based phototherapy systems: molecular mechanisms and clinical applications
items.summary: This review examines nanoparticle-based phototherapy systems, focusing on how integrating nanoparticles with light-activated treatment modalities enhances therapeutic precision across a range of diseases. The authors survey the core components, classification schemes, and delivery platforms—including gold nanoparticles, liposomes, and dendrimers—that underpin photodynamic and photothermal therapies, highlighting their roles in improving light absorption, targeting, reactive oxygen species generation, and localized heating. At the molecular level, the review dissects how light-triggered interventions induce oxidative stress, activate apoptotic and autophagic cascades, and modulate immune responses through cytokine profiles and T-cell activity, with relevance not only to cancer but also to cardiovascular, neurodegenerative, metabolic, and autoimmune conditions. The authors critically evaluate regulatory-approved agents and recent clinical trial findings, addressing translational challenges such as nanoparticle optimization, effective light delivery, and regulatory barriers. Overall, the review positions nanoparticle-based phototherapy as a transformative, noninvasive strategy with broad therapeutic potential across chronic and complex diseases.
items.citation: Deepak S. Chauhan, Rajendra Prasad, Mukesh Dhanka et al.. Nanoparticles-based phototherapy systems: molecular mechanisms and clinical applications. Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy. 2026

items.title: Cell death in cancer
items.summary: This review paper examines the diverse programs of cell death and their roles in cancer development, progression, treatment response, and resistance. The authors synthesize knowledge spanning apoptosis and more recently characterized modalities including necroptosis, pyroptosis, and ferroptosis, presenting a unified conceptual framework for how these processes operate in malignancy. While apoptosis remains central to the cell-killing effects of conventional therapies such as radiation and chemotherapy, the review highlights that non-apoptotic programs can drive inflammation and shape interactions among tumor cells, stromal components, and the immune system, thereby influencing immunotherapy outcomes. Ferroptosis receives particular attention as a distinct modality driven by iron-dependent lipid peroxidation that arises from metabolic perturbations rather than a canonical induction signal. The authors argue that fully understanding these cell death programs is essential for overcoming evasion of cell death, a recognized hallmark of cancer, and for revealing new therapeutic opportunities.
items.citation: Marcus Conrad, Andreas Strasser, Philipp J. Jost et al.. Cell death in cancer. Cell. 2026

items.title: Comprehensive Review on Candidemia: Epidemiology, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Future Directions
items.summary: This review examines candidemia, a serious nosocomial bloodstream infection caused by *Candida* species, focusing on the challenges that make it difficult to manage effectively in clinical settings. The authors synthesize current knowledge on the epidemiology, species distribution, and origins of candidemia, alongside a critical appraisal of conventional diagnostic methods and their limitations in achieving timely detection. The review evaluates emerging diagnostic technologies, susceptibility-guided antifungal therapy, and therapeutic strategies encompassing empiric and targeted regimens, management of mixed infections, and host-drug interactions. Particular attention is given to antifungal resistance, the potential of combination therapy, and novel agents in development that target previously unexploited fungal pathways. The authors also explore future directions including the application of artificial intelligence in diagnostics, vaccine-based prophylaxis, and synergistic treatment approaches, with the overarching aim of guiding clinicians and researchers in addressing the evolving complexities of candidemia management.
items.citation: Haojie Dong, Minghui Song, Jingfang Sun et al.. Comprehensive Review on Candidemia: Epidemiology, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Future Directions. iFungi. 2026

items.title: Multi-omics and artificial intelligence for precision drug discovery and potential clinical applications
items.summary: This review examines how the integration of multiomics technologies and artificial intelligence is reshaping precision drug discovery and translational medicine. The authors synthesize how approaches spanning genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, and metabolomics generate deep molecular insights into disease mechanisms, while advanced deep learning architectures are applied to interpret these complex biological datasets and build predictive models. The review covers the application of this combined framework across the drug development pipeline, including target identification, drug repositioning, de novo compound design, virtual screening, pharmacokinetic modeling, and safety assessment. Case examples drawn from oncology, neurodegenerative diseases, and cardiovascular conditions are used to illustrate the practical potential of these technologies. The authors also acknowledge persistent challenges such as harmonizing disparate omics data streams, ensuring reproducibility, and addressing algorithmic biases, while arguing that the convergence of multiomics and artificial intelligence represents a new era in bench-to-clinic therapeutic development.
items.citation: Yuqing Liu, Kun Zhu, Weijun Peng et al.. Multi-omics and artificial intelligence for precision drug discovery and potential clinical applications. Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy. 2026

items.title: QGPINNs: A Physics-Informed Neural Network Framework for Nonlocal Differential Equations on Quantum Graphs
items.summary: This paper introduces QGPINNs, a physics-informed neural network framework built in PyTorch for solving nonlocal differential equations defined on quantum graphs, which are networks of edges and vertices governed by differential equations coupled through transmission conditions. The framework assigns a separate neural network to each edge of the graph and enforces governing equations alongside boundary, initial, and vertex conditions through a unified graph-based loss function, thereby constructing a globally consistent solution. It targets two classes of nonlinear fractional problems—multi-order fractional elliptic equations and time-fractional evolution equations—and incorporates specialized learning strategies such as dynamic loss balancing, Fourier feature embeddings, and a learnable feature designed to capture the weakly singular behavior typical of fractional-order solutions. The framework is also extended to inverse problems, enabling identification of fractional operator orders and physical parameters from noisy data. Validation on benchmark graph structures and real-world networks, including an electrical power system and an agricultural drainage network, demonstrates the accuracy, computational efficiency, and physical consistency of the approach.
items.citation: Vaibhav Mehandiratta, Saket Ramchandra. QGPINNs: A Physics-Informed Neural Network Framework for Nonlocal Differential Equations on Quantum Graphs. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Interaction corrections to topological density three-point functions in two-dimensional Fermi liquids: a coadjoint orbit perspective
items.summary: This paper investigates how electron-electron interactions modify density three-point correlation functions in two-dimensional Fermi liquids, focusing on whether these correlations retain their ability to probe the topology of the Fermi sea in the presence of interactions. The authors employ a coadjoint-orbit effective field theory framework, which recasts fermionic loop diagrams as tree-level diagrams in a bosonized language and provides a systematic treatment of generalized Landau interactions. They find that even at linear order in the generalized Landau interaction parameter, a contribution proportional to the band curvature at the Fermi momentum emerges that alters the nonanalytic structure of the free density three-point function. This interaction-induced nonanalytic term is distinct from those appearing in either the noninteracting case or in an interacting Galilean-invariant system, demonstrating that interaction effects can qualitatively change the topology-detecting character of the density three-point correlator.
items.citation: Akshay Pal, Andrew Lucas, Umang Mehta. Interaction corrections to topological density three-point functions in two-dimensional Fermi liquids: a coadjoint orbit perspective. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Continuity equation on metric spaces via measure-valued derivations and BV-Wasserstein curves
items.summary: This paper develops a theory of continuity equations on general metric spaces capable of handling curves of probability measures that are of bounded variation with respect to the 1-Wasserstein distance, going beyond the classical absolutely continuous setting. The central innovation is a notion of measure-valued derivations, whose foundational theory is established here, serving as the analytic object that replaces the classical velocity field in the continuity equation. The authors characterize bounded variation curves in the space of probability measures with the extended 1-Wasserstein distance precisely as those satisfying the continuity equation driven by a measure-valued derivation of finite mass, extending earlier work on probabilistic representations of such curves. On Euclidean space, the framework is shown to be consistent with a recently introduced continuity equation for singular fluxes, including its notion of minimal solutions, while on general geodesic metric spaces the probabilistic representations are used to construct the required measure-valued derivations and flux measures explicitly.
items.citation: Ehsan Abedi, Zhenhao Li, Timo Schultz. Continuity equation on metric spaces via measure-valued derivations and BV-Wasserstein curves. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Renormalization-guided cascade upscaling for lattice field generation
items.summary: This paper introduces a machine-learning algorithm for generating lattice field configurations that is guided by the renormalization group. The approach combines a "perfect blocking" construction to supply equilibrated long-distance modes with a conditional normalizing flow that reconstructs short-distance details, followed by brief rethermalization to remove residual errors. By inverting a renormalization group transformation approximately, the method enables recursive cascade upscaling of lattice sizes. Applied to two-dimensional scalar field theory at criticality, a normalizing flow trained only on small lattices can be reused recursively to generate configurations on much larger lattices while preserving correct long-distance physics.
items.citation: Anna Hasenfratz, Ethan T. Neil, Letizia Parato et al.. Renormalization-guided cascade upscaling for lattice field generation. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Renormalization-guided inverse blocking for lattice field generation: construction and validation
items.summary: This paper proposes and validates a new algorithm for generating lattice field configurations by approximately inverting a renormalization-group blocking transformation. The method optimizes a blocking transformation under a "perfect blocking" condition so that the coarse-grained distribution is well described by a simple action, then uses a conditional normalizing flow to reconstruct the short-distance degrees of freedom lost during decimation, followed by a brief rethermalization step to correct residual mismatches. A key feature is that the same blocking transformation and learned flow can be applied recursively, enabling a cascade that upscales configurations from a small initial lattice to much larger volumes without retraining. The approach is tested in two-dimensional scalar field theory at criticality, demonstrating stable upscaling across several orders of magnitude in lattice size on modest computational hardware. Rethermalization tests confirm that short-distance mismatches relax quickly while long-distance (relevant-direction) mismatches relax slowly, and the authors argue the framework naturally extends toward higher-dimensional, gauge, and fermionic theories.
items.citation: Anna Hasenfratz, Ethan T. Neil, Letizia Parato et al.. Renormalization-guided inverse blocking for lattice field generation: construction and validation. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Modular Functors with Singularities from Vertex Operator Algebras Beyond Rigidity and Finiteness
items.summary: This paper proposes a construction of conformal blocks organized into an open-closed modular functor with singularities, starting from a vertex operator algebra and a suitable category of its modules. The approach implements the principle of holomorphic factorization directly, using the strategy of modular extension to build mapping class group representations for surfaces with boundary components carrying specified boundary labels. A key advantage of this construction is that it operates beyond the usual assumptions of rationality, rigidity, self-contragredience, and finiteness that constrain other approaches. The authors show that when the module category is a not necessarily semisimple modular category, their spaces recover string-net spaces and the modular functor for the Drinfeld center, and they prove properties including excision, finite-dimensionality in the cofinite case, and generalizations of surface braid group representations. As a concrete application, they demonstrate that boundary conditions introduced in prior work on the triplet algebra produce well-defined correlation functions within the framework of modular functors with singularities they develop.
items.citation: Lukas Müller, Lukas Woike. Modular Functors with Singularities from Vertex Operator Algebras Beyond Rigidity and Finiteness. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Ultrabright PCNs@Coumarin 6-Enhanced Wireless Lateral Flow Immunoassay Platform for Ultrasensitive Detection of Porphyromonas gingivalis.
items.summary: This study developed an ultrasensitive wireless lateral flow immunoassay platform for detecting *Porphyromonas gingivalis*, a key bacterial pathogen linked to periodontal and systemic diseases, addressing limitations of traditional detection methods such as poor sensitivity and procedural complexity. The platform integrated a novel fluorescent metal-organic framework nanocomposite with substantially enhanced fluorescence intensity and prolonged lifetime, combined with a quadruped DNA walker system that amplifies fluorescence signals through enzyme-dependent activity. A self-developed wireless analyzer enabled rapid and accurate interpretation of lateral flow test strips across a wide bacterial concentration range, achieving an exceptionally low detection limit. Validation with clinical saliva samples demonstrated high accuracy and strong resistance to interference, while remaining less costly and more operationally convenient than polymerase chain reaction. The authors conclude that this platform is well-suited for point-of-care testing scenarios including chair-side diagnostics, home self-testing, and large-scale community screening.
items.citation: Zhou M, Shen H, Long Z et al.. Ultrabright PCNs@Coumarin 6-Enhanced Wireless Lateral Flow Immunoassay Platform for Ultrasensitive Detection of Porphyromonas gingivalis.. ACS applied materials & interfaces. 2026

items.title: Noninvasive SARS-CoV-2 detection using a low-cost electronic nose.
items.summary: This study investigated whether a low-cost, metal-oxide-sensor-based electronic nose could noninvasively detect SARS-CoV-2 infection by analyzing volatile organic compounds in saliva and exhaled breath. The device used an array of commercially available gas sensors paired with several machine learning classification algorithms, including K-Nearest Neighbors, Support Vector Machine, Neural Networks, and Random Forest, to distinguish between infected and non-infected individuals in a real-world hospital cohort. Detection accuracy varied across algorithms and sample types, with exhaled breath generally outperforming saliva, and the K-Nearest Neighbors algorithm achieving the best overall discrimination for both sample types. The findings demonstrate proof-of-concept feasibility for a rapid, point-of-care diagnostic tool that avoids the discomfort and delays associated with conventional testing methods.
items.venue: The Brazilian journal of infectious diseases : an official publication of the Brazilian Society of Infectious Diseases
items.citation: Fialkovitz G, Sousa PL, Hidifira AM et al.. Noninvasive SARS-CoV-2 detection using a low-cost electronic nose.. The Brazilian journal of infectious diseases : an official publication of the Brazilian Society of Infectious Diseases. 2026

items.title: Smart wearable and implantable biosensors for continuous health monitoring: materials, biocompatibility, and AI integration
items.summary: This review examines the current state of smart wearable and implantable biosensors designed for continuous, real-time monitoring of biophysical and biochemical signals in the context of personalized and preventive healthcare. The paper surveys advances in flexible, stretchable, and biocompatible materials that enable long-term comfort and seamless integration with the body, as well as multimodal and multi-analyte sensing approaches that improve measurement robustness. The role of artificial intelligence in enhancing signal processing and generating predictive health insights is also assessed. The review identifies persistent challenges including motion artifacts, energy autonomy, data privacy, and the clinical interpretability of sensor outputs. Overall, the paper synthesizes progress across materials science, device architecture, and AI-assisted strategies to outline the trajectory of biosensor development for health monitoring applications.
items.citation: Thirumalaisamy Suryaprabha, Chunghyeon Choi, Yanfang Wu et al.. Smart wearable and implantable biosensors for continuous health monitoring: materials, biocompatibility, and AI integration. npj Flexible Electronics. 2026

items.title: Analytical Performances of Polymer-Based Biosensors for Real Samples Application
items.summary: This review examined how polymer-based biosensors perform analytically when applied to complex real-world samples across food, environmental, and clinical matrices. The authors conducted a meta-trend analysis of nearly a hundred original research articles spanning a decade, evaluating four polymer classes—conductive polymers, redox-mediator polymers, hydrogels, and molecularly imprinted polymers—across electrochemical and other detection formats. Each polymer class showed distinct strengths, with conductive polymers reducing interference at low operating potentials, hydrogels preserving enzyme function in protein-rich environments, and molecularly imprinted polymers offering robust trace detection in harsh conditions despite slow analyte diffusion. A critical finding was widespread validation deficiency, with the vast majority of studies omitting limits of quantification and substantial fractions lacking reproducibility and precision data. The authors conclude that maintaining calibration across diverse hostile matrices remains the central barrier to commercial deployment, while emerging architectures such as nanocapsulation, hierarchical nanocomposites, and microneedle-integrated systems offer promising routes toward improved fouling resistance and operational stability.
items.citation: Marcello Mascini, Sara Palmieri, Fabiola Eugelio et al.. Analytical Performances of Polymer-Based Biosensors for Real Samples Application. Biosensors. 2026

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Applications in Medical Devices for Personalized Health Care Solutions: Systematic Review
items.summary: This systematic review examined the scope and impact of artificial intelligence integration in medical devices, with a focus on enabling personalized and precision health care. The authors analyzed peer-reviewed literature, industry analyses, and regulatory advisories spanning several years to assess current applications, implementation barriers, and strategies for overcoming those barriers. The review found meaningful advances across diagnostics, treatment personalization, wearable health monitoring, and smart prosthetics, with AI-based tools demonstrating high accuracy in disease classification and clinical recognition tasks. Key challenges identified include data security vulnerabilities, algorithmic bias, regulatory constraints, and difficulties integrating AI systems into existing health care infrastructures. The authors conclude that while AI-driven personalization holds considerable promise for more adaptive and patient-centered care, realizing its full potential depends on resolving technical, ethical, and regulatory hurdles, and that emerging technologies such as quantum computing and blockchain-based data management may further strengthen AI performance and security in medical applications.
items.citation: Hemanth Ponnambalath Mohanadas, A Manikandan, Ahmad Fauzi Ismail et al.. Artificial Intelligence Applications in Medical Devices for Personalized Health Care Solutions: Systematic Review. Journal of Medical Internet Research. 2026

items.title: A review of nanofiber-based drug delivery systems: fabrication, characterization, advances, and future prospects
items.summary: This review examines nanofiber-based drug delivery systems, which have gained attention for their large surface area, tunable porosity, and capacity for controlled and sustained drug release. The paper systematically analyzes multiple fabrication approaches, including electrospinning, self-assembly, phase separation, printing methods, and template-assisted techniques, while evaluating the roles of synthetic, natural, and composite polymers in optimizing performance for biomedical use. The review addresses persistent challenges such as scalability, biocompatibility, and in vivo applicability, alongside recent progress in hybrid and biomimetic nanofiber designs. Notable emphasis is placed on emerging strategies that integrate artificial intelligence and three-dimensional bioprinting to enable personalized, patient-specific therapeutic solutions. The authors outline a forward-looking research agenda centered on bioresponsive and smart nanofiber systems, implantable and in situ-forming platforms, and scalable sustainable manufacturing as key steps toward translating nanofiber technology from laboratory settings to clinical practice.
items.citation: A. M. Saleh, Radwa N. Selim, Manar T El-Morsy et al.. A review of nanofiber-based drug delivery systems: fabrication, characterization, advances, and future prospects. Journal of Materials Science Polymers. 2026

items.title: Harmonizing definitions in liquid biopsy: A terminology framework by the international society of liquid biopsy
items.summary: The paper addresses the problem of inconsistent terminology in the rapidly growing field of liquid biopsy, which has hampered clear communication, comparison of results, and clinical translation across research and practice. The International Society of Liquid Biopsy developed a comprehensive, harmonized terminology framework to standardize definitions and concepts used throughout the discipline. The framework establishes a formal definition of liquid biopsy encompassing the analysis of cells, nucleic acids, proteins, metabolites, and extracellular vesicles obtained from bodily fluids via minimally invasive methods. It provides rigorous clarification of analyte-specific terms—including circulating free and tumor-derived DNA and RNA, tumor fraction, variant allele frequency, circulating tumor cells, extracellular vesicles, and metabolomic signatures—as well as the analytical methodologies and clinical applications spanning early detection, molecular residual disease assessment, predictive biomarker evaluation, and tumor monitoring. By establishing this cohesive vocabulary, the framework aims to serve as an evolving reference standard to guide the integration of liquid biopsy into precision oncology.
items.citation: Eloísa Jantus-Lewintre, Silvia Calabuig-Fariñas, David Gandara et al.. Harmonizing definitions in liquid biopsy: A terminology framework by the international society of liquid biopsy. The Journal of Liquid Biopsy. 2026

items.title: Biomaterials in personalized drug delivery: innovations, challenges, and future directions
items.summary: This review examines the role of biomaterials in drug delivery, focusing on how engineered materials can enable personalized and controlled therapeutic applications. The authors survey a broad range of biomaterial classes—including polymers, metals, ceramics, and nanostructured carriers such as liposomes, micelles, and dendrimers—discussing how tunable properties like degradation kinetics, surface chemistry, and mechanical stability allow precise control over drug release and target-site accumulation. Polymer-based systems enable sustained or stimulus-responsive release that can extend therapeutic exposure and reduce dosing frequency relative to conventional formulations, while nanocarriers improve solubility, cellular uptake, and ligand-mediated site-specific targeting. Despite these advances, the review identifies persistent barriers to clinical translation, including immune–biomaterial interactions, manufacturing variability, unpredictable long-term biodegradation, and regulatory compliance challenges. The authors conclude that future progress requires precision fabrication methods, manufacturing-practice-compatible production pipelines, and biologically informed design strategies that accommodate patient-specific variability to realize the promise of personalized drug delivery.
items.citation: Adna Hrapović, Nadia Islam, Asmaa Al Bourghli et al.. Biomaterials in personalized drug delivery: innovations, challenges, and future directions. PeerJ. 2026

items.title: QGPINNs: A Physics-Informed Neural Network Framework for Nonlocal Differential Equations on Quantum Graphs
items.summary: This paper introduces QGPINNs, a physics-informed neural network framework built in PyTorch for solving nonlocal differential equations defined on quantum graphs, which are metric graphs equipped with differential operators on each edge. The approach assigns a separate neural network to each edge of the graph and enforces the governing equations alongside continuity, Kirchhoff-Neumann, and Dirichlet conditions through a unified graph-based loss function, coupling local edge-wise approximations into a coherent global solution. The framework targets two classes of nonlinear fractional models—multi-order fractional elliptic problems and time-fractional evolution equations—and incorporates specialized training strategies such as dynamic loss balancing, Fourier feature embeddings, and a learnable singularity-capturing feature to handle the weakly singular solutions these problems can produce. QGPINNs is also extended to inverse problems, enabling recovery of fractional operator orders and physical parameters from noisy data. Validation on benchmark graph structures and real-world networks demonstrates the framework's accuracy, computational efficiency, and physical consistency.
items.citation: Vaibhav Mehandiratta, Saket Ramchandra. QGPINNs: A Physics-Informed Neural Network Framework for Nonlocal Differential Equations on Quantum Graphs. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Continuity equation on metric spaces via measure-valued derivations and BV-Wasserstein curves
items.summary: This paper develops a theory of continuity equations on general metric spaces, capable of describing curves of probability measures that are absolutely continuous or of bounded variation with respect to the 1-Wasserstein distance. The authors introduce the notion of measure-valued derivations as the central analytical tool, building their basic theory and using it to formulate the continuity equation in this abstract setting. They show that on Euclidean space their framework is consistent with a previously introduced continuity equation with singular flux, including the associated notion of minimal solutions. A key result characterizes curves of bounded variation in the space of probability measures equipped with the extended 1-Wasserstein distance as precisely those curves satisfying the continuity equation driven by a measure-valued derivation of finite mass. To establish this characterization, the authors extend their prior work on probabilistic representations of bounded-variation curves and construct explicit measure-valued derivations and flux measures on geodesic metric spaces and Euclidean space, respectively.
items.citation: Ehsan Abedi, Zhenhao Li, Timo Schultz. Continuity equation on metric spaces via measure-valued derivations and BV-Wasserstein curves. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Renormalization-guided cascade upscaling for lattice field generation
items.summary: This paper introduces a machine-learning approach to generating lattice field configurations by approximately inverting renormalization-group transformations. The method combines a "perfect blocking" construction to supply equilibrated long-distance modes with a conditional normalizing flow that reconstructs short-distance details, followed by brief rethermalization to correct residual errors. By training the normalizing flow at relatively small lattice sizes and then applying it recursively in a cascade, the method achieves scalable generation of configurations at much larger lattice sizes. Applied to two-dimensional scalar field theory at criticality, the approach correctly reproduces long-distance physics at lattice sizes far beyond those used in training, demonstrating that the learned flow generalizes across scales through the recursive cascade procedure.
items.citation: Anna Hasenfratz, Ethan T. Neil, Letizia Parato et al.. Renormalization-guided cascade upscaling for lattice field generation. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Renormalization-guided inverse blocking for lattice field generation: construction and validation
items.summary: This paper proposes a lattice field theory generation algorithm that inverts a renormalization-group blocking transformation to efficiently produce configurations across multiple length scales. The approach optimizes a blocking transformation under a "perfect blocking" condition so that the resulting coarse-lattice distribution is well described by a simple action, then separates the blocking into an invertible smoothing step followed by decimation, with a conditional normalizing flow used to reconstruct the short-distance modes lost in decimation. A brief rethermalization step corrects residual mismatches between the generated and target distributions. The method operates recursively, reusing the same blocking transformation and learned flow to upscale configurations in a cascade from a small initial ensemble to much larger lattices. Testing in two-dimensional scalar field theory at criticality demonstrates stable cascade upscaling across several orders of magnitude in lattice volume on local computational resources, with rethermalization tests confirming that short-distance mismatches relax quickly while long-distance mismatches relax slowly, consistent with renormalization-group expectations.
items.citation: Anna Hasenfratz, Ethan T. Neil, Letizia Parato et al.. Renormalization-guided inverse blocking for lattice field generation: construction and validation. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Modular Functors with Singularities from Vertex Operator Algebras Beyond Rigidity and Finiteness
items.summary: This paper proposes a construction of spaces of conformal blocks for a vertex operator algebra and a suitable category of its modules, organized into an open-closed modular functor with singularities. The approach is built around the principle of holomorphic factorization, using a modular extension strategy to assign mapping class group representations to surfaces with boundary components and specified boundary labels, with the construction described explicitly on generating Dehn twists. A key advantage is that the framework operates beyond the usual requirements of rationality, rigidity, self-contragredience, and finiteness that constrain other approaches. The authors prove that their construction satisfies excision, is finite-dimensional in the cofinite case, and in the special case where the module category is a modular category, the resulting spaces are equivalent to string-net spaces and the modular functor for the corresponding Drinfeld center. As a concrete application, they verify that certain boundary conditions for the triplet algebra, a logarithmic conformal field theory with non-exact fusion product, yield well-defined correlation functions within the developed framework.
items.citation: Lukas Müller, Lukas Woike. Modular Functors with Singularities from Vertex Operator Algebras Beyond Rigidity and Finiteness. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Super-resolution Control of Two-dimensional Quantum Emitters
items.summary: This paper studied localized interlayer excitons in semiconducting transition-metal dichalcogenide heterobilayers, which act as quantum emitters and nanoscale charge sensors capable of probing correlated quantum phases. The researchers combined cryogenic optical spectroscopy with scanning probe microscopy to investigate trapped interlayer excitons in WSe₂/MoSe₂ bilayers. By exploiting an AFM-based local Stark shift, they achieved super-resolution localization of emitters separated by only a few tens of nanometers and demonstrated deterministic control of individual charge states, including trion formation. Time-resolved measurements further revealed that the scanning tip modifies the electromagnetic vacuum around individual emitters, thereby controlling their radiative emission rates. The authors propose that this multi-point charge sensing platform with optical readout is well-suited for studying exotic quantum phenomena such as fractionalization and anyon dynamics in semiconducting fractional Chern insulators.
items.citation: Bosai Lyu, Valeria Vento, Ludivine Fausten et al.. Super-resolution Control of Two-dimensional Quantum Emitters. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Trends of nucleic acid - based point-of-care diagnostics for infectious diseases.
items.summary: This review paper examines the landscape of nucleic acid-based point-of-care diagnostics for infectious diseases, motivated by the need for rapid, decentralized testing solutions beyond conventional laboratory settings. The authors organized their analysis around the three core operational steps of such diagnostics: nucleic acid extraction, amplification, and detection. For extraction, they assessed approaches including magnetic bead-based, paper-based, and integrated microfluidic methods, evaluating their suitability for simplified and equipment-free deployment. Amplification strategies reviewed include both thermal cycling methods such as PCR and isothermal alternatives such as LAMP, NASBA, and RPA, all of which have been adapted for portable and low-power conditions. On the detection side, the review spans colorimetric and fluorescent lateral flow assays through to advanced biosensor platforms exploiting CRISPR/Cas systems and toehold switch principles, highlighting the trajectory toward increasingly sensitive and programmable nucleic acid recognition at the point of care.
items.citation: Hatem H, Mysara M, Ramadan R. Trends of nucleic acid - based point-of-care diagnostics for infectious diseases.. Journal of biological engineering. 2026

items.title: Detection of Viral Nucleic Acid in Specimens Spotted on Commercial Filter Papers: A Review and Meta-Analysis.
items.summary: This paper reviewed and statistically synthesized the published literature on using commercial filter papers to collect, transport, and store biological samples for viral nucleic acid detection across human and veterinary pathogens. Following established systematic review guidelines, the authors searched multiple databases, identified eligible studies spanning dozens of filter paper types, and applied multilevel meta-analysis to calculate and compare nucleic acid detection rates. They found that detection rates varied substantially both by filter paper type and by virus target, with cellulose-based products such as Whatman and FTA matrices dominating the literature while polyester and glass fiber substrates were also represented. Experimental conditions including storage temperature, drying time, and humidity were inconsistently reported across studies yet appeared to influence viral nucleic acid recovery. The authors concluded that filter paper-based viral nucleic acid detection is highly variable and called for more rigorously designed comparative studies conducted across a defined range of conditions.
items.citation: Armenta-Leyva B, Munguía-Ramírez B, Kuennen B et al.. Detection of Viral Nucleic Acid in Specimens Spotted on Commercial Filter Papers: A Review and Meta-Analysis.. Viruses. 2026

items.title: 2025 Clinical Practice Guideline Update by the Infectious Diseases Society of America on Group A Streptococcal Pharyngitis: Risk Assessment Using Clinical Scoring Systems in Children and Adults.
items.summary: This guideline update from the Infectious Diseases Society of America examined whether clinical scoring systems should be used to guide diagnostic testing decisions for group A streptococcal pharyngitis in children and adults. The authors conducted a systematic review of randomized and nonrandomized studies comparing the diagnostic accuracy of standardized clinical scoring systems — which quantify infection probability based on features such as fever, tonsillar findings, lymphadenopathy, and absence of cough — against clinician judgment alone in predicting throat culture results. The evidence suggests that clinical scoring systems perform comparably to or slightly better than clinician judgment, though the available studies are limited by small sample sizes, inconsistent outcome measures, and incomplete data. Based on this review, the guideline panel concluded that the benefits of using a clinical scoring system outweigh the harms, recommending its incorporation into patient evaluation for sore throat. The primary value of such scoring systems lies in identifying patients with a low probability of infection, thereby reducing unnecessary diagnostic testing.
items.venue: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
items.citation: Linder JA, Watson ME, Wessels MR et al.. 2025 Clinical Practice Guideline Update by the Infectious Diseases Society of America on Group A Streptococcal Pharyngitis: Risk Assessment Using Clinical Scoring Systems in Children and Adults.. Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America. 2026

items.title: The WHO priority list of antibiotic-resistant bacteria: challenges and opportunities for next-generation antimicrobial development
items.summary: This narrative review examines the global challenge of antimicrobial resistance with a focus on pathogens designated as priorities by the World Health Organization. The authors synthesize current understanding of the molecular mechanisms by which these bacteria evade existing antibiotics, encompassing reduced membrane permeability, efflux pumps, enzymatic inactivation, target modification, biofilm formation, and horizontal gene transfer. The review critically evaluates why conventional antibiotic discovery pipelines have failed to keep pace with resistance and assesses a range of emerging therapeutic strategies—including artificial intelligence-assisted drug discovery, phage therapy, antimicrobial peptides, CRISPR-based systems, and natural product-derived compounds—with attention to their pharmacological feasibility, toxicity, delivery challenges, and regulatory hurdles. The authors also address the clinical and economic burden imposed by resistant infections and emphasize that antimicrobial stewardship, surveillance, and a One Health framework integrating human, animal, and environmental sectors are essential complements to new drug development. The overarching conclusion is that tackling priority pathogens will require integrated, multidisciplinary approaches spanning molecular biology, pharmacology, clinical translation, and public health.
items.citation: Emad M. Abdallah, Abdulrahman Mohammed Alhudhaibi, Mahmoud M. Dahab et al.. The WHO priority list of antibiotic-resistant bacteria: challenges and opportunities for next-generation antimicrobial development. Frontiers in Pharmacology. 2026

items.title: Detection to Disruption: A Comprehensive Review of Bacterial Biofilms and Therapeutic Advances
items.summary: This review examines the biology, clinical significance, and treatment of bacterial biofilms, which are structured microbial communities embedded in a self-produced extracellular polymeric substance matrix. The authors synthesize current knowledge on how biofilms develop, how their matrix composition and physiological heterogeneity protect bacteria from both antimicrobials and host immune defenses, and how specific resistance mechanisms—including limited antibiotic diffusion, efflux pump upregulation, persister cell formation, and horizontal gene transfer—make these infections exceptionally difficult to eradicate. The review maps the clinical contexts in which biofilms are most problematic, spanning chronic wounds, cystic fibrosis, osteomyelitis, device-associated infections, and breast implant illness, where persistent biofilm-driven inflammation may contribute to systemic manifestations. The authors also survey conventional and emerging detection methods alongside therapeutic strategies that pair antibiotics with matrix-disrupting enzymes, quorum-sensing inhibitors, bacteriophages, metabolic reactivators, and nanotechnology-based delivery systems. They conclude that effective management of biofilm-associated disease requires integrated detection and multifaceted treatment approaches, and that advances in multi-omics and systems-level modeling will be critical for developing next-generation interventions.
items.citation: Pranay Amruth Maroju, Angad S. Sidhu, Amogh R. Motaganahalli et al.. Detection to Disruption: A Comprehensive Review of Bacterial Biofilms and Therapeutic Advances. Antibiotics. 2026

items.title: Advances in Natural Product Extraction: Established and Emerging Technologies
items.summary: This review examines recent advances in the extraction and isolation of natural products, motivated by the renewed prominence of nature-derived compounds in drug discovery. The authors surveyed progress across a range of established and emerging technologies, including green and designer solvent systems, pressurized and ultrasound-assisted extraction platforms, supercritical fluid techniques, and integrated purification workflows. Particular attention is given to the application of artificial intelligence and machine learning for solvent selection, extraction optimization, and metabolite dereplication, which together with advanced phase-separation and informatic tools have expanded the range of detectable metabolites in complex biological matrices. The review concludes that combinatorial extraction strategies and next-generation solvent systems have collectively improved operational efficiency, selectivity, compound recovery, and analytical throughput over the recent period surveyed.
items.citation: Carsyn R. Travis, Jared McMaster, Fatima Rivas. Advances in Natural Product Extraction: Established and Emerging Technologies. Molecules. 2026

items.title: Harnessing biogenic nanoparticles for combating antibiotic resistance: green synthesis, mechanistic insights, and biotechnological applications
items.summary: This review examines biogenic nanoparticles as a potential strategy to address the growing global crisis of antimicrobial resistance, focusing on materials synthesized through biological processes using plants, microorganisms, algae, or isolated biomolecules. The authors surveyed recent advances in green synthesis approaches, describing how biological metabolites govern metal ion reduction, nucleation, and stabilization, which in turn determine nanoparticle size, morphology, and antimicrobial properties. A range of metal and metal oxide nanoparticles were reviewed for their antibacterial activity against WHO-priority and ESKAPE pathogens, with multiple proposed mechanisms including membrane disruption, reactive oxygen species generation, biofilm suppression, and quorum sensing interference. The review also covers their experimental use as adjuncts to antibiotics or phytochemicals, where synergistic effects may lower required drug concentrations, as well as applications in wound care, drug delivery, biosensing, and food packaging. The authors conclude that while biogenic nanoparticles show considerable promise, substantial obstacles including inconsistent synthesis protocols, limited scalability, and insufficient toxicological and environmental safety data must be resolved before clinical or regulatory advancement is feasible.
items.citation: Emad M. Abdallah, Abdulrahman Mohammed Alhudhaibi, Ibrahim Mohammed Hussaini et al.. Harnessing biogenic nanoparticles for combating antibiotic resistance: green synthesis, mechanistic insights, and biotechnological applications. Frontiers in Bioengineering and Biotechnology. 2026
