items.title: Interaction corrections to topological density three-point functions in two-dimensional Fermi liquids: a coadjoint orbit perspective
items.summary: This paper investigates how electron-electron interactions affect density three-point correlation functions in two-dimensional Fermi liquids, which are known to encode topological information about the Fermi sea in the noninteracting limit. The authors employ the coadjoint-orbit effective field theory framework, which allows Landau interactions to be incorporated systematically by mapping fermionic loop diagrams onto tree-level calculations in a bosonized description. They find that even at linear order in the generalized Landau interaction parameter, a contribution proportional to the band curvature at the Fermi momentum emerges that alters the nonanalytic structure of the free density three-point function. This new nonanalytic structure is distinct from both the noninteracting case and the interacting Galilean-invariant limit, demonstrating that interactions can qualitatively modify the topology-detecting character of the density three-point correlator. The results indicate that the relationship between these correlation functions and Fermi sea topology is more subtle in the presence of interactions than previously appreciated.
items.citation: Akshay Pal, Andrew Lucas, Umang Mehta. Interaction corrections to topological density three-point functions in two-dimensional Fermi liquids: a coadjoint orbit perspective. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Bounds for inertialess dynamo
items.summary: This paper derives rigorous mathematical necessary conditions that must be satisfied for dynamo action to occur in rotating convective systems. The authors analyze a magnetohydrodynamic model in two settings: a rapidly rotating plane layer where inertia and viscosity are neglected, and a more general configuration with finite viscosity, in both cases coupling the magnetic field evolution to an inertialess force balance rather than treating the velocity field as kinematically prescribed. They establish that the buoyancy-driven component of the flow must exceed a threshold involving the magnetic Reynolds number and a norm of the flow field, expressed as an inequality over a range of Lebesgue norms, with a refined version using an anisotropic norm derived from poloidal-toroidal decomposition. For the viscous case, necessary conditions are also obtained for the growth of magnetic enstrophy and combined thermo-magnetic energy, with one branch of constraints implying a specific scaling relationship between the Rayleigh number and Ekman number that must hold for dynamo action to be possible.
items.citation: Ali Arslan, Hezekiah Grayer. Bounds for inertialess dynamo. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Layer-Controlled Intermolecular Coupling and Many-Body Effects in C$_{60}$ Films
items.summary: This paper investigated how electronic properties of crystalline C₆₀ molecular thin films evolve as a function of film thickness, from the monolayer limit to the bulk. Using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy combined with Holstein-model simulations, the researchers systematically characterized the band structure across this thickness range. They found a non-monotonic evolution of the highest occupied molecular orbital-derived band, with intermediate-thickness films exhibiting larger bandwidth, reduced effective mass, and pronounced gap-like and sub-band features compared to both thinner and thicker films. These observations were attributed to strengthened intermolecular electronic coupling and enhanced electron-phonon-induced spectral renormalization specifically in the intermediate-thickness regime. The study identifies a dimensional crossover in C₆₀ films and establishes layer number as a tunable parameter for controlling electronic structure and many-body interactions in molecular thin films, offering a complementary approach to the twist-angle tuning used in moiré van der Waals heterostructures.
items.citation: Hai-Lan Luo, Weitang Li, Luca Moreschini et al.. Layer-Controlled Intermolecular Coupling and Many-Body Effects in C$_{60}$ Films. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Renormalization-guided cascade upscaling for lattice field generation
items.summary: This paper introduces a machine-learning algorithm for generating lattice field configurations by approximately inverting a renormalization-group transformation. The method combines a "perfect blocking" construction to supply equilibrated long-distance modes with a conditional normalizing flow that reconstructs short-distance details, followed by brief rethermalization to correct residual errors. The approach is applied recursively in a cascade scheme, where a normalizing flow trained on small lattices is reused to generate progressively larger lattices. Testing on two-dimensional scalar field theory at criticality demonstrates that the method successfully reproduces correct long-distance physics at lattice sizes far exceeding those used during training, showcasing strong generalization across scales.
items.citation: Anna Hasenfratz, Ethan T. Neil, Letizia Parato et al.. Renormalization-guided cascade upscaling for lattice field generation. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Renormalization-guided inverse blocking for lattice field generation: construction and validation
items.summary: This paper proposes and validates a new algorithm for generating lattice field configurations by approximately inverting a renormalization-group blocking transformation. The approach optimizes the blocking using a perfect blocking condition so that the coarse-grained lattice distribution is captured by a simple action, then separates the blocking into an invertible smoothing step followed by decimation, with a conditional normalizing flow used to reconstruct the short-distance degrees of freedom lost during decimation. A brief fine-action rethermalization corrects residual mismatches, and the procedure can be applied recursively, cascading upward from a small initial ensemble to much larger lattices by reusing the same blocking transformation and trained flow. The method was tested in two-dimensional scalar field theory at criticality, successfully demonstrating stable cascade upscaling across several orders of magnitude in lattice volume using only local computational resources. Rethermalization tests confirm that short-distance mismatches relax quickly while mismatches in the relevant thermal direction relax slowly, consistent with expected renormalization-group behavior, and the authors argue the framework extends naturally toward higher-dimensional, gauge, and fermionic systems.
items.citation: Anna Hasenfratz, Ethan T. Neil, Letizia Parato et al.. Renormalization-guided inverse blocking for lattice field generation: construction and validation. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Modular Functors with Singularities from Vertex Operator Algebras Beyond Rigidity and Finiteness
items.summary: This paper develops a construction of conformal blocks associated to a vertex operator algebra and an appropriate category of its modules, organized into a mathematical structure called an open-closed modular functor with singularities. The authors implement the principle of holomorphic factorization directly, using a modular extension strategy to assign mapping class group representations to surfaces with boundary components and labeled boundary data, with the action describable explicitly on generating Dehn twists. In the special case where the module category is a not necessarily semisimple modular category, the resulting spaces are shown to be equivalent to string-net spaces and hence to the modular functor for the associated Drinfeld center, connecting the construction to established topological and algebraic-geometric approaches. A key advantage of the framework is that it extends beyond the usual requirements of rationality, rigidity, self-contragredience, and finiteness, and the authors prove that the construction satisfies excision, is finite-dimensional in the cofinite case, and yields representations of surface braid groups. As an application, they demonstrate for a specific non-semisimple example, the triplet algebra with non-exact fusion product, that physically motivated boundary conditions give rise to well-defined correlation functions within the developed notion of a modular functor with singularities.
items.citation: Lukas Müller, Lukas Woike. Modular Functors with Singularities from Vertex Operator Algebras Beyond Rigidity and Finiteness. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Innovative epitope-based ELISA assay for detecting Group B Streptococcus carriage in pregnant women.
items.summary: This study investigated synthetic peptide epitopes derived from *Streptococcus agalactiae* proteins as components of an ELISA-based immunodiagnostic test for detecting Group B Streptococcus infection and carriage in pregnant women. The researchers selected three epitopes from the bacterial proteins GroEL, enolase, and EF-Tu, and evaluated their ability to distinguish between GBS-positive and GBS-negative serum samples using IgG, IgM, and IgA antibody detection. All three synthetic epitopes, both individually and in combination, significantly differentiated between positive and negative sera, with the enolase-derived and EF-Tu-derived peptides performing best as individual candidates due to their higher immunoreactivity at lower concentrations. Notably, combining the epitopes in various mixtures further improved overall immunoreactivity compared to single-peptide use. The authors propose this epitope-based ELISA prototype as a promising alternative to the current culture-based gold standard, which is slow and sometimes yields ambiguous results.
items.citation: Brzychczy-Włoch M, Dobrut A, Drożdż K et al.. Innovative epitope-based ELISA assay for detecting Group B Streptococcus carriage in pregnant women.. Applied microbiology and biotechnology. 2026

items.title: Bridging the diagnostic gap: the role of culture methods in the era of syndromic panels for central nervous system infections.
items.summary: This study evaluated the diagnostic performance of a syndromic molecular panel for central nervous system infections by comparing it against conventional culture methods using cerebrospinal fluid samples collected over three years at a national reference center. The researchers analyzed concordance, sensitivity, specificity, and predictive values across a large dataset of paired molecular and culture results. They found moderate overall agreement between the two approaches, with the syndromic panel demonstrating high specificity but limited sensitivity when all culture-identified pathogens were considered; however, restricting analysis to bacterial targets actually included in the panel substantially improved both agreement and sensitivity, with a very high negative predictive value. Crucially, conventional culture identified clinically relevant organisms absent from the panel's target list, including pathogens of clear therapeutic importance, underscoring that the syndromic panel cannot serve as a standalone diagnostic tool. The authors conclude that optimal management of central nervous system infections requires systematic integration of syndromic molecular testing with conventional culture, and advocate for next-generation multiplex platforms with broader pathogen coverage guided by real-world epidemiological data.
items.venue: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
items.citation: Sberna G, D'Arezzo S, Valli MB et al.. Bridging the diagnostic gap: the role of culture methods in the era of syndromic panels for central nervous system infections.. Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology. 2026

items.title: Performance of the LIAISON PLEX gram-positive blood culture assay for identifying bacterial pathogens and resistance genes in blood cultures.
items.summary: This study evaluated the diagnostic performance of the LIAISON PLEX Gram-Positive Blood Culture Assay, a multiplexed molecular test designed to rapidly identify gram-positive bacterial pathogens and antibiotic resistance markers directly from positive blood culture bottles. The assay targets thirteen gram-positive bacterial species and four antibiotic resistance markers, and its performance was assessed across a large, diverse collection of prospective clinical, pre-selected, and contrived blood culture samples at multiple sites. The assay demonstrated very high overall sensitivity and specificity for all targets, with a near-perfect valid test rate, and showed broad inclusivity across tested bacterial strains with only minimal cross-reactivity among off-panel species. Performance was maintained in the presence of potential interfering substances, across blood culture bottles from multiple manufacturers, and in polymicrobial infection scenarios. The authors conclude that the assay offers fast, accurate, and reliable detection of gram-positive organisms and their resistance genes from positive blood cultures, with potential benefits for antibiotic stewardship and patient management.
items.citation: Chow S-K, Stevig C, Granato P et al.. Performance of the LIAISON PLEX gram-positive blood culture assay for identifying bacterial pathogens and resistance genes in blood cultures.. Journal of clinical microbiology. 2026

items.title: Utility and clinical relevance of multiplex PCR panels for diagnosis of central nervous system infections.
items.summary: This study evaluated the diagnostic performance and real-world clinical utility of multiplex polymerase chain reaction panels designed to detect multiple pathogens simultaneously from cerebrospinal fluid in patients with suspected meningitis or encephalitis. Researchers retrospectively reviewed samples tested over a five-year period at a tertiary care hospital, examining test results alongside clinical data and subsequent management decisions. Viral pathogens dominated the positive findings, with human herpesvirus-6, enterovirus, and herpes simplex virus type-1 most frequently detected, while Streptococcus pneumoniae was the leading bacterial pathogen identified. Despite the panels' capacity for rapid, broad pathogen detection, fewer than half of positive results were associated with a documented change in diagnosis or treatment, and repeat testing after an initial negative result added little diagnostic value. The authors conclude that inappropriate test utilisation and insufficient clinician familiarity with panel contents limit the clinical impact of these tools, and that clearer testing criteria are needed to improve diagnostic efficiency.
items.venue: The Indian journal of medical research
items.citation: Gürler M, Karaoğlu Ç, Yurtcu EE et al.. Utility and clinical relevance of multiplex PCR panels for diagnosis of central nervous system infections.. The Indian journal of medical research. 2026

items.title: Validation of an in-house developed rapid assay for Group B Streptococcus detection in pregnancy.
items.summary: This study addressed the need for a rapid and practical method to detect Group B Streptococcus colonization in pregnant women, a key risk factor for neonatal infections and preterm stillbirth. The researchers developed and validated an in-house assay combining CRISPR/Cas12a with recombinase polymerase amplification, an isothermal technique that eliminates the need for conventional thermal cycling. The assay was evaluated for specificity against other common female reproductive tract pathogens, and its limit of detection was established using serial dilutions of GBS-derived plasmids. Clinical performance was assessed using a large collection of vaginal-rectal swabs from pregnant women, with results compared against a commercial quantitative real-time PCR method. The assay completed testing within one hour, demonstrated high sensitivity and specificity, and showed strong concordance with the established PCR reference, supporting its potential for routine clinical use.
items.venue: International journal of medical microbiology : IJMM
items.citation: Hu S, Xie J, Liu L et al.. Validation of an in-house developed rapid assay for Group B Streptococcus detection in pregnancy.. International journal of medical microbiology : IJMM. 2026

items.title: Advances in tuberculosis diagnostics and biomarkers, 2020-26: scientific evidence, recommendations, gaps, and developmental priorities.
items.summary: This paper reviews advances in tuberculosis diagnostics and biomarker research over roughly a five-year period, synthesizing scientific evidence to inform updated WHO policy guidance that consolidates recommendations for detecting tuberculosis disease and drug resistance into a unified framework. Digital chest radiography with computer-aided detection has become a core WHO-recommended screening and triage tool, while decentralised molecular diagnosis has expanded through a diversified portfolio of rapid nucleic acid amplification tests, including automated and manual platforms, as well as near point-of-care devices under evaluation. Novel specimen types such as tongue swabs and non-sputum specimens including stool and nasopharyngeal samples have improved bacteriological confirmation in children and others who cannot produce sputum, and targeted next-generation sequencing is now endorsed for comprehensive drug-susceptibility testing at reference laboratory level. Urine lipoarabinomannan assays improve diagnostic yield in people with HIV and advanced disease, though their broader applicability remains limited, and host blood transcriptomic and other biomarker signatures show promise for prognosis and triage but none yet meets WHO target product profile criteria for a point-of-care test that reliably distinguishes infection from disease, including subclinical tuberculosis. The paper concludes that substantial performance, implementation, and equity gaps persist across the diagnostics landscape.
items.citation: Walzl G, McHugh TD, Chakaya J et al.. Advances in tuberculosis diagnostics and biomarkers, 2020-26: scientific evidence, recommendations, gaps, and developmental priorities.. The Lancet. Microbe. 2027

items.title: Development of a microfluidic isothermal amplification nucleic acid detection (mFIND) platform for simultaneous detection of respiratory pathogens.
items.summary: The paper describes the development of a centrifugal microfluidic platform designed to simultaneously detect multiple respiratory pathogens, including influenza A and B, SARS-CoV-2, and RSV, from a single sample. The system integrates isothermal amplification with lyophilized reagents in independent reaction chambers on a chip, paired with a portable analyzer that automates temperature control and real-time fluorescence detection, completing the process in under fifteen minutes using very small reaction volumes. The platform demonstrated extremely low limits of detection for all four target pathogens and showed no cross-reactivity against a broad panel of non-target organisms. Clinical validation against a large set of confirmed positive samples showed complete agreement with quantitative PCR for both positive and negative results. The authors conclude that the platform represents a practical point-of-care nucleic acid testing solution suitable for decentralized diagnostic settings, combining speed, simplified workflow, and multiplexed pathogen detection.
items.citation: He P, Feng Y, Zhou X et al.. Development of a microfluidic isothermal amplification nucleic acid detection (mFIND) platform for simultaneous detection of respiratory pathogens.. Biosensors & bioelectronics. 2026

items.title: Development and evaluation of a rapid duplex qPCR assay for Treponema pallidum using the GeneSoC microfluidic platform.
items.summary: This paper describes the development and evaluation of a rapid duplex quantitative PCR assay for detecting Treponema pallidum, the causative agent of syphilis, using a microfluidic platform. The assay targeted two genomic regions simultaneously and was tested against DNA standards, a reference strain, and clinical specimens including lesion swabs and urine samples, with and without prior DNA extraction. The assay demonstrated good linearity and amplification efficiency across both targets, showed no cross-reactivity with other pathogens, and achieved detection within a substantially shorter timeframe than a conventional comparator system, owing to the faster temperature transitions enabled by microfluidic thermal cycling. Detection was possible directly from clinical specimens without DNA extraction, though extraction was noted to improve sensitivity when target DNA concentrations are low. The authors conclude that this platform represents a promising approach for point-of-care syphilis diagnosis, including during the seronegative window period when serological tests may be unreliable.
items.citation: Kawahata T, Banno F, Hama M. Development and evaluation of a rapid duplex qPCR assay for Treponema pallidum using the GeneSoC microfluidic platform.. Diagnostic microbiology and infectious disease. 2026

items.title: Trends of nucleic acid - based point-of-care diagnostics for infectious diseases.
items.summary: This review examines the landscape of nucleic acid-based point-of-care diagnostics for infectious diseases, motivated by the global need for decentralized, rapid, and accessible testing outside conventional laboratory settings. The authors systematically organized their analysis around three core operational stages: nucleic acid extraction, amplification, and detection. For extraction, they evaluated approaches including magnetic bead-based, paper-based, and integrated microfluidic methods, emphasizing their suitability for simplified and equipment-free deployment. For amplification, they reviewed both thermal cycling methods such as polymerase chain reaction and isothermal alternatives including loop-mediated isothermal amplification, recombinase polymerase amplification, and nucleic acid sequence-based amplification, all adapted for portable and low-power conditions. On the detection side, the review spans colorimetric and fluorescent lateral flow assays through to advanced biosensor platforms exploiting CRISPR/Cas systems and toehold switch mechanisms, which offer highly sensitive and programmable nucleic acid recognition.
items.citation: Hatem H, Mysara M, Ramadan R. Trends of nucleic acid - based point-of-care diagnostics for infectious diseases.. Journal of biological engineering. 2026

items.title: A nested PCR-based point-of-care multiplex test for detection of bacterial pathogens in cerebrospinal fluids.
items.summary: This study developed and evaluated a multiplex one-tube nested real-time PCR assay integrated with a point-of-care testing instrument for detecting three bacterial pathogens responsible for central nervous system infections in cerebrospinal fluid. The researchers assessed analytical sensitivity using recombinant plasmids and simulated cerebrospinal fluid samples, evaluated specificity against common pathogens, and validated clinical performance using over one hundred clinical samples compared against conventional real-time PCR with manual nucleic acid extraction. The integrated point-of-care system achieved low detection limits for all three target pathogens with no cross-reactivity, and reduced total testing time to approximately two hours compared to four hours with manual methods. In clinical testing, the new assay identified additional positive cases that conventional real-time PCR had missed, demonstrating superior sensitivity. The authors conclude that this automated, culture-free workflow offers a rapid and highly sensitive diagnostic approach for bacterial meningitis pathogens directly from cerebrospinal fluid.
items.venue: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
items.citation: Wu J, Zhao Z, Pang P et al.. A nested PCR-based point-of-care multiplex test for detection of bacterial pathogens in cerebrospinal fluids.. Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology. 2026

items.title: A Novel Voltammetric Point-of-Care Device for Rapid and Accurate Nucleic Acid and Viral Pathogen Detection.
items.summary: This paper investigated a novel electrochemical approach to infectious disease diagnostics designed to overcome the sensitivity limitations of lateral flow assays and the optical detection challenges of isothermal amplification methods. The researchers developed a nucleic acid amplification test that couples isothermal loop-mediated amplification with real-time voltammetric detection, using a pH-sensing redox compound to monitor the proton release that accompanies amplification. The method was evaluated against established RT-qPCR standards across several respiratory pathogens, including SARS-CoV-2, influenza A and B viruses, RSV A, and equine herpesvirus, using both purified RNA from clinical samples and an extraction-free workflow with nasal swabs. The system demonstrated high concordance with RT-qPCR results and achieved a low limit of detection for influenza A virus. The authors conclude that real-time voltammetric amplification is feasible across multiple sample types and pathogens, while acknowledging that further validation in additional matrices and prospective cohorts is needed before broad point-of-care deployment.
items.citation: Munita R, Lyttleton R, Danefur E et al.. A Novel Voltammetric Point-of-Care Device for Rapid and Accurate Nucleic Acid and Viral Pathogen Detection.. ACS omega. 2026

items.title: Biosensing technologies for foodborne pathogen detection and healthcare: principles, emerging materials, and intelligent platforms
items.summary: This review examines the current state and future directions of biosensing technologies designed to detect priority foodborne pathogens, including Escherichia coli, Salmonella, and Listeria monocytogenes, with relevance to both food safety and clinical healthcare settings. The authors survey electrochemical, optical, and microfluidic sensing platforms, evaluating how advances in functional nanomaterials, aptamers, nanozymes, and surface engineering strategies have improved sensor sensitivity, specificity, and performance in complex food matrices. A central focus is the integration of artificial intelligence and machine learning with these biosensors, enabling real-time analytics, intelligent pattern recognition, and high-throughput multiplexed detection that transforms conventional systems into smart diagnostic devices. The review critically addresses persistent challenges such as matrix interference, biorecognition element instability, scalability limitations, and the absence of regulatory standardization, while proposing mitigation strategies including ratiometric sensing, microfluidic pre-treatment, and explainable AI frameworks. Looking forward, the authors advocate for self-powered biosensors, modular pathogen detection panels, blockchain-based data integrity, and standardized validation pipelines as pathways toward deployable, regulation-ready platforms for next-generation food safety monitoring.
items.citation: Purshottam J. Assudani, Balakrishnan . P., Anny Leema A et al.. Biosensing technologies for foodborne pathogen detection and healthcare: principles, emerging materials, and intelligent platforms. Microchimica Acta. 2026

items.title: Loss-of-function mutation in Omicron variants reduces spike protein expression and attenuates SARS-CoV-2 infection
items.citation: Michelle N. Vu, R. Elias Alvarado, Dorothea R. Morris et al.. Loss-of-function mutation in Omicron variants reduces spike protein expression and attenuates SARS-CoV-2 infection. Nature Communications. 2026

items.title: Data-Centric Foundation Models in Computational Healthcare: A Survey
items.summary: This survey examines the intersection of foundation models and computational healthcare through a data-centric lens, focusing on how data quality, scale, and characterization shape AI performance in clinical settings. The authors reviewed a broad range of data-centric approaches spanning the full pipeline from model pre-training through inference, addressing longstanding healthcare-specific challenges such as data scarcity, annotation burden, patient privacy, and ethical considerations. The survey also discusses AI security, model assessment, and alignment with human values as critical considerations for deploying foundation models in medical contexts. The authors conclude with an optimistic outlook on the potential of foundation model-based analytics to improve patient outcomes and streamline clinical workflows, and they maintain a living repository of relevant models and datasets to support ongoing research in the field.
items.citation: Yunkun Zhang, Jin Gao, Zheling Tan et al.. Data-Centric Foundation Models in Computational Healthcare: A Survey. ACM Computing Surveys. 2026

items.title: Comprehensive Review on Candidemia: Epidemiology, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Future Directions
items.summary: This review examines candidemia, a major cause of hospital-acquired bloodstream infections that carries high mortality and significant healthcare burden. The authors conducted a comprehensive literature synthesis covering the epidemiology, species distribution, and origins of candidemia, alongside an evaluation of current and emerging diagnostic approaches. The review addresses therapeutic strategies in depth, including empiric and targeted antifungal regimens, management of mixed infections, host-drug interactions, and the growing problem of antifungal resistance, with particular attention to combination therapy as a potential solution. Advances in drug development are highlighted, encompassing agents under clinical investigation and compounds directed at novel fungal targets. Looking forward, the review identifies artificial intelligence-assisted diagnostics, vaccine-based prophylaxis, and synergistic treatment strategies as promising avenues to improve candidemia management for both clinicians and researchers.
items.citation: Haojie Dong, Minghui Song, Jingfang Sun et al.. Comprehensive Review on Candidemia: Epidemiology, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Future Directions. iFungi. 2026

items.title: Multi-omics and artificial intelligence for precision drug discovery and potential clinical applications
items.summary: This review examines the integration of multiomics technologies and artificial intelligence as a combined framework for advancing precision drug discovery. The paper surveys how approaches including genome-wide association studies, transcriptomics, proteomics, and metabolomics generate deep molecular insights into disease mechanisms, and how deep learning architectures can extract meaningful patterns from these complex datasets. The authors analyze applications across the drug development pipeline, including target deconvolution, drug repositioning, de novo compound discovery, virtual screening, pharmacokinetic modeling, and safety assessment. Case examples drawn from oncology, neurodegenerative diseases, and cardiovascular conditions are used to illustrate the practical potential of this convergence, while the review also acknowledges persistent challenges such as harmonizing disparate data streams, ensuring reproducibility, and reducing algorithmic bias. The authors conclude that combining multiomics with artificial intelligence opens new pathways for therapeutic innovation and represents a transformative advance in translational medicine.
items.citation: Yuqing Liu, Kun Zhu, Weijun Peng et al.. Multi-omics and artificial intelligence for precision drug discovery and potential clinical applications. Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy. 2026

items.title: In vivo endosomal escape assay identifies mechanisms for efficient hepatic LNP delivery
items.citation: Antony Jozić, C. Roux, Jeonghwan Kim et al.. In vivo endosomal escape assay identifies mechanisms for efficient hepatic LNP delivery. Nature Biotechnology. 2026

items.title: Renormalization-guided inverse blocking for lattice field generation: construction and validation
items.summary: This paper introduces a lattice field configuration generation algorithm that inverts a renormalization-group blocking transformation to efficiently sample field configurations across multiple length scales. The blocking transformation is optimized using a "perfect blocking" condition so that the coarse-grained lattice follows a simple action, and it is decomposed into an invertible smoothing step followed by decimation, with a conditional normalizing flow reconstructing the short-distance degrees of freedom lost during decimation. A brief rethermalization step corrects residual mismatches, and the procedure is applied recursively in a cascade, reusing the same learned transformation to upscale from small to very large volumes. Tested in two-dimensional scalar field theory at criticality, the method successfully generates configurations through cascade upscaling spanning several orders of magnitude in lattice size using only local computational resources. Rethermalization tests confirm that short-distance mismatches relax quickly, while mismatches in the relevant thermal direction relax much more slowly, consistent with expected renormalization-group behavior, and the framework is designed to generalize to higher dimensions, gauge fields, and fermionic systems.
items.citation: Anna Hasenfratz, Ethan T. Neil, Letizia Parato et al.. Renormalization-guided inverse blocking for lattice field generation: construction and validation. arXiv. 2026

items.title: QUEST: A Query and Extraction System for Topics in Asylum Law Application Decisions
items.summary: The paper addresses the challenge of automatically identifying credibility-related factors in asylum application appeal decisions, which are lengthy, complex legal documents combining interviews, original rulings, and supporting materials. The authors developed QUEST, an information retrieval system that combines synthetic query generation, topic extraction, and relevance assessment to locate information pertaining to credibility indicators within two datasets of Danish asylum appeal decisions. Beyond standard retrieval evaluation metrics, they proposed a novel domain-specific assessment framework tailored to credibility factors rather than conventional topical relevance. Their findings reveal that evaluating system performance through credibility-based relevance assessments is considerably more difficult than standard retrieval evaluation, highlighting the inherent complexity of extracting legally meaningful credibility information from asylum documents.
items.citation: Maria Vlachou, Anna Murphy Høgenhaug, Mohammad N. S. Jahromi et al.. QUEST: A Query and Extraction System for Topics in Asylum Law Application Decisions. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Offline-Verifiable Accountability for Cross-Organization Agent Messaging: A Preserved Evidence-Bundle Approach
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of verifying accountability for cross-organization agent-to-agent messaging workflows when live systems are unavailable, controlled by a single party, or not mutually trusted. The authors propose a preserved evidence-bundle model in which each workflow event carries policy-required evidence including sender authentication, log commitments, witness-backed checkpoints, append-only continuity proofs, delegation authorization, and optional receiver-signed receipts. A policy-controlled offline verifier then assesses whether a given bundle satisfies the selected policy's evidence requirements without inferring delivery or receipt from transport behavior alone. In a prototype evaluation across hundreds of complete workflows and thousands of preserved bundles, the system successfully rejected all corrupted or policy-insufficient bundles with no false acceptances, while checkpoint-context anchoring was identified as the highest-latency component. The work aims to provide a principled, verifier-centered basis for audit and dispute resolution that does not depend on platform-specific logs or online service availability.
items.citation: Adil Alshammari, Hayretdin Bahsi. Offline-Verifiable Accountability for Cross-Organization Agent Messaging: A Preserved Evidence-Bundle Approach. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Analysis of Polynomial Threshold Functions on Random Regular Graphs: Computational Complexity of Detecting Noisy Random Lift
items.summary: The paper studies the computational complexity of a hypothesis testing problem: distinguishing a noisy random lift of a base regular graph from a uniformly random regular graph. To analyze this problem, the authors develop the first treatment of low-degree polynomial threshold functions in this setting, characterizing the power and limitations of this class of computationally efficient algorithms. A key technical contribution is a new result on the distribution of short cycle counts in noisy random lifts up to logarithmic lengths, which generalizes several prior results on cycle statistics in random regular graphs and random lifts. The findings contribute to understanding which graph hypothesis testing problems are computationally tractable versus intractable for low-degree methods.
items.citation: Xifan Yu. Analysis of Polynomial Threshold Functions on Random Regular Graphs: Computational Complexity of Detecting Noisy Random Lift. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Hierarchical organization governs nonlinear mechanical reversibility in $ι$-carrageenan gels
items.summary: This paper investigated how the molecular and mesoscale organization of ι-carrageenan gels controls their mechanical behavior under both small and large deformations. The researchers studied temperature-dependent rheology of these thermoreversible polysaccharide gels formed in potassium chloride solutions, using linear and nonlinear oscillatory rheology alongside normal-force measurements. They found that deeper temperature quenches produce gels with higher elastic moduli and pronounced strain stiffening before yielding, accompanied by internal stresses evidenced by negative normal forces. Strikingly, large deformations partially and reversibly altered the network by suppressing strain stiffening while leaving the small-strain elastic modulus intact. The authors interpret these findings through a hierarchical network model in which a robust intermolecular network governs linear elasticity, while a more fragile mesoscale organization enables cooperative structural alignment and stress amplification that can be reversibly disrupted under deformation.
items.citation: Thomas Gibaud, Loïc Hilliou. Hierarchical organization governs nonlinear mechanical reversibility in $ι$-carrageenan gels. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Understanding Venture Capital Syndication in Information Technology Sectors: A Network Formation Perspective
items.summary: This paper investigates how venture capital co-investment networks form and evolve within the U.S. information technology sector, focusing on the mechanisms that drive syndication partnerships among investors. Using a comprehensive dyadic dataset spanning several decades across hardware, software, and hybrid subsectors, the researchers tested how factors such as prior collaboration, shared investment partners, geographic proximity, and organizational similarity influence the likelihood of two investors co-investing in a given year. They employed dyadic logit models with clustered standard errors across the full sample as well as an exponential random graph model applied to a snapshot of the software network. The findings consistently show that prior collaboration is the strongest predictor of new co-investment ties, while triadic closure and geographic homophily also robustly structure network formation, with other mechanisms like domain overlap and prominence showing more context-dependent effects. The study concludes that relational persistence, network closure, and similarity jointly govern how syndication networks are organized in information technology venture finance.
items.citation: Liheng Tan, Zhengkai Tu, Prasanna Karhade. Understanding Venture Capital Syndication in Information Technology Sectors: A Network Formation Perspective. arXiv. 2026

items.title: A rapid detection of Nipah virus nucleocapsid antigen in inactivated viral cultures.
items.citation: Choi G, Kim J, Lee H et al.. A rapid detection of Nipah virus nucleocapsid antigen in inactivated viral cultures.. Emerging microbes & infections. 2026

items.title: Point prevalence assessments of five respiratory viruses in adults ≥ 50 years of age in Germany by multi-pathogen rapid antigen testing on June 1, 2024, and December 15, 2024.
items.summary: This study investigated the circulation of five respiratory viruses among community-dwelling adults aged fifty years and older in Germany using two cross-sectional point prevalence assessments conducted in summer and winter of 2024. Participants self-administered multi-pathogen rapid antigen tests capable of detecting adenovirus, SARS-CoV-2, influenza A and B, and respiratory syncytial virus, while also reporting symptoms, healthcare use, and work absenteeism. The overall pathogen detection rate was low, with the majority of tests returning negative results, but adenovirus was the most frequently detected pathogen in both assessment periods, a finding that contrasts with its typical underrepresentation in routine surveillance. SARS-CoV-2 was associated with the greatest clinical and economic burden among positive cases, driving the highest rates of healthcare consultations and work absenteeism. The authors conclude that community-based screening using multi-pathogen testing can reveal asymptomatic reservoirs and underreported viral circulation, including a potential co-infecting role for adenovirus, while providing insight into the real-world impact of respiratory viruses on older adults.
items.citation: Anggitakirana M, Nacov JA, Salmanton-García J et al.. Point prevalence assessments of five respiratory viruses in adults ≥ 50 years of age in Germany by multi-pathogen rapid antigen testing on June 1, 2024, and December 15, 2024.. Infection. 2026

items.title: 'No, it is a virus, your body will fight it.' The value of diagnostic testing for managing respiratory viruses in primary care: an observational study from a post-COVID pilot programme.
items.summary: This study examined how laboratory-based polymerase chain reaction testing for respiratory viruses, combined with rapid antigen testing for COVID-19, influenced patient management in a primary care setting during the pandemic. Using electronic medical records from a single urban general practice in New Zealand, researchers analysed data on test results, antibiotic prescribing, patient presentations, and follow-up communications over a ninety-day window before and after testing. They found that a majority of presentations yielded a positive polymerase chain reaction result, yet antibiotic prescribing rates remained high and, notably, patients who tested positive for a respiratory virus were actually more likely to receive antibiotics than those who tested negative. While digital communication methods such as texts and emails were used to convey results to some patients, gaps in result communication and inconsistent prescribing patterns persisted. The authors conclude that broader environmental, clinical, and psychological factors limit the impact of diagnostic testing on prescribing behaviour, and suggest that faster point-of-care technologies may partially, but not fully, address these challenges.
items.citation: Wesley-Smith L, Dowell A, Turner N et al.. 'No, it is a virus, your body will fight it.' The value of diagnostic testing for managing respiratory viruses in primary care: an observational study from a post-COVID pilot programme.. Journal of primary health care. 2026

items.title: Respiratory multi-viral rapid-antigen point-of-care tests in New Zealand primary care: a mixed-methods pilot.
items.summary: This pilot study examined whether multi-viral rapid-antigen point-of-care tests could be feasibly integrated into routine primary care in New Zealand and assessed the attitudes of both patients and clinicians toward their use. Using a prospective mixed-methods design across seven primary care clinics during winter, the researchers administered these tests to patients presenting with acute respiratory symptoms, then collected data through medical record audits, surveys, and qualitative interviews and focus groups. The tests were well-received by all clinicians who participated, with the majority reporting that results influenced their antibiotic prescribing decisions and a subset using them to guide secondary care referrals. Nearly all patients, whether testing positive or negative, expressed a desire to have access to these tests in the future, and those who tested positive reported greater intention to adopt non-pharmaceutical measures to limit transmission. The authors conclude that multi-viral rapid-antigen point-of-care tests are acceptable and practical in primary care settings and could improve management of respiratory illnesses while encouraging behaviour change to reduce spread.
items.citation: Bibby S, Marsh S, Dowell A et al.. Respiratory multi-viral rapid-antigen point-of-care tests in New Zealand primary care: a mixed-methods pilot.. BJGP open. 2026

items.title: Evaluation of the QuickFinder COVID-19/Flu/RSV antigen test for rapid simultaneous detection of SARS-CoV-2, influenza A/B viruses, and respiratory syncytial virus.
items.summary: This study evaluated the diagnostic performance of the QuickFinder COVID-19/Flu/RSV Antigen Test, a lateral flow immunoassay designed to simultaneously detect SARS-CoV-2, influenza A and B viruses, and respiratory syncytial virus from nasopharyngeal swab specimens. Archived clinical specimens were tested in parallel using the QuickFinder and real-time reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction as the reference standard, with cross-reactivity also assessed against a panel of respiratory pathogens. The test demonstrated high sensitivity for SARS-CoV-2 and influenza A, with somewhat lower sensitivity for influenza B and RSV, and achieved perfect specificity for all four targets with no cross-reactivity observed. Sensitivity was consistently strong in specimens with high viral loads but diminished in low viral load samples. The authors conclude that while the QuickFinder is a reliable rapid screening tool for differentiating major respiratory viruses, it should complement rather than replace molecular testing due to its reduced sensitivity when viral loads are low.
items.citation: Kim JA, Kang M, Yu HJ et al.. Evaluation of the QuickFinder COVID-19/Flu/RSV antigen test for rapid simultaneous detection of SARS-CoV-2, influenza A/B viruses, and respiratory syncytial virus.. Diagnostic microbiology and infectious disease. 2026

items.title: No detection of respiratory syncytial virus at one clinic in Japan with rapid immunochromatographic antigen tests for three viruses using the same nasopharyngeal swabs from adult patients
items.summary: This study investigated the disease burden of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection among adult patients at a Japanese clinic by testing nasopharyngeal swabs using rapid immunochromatographic antigen tests capable of detecting SARS-CoV-2, influenza viruses A and B, and RSV simultaneously. Samples were collected from adult patients presenting with acute respiratory infection symptoms over approximately one year. While the tests successfully identified patients positive for SARS-CoV-2 and influenza A and B, no RSV-positive cases were detected among the cohort. Comparing this outcome with previous studies that used polymerase chain reaction testing, which identified RSV in a notable proportion of patients, the RSV-positive rate was significantly lower. The authors conclude that rapid immunochromatographic antigen testing has limited usefulness for diagnosing RSV infections in Japanese adults, likely due to insufficient sensitivity compared with PCR-based methods.
items.citation: Kajiwara N, Tsunetoshi Y, Shiode S. No detection of respiratory syncytial virus at one clinic in Japan with rapid immunochromatographic antigen tests for three viruses using the same nasopharyngeal swabs from adult patients. 2026

items.title: Can exercise affect immune function to increase susceptibility to infection?
items.summary: This debate article examined the contested question of whether exercise itself can suppress immune function and increase susceptibility to infection. The paper structured opposing arguments around several key issues, including whether high-performance athletes are genuinely more infection-prone than the general population, whether exercise independently alters immunity beyond the effects of confounding factors such as sleep disruption, nutritional deficits, travel, and psychological stress, and whether commonly used biomarkers and experimental data adequately capture immune health in those performing arduous exercise. Both sides agreed that regular, moderate-duration exercise appears beneficial for immune defense, particularly in older and chronically ill individuals, while acknowledging that infection burden is notably high among elite athletes and military personnel. A point of consensus was that infection susceptibility is multifactorial in nature, but whether exercise per se causally drives increased infection risk in high-performance populations remains unresolved, with the authors calling for more rigorous empirical research to clarify this fundamental question in exercise immunology.
items.citation: Richard J. Simpson, Richard J. Simpson, Maree Gleeson et al.. Can exercise affect immune function to increase susceptibility to infection?. PubMed. 2026

items.title: Spinal cord injury: Known and possible influences on the immune response to exercise
items.summary: This review paper examined how spinal cord injury affects immune function, with a particular focus on the immune response to exercise. The authors conducted a comprehensive literature search across multiple databases to gather all relevant existing research on exercise immunology in individuals with spinal cord injury across patient, recreationally active, and athlete populations. Spinal cord injury was found to compromise immunity through multiple mechanisms, including reductions in lymphocyte numbers, disrupted autonomic function, and altered catecholamine concentrations, with individuals with tetraplegia being especially affected due to greater loss of sympathetic nervous system control over immune cells. However, some immune responses to exercise, such as increases in natural killer cell cytotoxicity and mucosal immunity changes in those with tetraplegia, appeared independent of catecholamine responses and similar to those seen in able-bodied individuals, suggesting that compensatory mechanisms such as sympathetic reflex activity, receptor hypersensitivity, or neuroendocrine adjustments may offset some injury-related immune deficits. The authors concluded that exercise and rehabilitation can enhance certain immune and autonomic measures following spinal cord injury, and called for further research to clarify the underlying mechanisms and the implications for infection susceptibility.
items.citation: Christof A. Leicht, Victoria L. Goosey‐Tolfrey, Nicolette C. Bishop. Spinal cord injury: Known and possible influences on the immune response to exercise. PubMed. 2026

items.title: Understanding graft-versus-host disease. Preliminary findings regarding the effects of exercise in affected patients
items.summary: This paper examined graft-versus-host disease, a serious multi-systemic complication arising from allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation in which donor immune cells attack host tissues, causing substantial morbidity and reduced physical capacity in long-term survivors. The authors reviewed the pathophysiological mechanisms underlying the disease, with particular attention to its chronic form, alongside available evidence from both animal and human studies on the effects of exercise as an adjunct therapy. Their review indicates that exercise training shows promise for improving physical fitness, potentially enhancing immune function, and reducing fatigue in affected patients. However, the authors conclude that the evidence base remains limited and that further randomized controlled trials focused specifically on this patient population are needed before firm recommendations can be made.
items.citation: Carmen Fiuza‐Luces, Nuria Garatachea, Nathan A. Berger et al.. Understanding graft-versus-host disease. Preliminary findings regarding the effects of exercise in affected patients. PubMed. 2026

items.title: Disorders of Gut–Brain Interaction and the Rome V Process
items.summary: This paper describes the development and scope of the Rome V criteria for disorders of gut–brain interaction, which are gastrointestinal conditions arising from disturbances in motility, visceral sensitivity, mucosal function, gut microbiota, or central nervous system processing. The Rome Foundation undertook a comprehensive revision building on the previous Rome IV framework, incorporating a decade of accumulated basic and clinical research. The update refined diagnostic definitions, introduced new evidence on the roles of diet, the gut microenvironment, pharmacogenomics, and biopsychosocial and sociocultural factors, and generated updated diagnostic algorithms. The process also addressed language issues by reducing imprecise or stigmatizing terminology and placed greater emphasis on the patient illness experience. The result is a broad, evidence-based framework intended to improve both the classification and therapeutic management of these conditions.
items.citation: Douglas A. Drossman, L Chang, Jan Tack. Disorders of Gut–Brain Interaction and the Rome V Process. Gastroenterology. 2026

items.title: Osteoarthritis: molecular pathogenesis and potential therapeutic options
items.summary: This review examines the molecular pathogenesis of osteoarthritis, focusing on the cellular and organelle-level mechanisms that drive disease progression and associated pain. The authors synthesized current knowledge on nociceptive pathways connecting the knee joint to the central nervous system, inflammatory mediator activity, and dysfunction across three organelle systems: mitochondria, lysosomes, and the endoplasmic reticulum. They identify that mitochondrial dysfunction characterized by excessive reactive oxygen species and impaired energy production, lysosomal destabilization leading to chondrocyte apoptosis, and unresolved endoplasmic reticulum stress from compensatory protein overproduction collectively perpetuate cartilage degradation. Building on these mechanistic insights, the review outlines emerging pharmacological strategies that simultaneously target inflammatory cascades, restore organelle homeostasis through approaches such as mitophagy enhancement and lysosomal integrity preservation, and attenuate pain signaling. The authors also highlight organelle-targeted drug delivery systems as a means to improve therapeutic efficacy, proposing a multimodal framework aimed at addressing both the structural and clinical manifestations of osteoarthritis.
items.citation: Yi Zhang, Yanqi Han, Ying Sun et al.. Osteoarthritis: molecular pathogenesis and potential therapeutic options. Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy. 2026

items.title: New approach methodologies for drug discovery
items.summary: This review examines the growing field of new approach methodologies as alternatives to traditional animal-based drug discovery, which has been burdened by high failure rates. The authors survey recent advances in stem cell-based, organoid-based, and computational approaches that now cover the full drug-discovery continuum, from disease modeling and drug design through efficacy testing. The review highlights progress in identifying therapeutic candidates, developing novel models and technologies, and exploring NAMs themselves as potential treatments in preclinical and clinical settings. Key biological, technical, and regulatory bottlenecks limiting broader translational adoption are identified and discussed alongside evolving guidance from major regulatory and funding agencies. The authors conclude by outlining future human-centric discovery pipelines and the translational and societal considerations necessary for the responsible integration of these methodologies into mainstream drug development.
items.citation: Wenqiang Liu, Paul Pang, Catherine A. Wu et al.. New approach methodologies for drug discovery. Cell. 2026

items.title: A Similarity Theorem and Its Breakdown in Atomic Black Hole Accretion
items.summary: This paper investigates the mathematical structure of atomic gas accretion onto a point mass, demonstrating that the governing equations possess an exact similarity symmetry under a simultaneous rescaling of black hole mass and ambient density. The authors prove this rescaling is unique within its class and show it is preserved across time-dependent flows, two-body atomic microphysics, and a broad family of radiation and feedback prescriptions, leaving dimensionless flow profiles and Eddington ratios invariant. They introduce a dimensionless parameter measuring the fractional mass gained per Bondi time, which equivalently describes how fast the Bondi radius expands relative to the local sound speed, and show that sonic dilation marks the boundary where the similarity breaks down. For power-law accretion rates, the system reaches this breakdown after a finite mass increase and a bounded number of additional Bondi times, and the paper argues that canonical hyper-Eddington accretion scenarios have already crossed this threshold. The theorem is shown to unify radiating Bondi accretion and feedback-regulated scalings while identifying the regime where steady-state fixed-mass approximations lose validity.
items.citation: Marcus DuPont. A Similarity Theorem and Its Breakdown in Atomic Black Hole Accretion. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Renormalization-guided inverse blocking for lattice field generation: construction and validation
items.summary: This paper proposes and validates a lattice field configuration generation algorithm that inverts a renormalization-group blocking transformation to efficiently produce configurations across multiple length scales. The method optimizes a blocking transformation under a "perfect blocking" condition so that the coarse-grained lattice can be described by a simple action, then uses a conditional normalizing flow to reconstruct the fine-scale degrees of freedom lost during decimation, followed by a brief rethermalization step to correct residual mismatches. The procedure is applied recursively in a cascade, reusing the same blocking transformation and learned flow to scale up from a small initial ensemble to much larger lattices without retraining. Testing in two-dimensional scalar field theory at criticality demonstrates stable upscaling across several orders of magnitude in lattice volume using only local computational resources. Rethermalization diagnostics confirm that short-distance mismatches relax quickly while long-distance (relevant) mismatches relax slowly, consistent with renormalization-group expectations, and the authors argue the framework extends naturally toward higher-dimensional, gauge, and fermionic theories.
items.citation: Anna Hasenfratz, Ethan T. Neil, Letizia Parato et al.. Renormalization-guided inverse blocking for lattice field generation: construction and validation. arXiv. 2026

items.title: QUEST: A Query and Extraction System for Topics in Asylum Law Application Decisions
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of automatically identifying credibility-related factors in asylum application appeal decisions, which are lengthy and complex legal documents. The authors developed QUEST, a system combining synthetic query generation, topic extraction, and relevance assessment to extract information pertaining to credibility indicators from two datasets of Danish asylum appeals. Beyond standard information retrieval evaluation metrics, they introduced a novel domain-specific evaluation framework that assesses system performance specifically with respect to credibility factors, rather than general relevance. Their findings show that evaluating system performance through credibility-based relevance assessments reveals greater difficulty than standard metrics suggest, highlighting the particular challenge of automating credibility analysis in asylum law contexts.
items.citation: Maria Vlachou, Anna Murphy Høgenhaug, Mohammad N. S. Jahromi et al.. QUEST: A Query and Extraction System for Topics in Asylum Law Application Decisions. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Offline-Verifiable Accountability for Cross-Organization Agent Messaging: A Preserved Evidence-Bundle Approach
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of verifying accountability in cross-organization agent-to-agent workflows when live systems are unavailable, controlled by a single party, or not trusted by all participants. The authors propose a preserved evidence-bundle model in which each workflow event carries all policy-required evidence—including sender authentication, delegation-aware authorization, log commitments, witness-backed checkpoints, and receiver-signed receipts—alongside a policy-controlled offline verifier that assesses evidence sufficiency without relying on transport behavior or platform-specific logs. The verifier is designed to accept only claims explicitly supported by the selected policy profile, providing a principled basis for later audit or dispute review. In a prototype evaluation spanning hundreds of complete workflows and thousands of preserved bundles, the system was tested across multiple policy profiles and evidence configurations, with checkpoint-context anchoring identified as the highest-latency component. Critically, all corrupted or policy-insufficient bundles were rejected with no false acceptances, supporting the approach's suitability for evidence-based accountability in adversarial or multi-party settings.
items.citation: Adil Alshammari, Hayretdin Bahsi. Offline-Verifiable Accountability for Cross-Organization Agent Messaging: A Preserved Evidence-Bundle Approach. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Analysis of Polynomial Threshold Functions on Random Regular Graphs: Computational Complexity of Detecting Noisy Random Lift
items.summary: The paper investigates the computational hardness of a hypothesis testing problem: distinguishing a noisy random lift of a base d-regular graph from a uniformly random d-regular graph. The authors analyze low-degree polynomial threshold functions applied to this detection problem, providing the first such analysis in this setting. As part of their approach, they derive new results on the distribution of short cycle counts in noisy random lifts up to logarithmic lengths, generalizing prior work on random regular graphs and random lifts. The findings contribute to understanding the statistical and computational complexity of detecting structured random graph models, situating the noisy random lift problem within the broader landscape of low-degree hardness results.
items.citation: Xifan Yu. Analysis of Polynomial Threshold Functions on Random Regular Graphs: Computational Complexity of Detecting Noisy Random Lift. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Understanding Venture Capital Syndication in Information Technology Sectors: A Network Formation Perspective
items.summary: This paper investigates how co-investment relationships form among venture capital firms operating in U.S. information technology sectors, examining the structural forces that shape syndication networks over time. Using comprehensive dyadic panel data spanning several decades across hardware, software, and hybrid subsectors, the authors tested seven theoretical mechanisms—including prior collaboration, shared partners, geographic proximity, and organizational similarity—through dyadic logit models and an exponential random graph model of a recent software investor network. The findings consistently identify prior collaboration as the strongest predictor of co-investment link formation, with shared partners, geographic proximity, and organizational-type similarity also positively associated with tie formation, while the influence of domain overlap, prominence, and experience varies by subsector. The whole-network model further confirms that triadic closure and geographic homophily structure the syndication landscape, illustrating how relational persistence and network closure jointly govern how venture capital partnerships coalesce in technology finance.
items.citation: Liheng Tan, Zhengkai Tu, Prasanna Karhade. Understanding Venture Capital Syndication in Information Technology Sectors: A Network Formation Perspective. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Biosensing technologies for foodborne pathogen detection and healthcare: principles, emerging materials, and intelligent platforms
items.summary: This review examines the current state and future directions of biosensing technologies designed to detect priority foodborne pathogens, including *Escherichia coli*, *Salmonella*, and *Listeria monocytogenes*, which continue to represent significant global public health threats. The authors surveyed advances across electrochemical, optical, and microfluidic sensing modalities, with particular attention to how functional nanomaterials, aptamers, nanozymes, and surface engineering strategies have improved sensor sensitivity, specificity, and performance in complex food matrices. A central theme is the integration of artificial intelligence and machine learning into biosensing platforms, enabling intelligent pattern recognition, real-time analytics, and high-throughput multiplexing that transforms conventional detection systems into smart diagnostic tools. The review critically identifies persistent challenges such as matrix interference, bioreceptor instability, manufacturing scalability, and regulatory standardization, while proposing mitigation strategies including ratiometric sensing, microfluidic pre-treatment, explainable AI, and printable electronics. Looking ahead, the authors advocate for self-powered biosensors, modular pathogen panel hubs, blockchain integration, and standardized validation pipelines as pathways toward regulation-ready platforms for next-generation food safety monitoring.
items.citation: Purshottam J. Assudani, Balakrishnan . P., Anny Leema A et al.. Biosensing technologies for foodborne pathogen detection and healthcare: principles, emerging materials, and intelligent platforms. Microchimica Acta. 2026

items.title: Advances in Pathogen Detection by Nanosensors: Biorecognition Strategies, Signal Amplification, and Platform Engineering
items.summary: This review paper examines the current state and emerging advances in nanosensor-based technologies for detecting pathogens in the context of growing infectious disease threats and antimicrobial resistance. The authors systematically survey three converging domains: biorecognition elements such as antibodies, aptamers, bacteriophages, antimicrobial peptides, molecularly imprinted polymers, and lectins that enable selective pathogen identification in complex biological samples; signal amplification strategies leveraging nanomaterials, enzymatic cascades, and isothermal nucleic acid amplification to achieve detection sensitivity down to single-cell and femtomolar levels; and integrated platform engineering combining CRISPR-Cas systems, artificial intelligence, and microfluidics for multiplexed point-of-care diagnostics. The review evaluates these advances against standardized performance metrics including detection limits, assay speed, specificity, and operational simplicity to identify both opportunities for synergy and persistent barriers to clinical translation. The authors conclude that these combined developments establish a strategic framework for next-generation diagnostic platforms capable of transforming infectious disease surveillance and enabling precision-guided treatment decisions.
items.citation: Aroofa Zargul, He Liu, Weiyu Zhang et al.. Advances in Pathogen Detection by Nanosensors: Biorecognition Strategies, Signal Amplification, and Platform Engineering. ACS Nano. 2026

items.title: Advances in tuberculosis diagnostics and biomarkers, 2020-26: scientific evidence, recommendations, gaps, and developmental priorities.
items.summary: This review synthesizes major advances in tuberculosis diagnostics and biomarker research from 2020 to 2025, examining how new evidence has shaped updated WHO policy guidance that consolidates recommendations for detecting tuberculosis disease and drug resistance within a unified framework. Digital chest radiography with computer-aided detection has become a core screening and triage tool, while decentralised molecular diagnosis has expanded through multiple classes of rapid nucleic acid amplification tests, including automated and manual platforms suited to low-resource settings. Novel specimen types such as tongue swabs, expanded use of non-sputum specimens in children, and programmatic innovations like sputum pooling have improved bacteriological confirmation in populations who cannot easily produce sputum, and targeted next-generation sequencing has been endorsed for comprehensive drug-susceptibility testing at reference laboratory level. Host blood transcriptomic signatures demonstrate promising prognostic and triage performance, and proteomic, metabolomic, and other biomarker classes are advancing through evaluation, yet no biomarker has met WHO target product profile criteria for a point-of-care test capable of reliably distinguishing infection from disease, including subclinical tuberculosis. The review concludes that significant gaps in diagnostic performance, implementation, and equity remain, defining priorities for future research and development.
items.citation: Walzl G, McHugh TD, Chakaya J et al.. Advances in tuberculosis diagnostics and biomarkers, 2020-26: scientific evidence, recommendations, gaps, and developmental priorities.. The Lancet. Microbe. 2027

items.title: Molecular Diagnostics of Infectious Diseases.
items.summary: This review paper examines the current landscape of molecular diagnostic technologies applied to the detection and characterization of infectious disease pathogens. The paper covers nucleic acid amplification approaches, including polymerase chain reaction variants optimized for speed, quantification, automation, and point-of-care use, as well as isothermal amplification methods that operate without thermal cycling equipment and are therefore suited to decentralized testing settings. CRISPR-based detection systems, which function at constant temperature and are often coupled with isothermal amplification, are presented as an emerging diagnostic strategy. Next-generation sequencing is described as a high-throughput approach capable of identifying novel pathogens, diagnosing complex infections, tracking outbreak transmission, monitoring pathogen evolution, and analyzing microbiomes as potential disease biomarkers. The authors conclude that future advances in molecular diagnostics will arise from integrating these complementary technologies into hybrid platforms that address the current limitations of each individual method.
items.citation: Takata M, Chikumi H, Yoshifuji A. Molecular Diagnostics of Infectious Diseases.. Yonago acta medica. 2026

items.title: SARS-CoV-2 Point-of-Care Testing Modalities: Integrating Molecular, Immunological, Biosensor, and AI Approaches.
items.summary: This review examined the landscape of point-of-care testing technologies developed for COVID-19 diagnosis, motivated by the pandemic's demonstration of the urgent need for rapid, decentralized diagnostic tools. The authors conducted a structured search of major scientific databases spanning the duration of the pandemic to evaluate molecular assays, antigen and antibody tests, biosensor platforms, and artificial intelligence-assisted diagnostic approaches. Molecular methods such as rapid RT-PCR, LAMP, and CRISPR-based technologies were found to offer high sensitivity and specificity suitable for decentralized use, while antigen tests provided fast and affordable screening with performance that varies by viral load, symptom timing, and variant. Antibody-based testing was deemed most useful for seroprevalence and immune monitoring rather than acute infection detection, and biosensor and AI-enabled systems showed promise but remained largely at prototype or early-validation stages requiring further clinical assessment. The review concludes that no single testing modality is universally optimal, and that combining complementary approaches alongside advances in multiplexing, digital connectivity, and variant-resilient detection will strengthen both COVID-19 management and future infectious disease preparedness.
items.citation: Hetta HF, Ahmed R, Haseeb A et al.. SARS-CoV-2 Point-of-Care Testing Modalities: Integrating Molecular, Immunological, Biosensor, and AI Approaches.. Diagnostics (Basel, Switzerland). 2026

items.title: AI-Enhanced Point-of-Care Diagnostics for Infectious Diseases in Resource-Limited Settings: A Scoping Review.
items.summary: This scoping review systematically mapped the landscape of artificial intelligence–enhanced point-of-care and rapid diagnostic technologies for infectious diseases in resource-limited settings, examining the extent of research, disease coverage, geographic representation, and validation rigor. Following established scoping review methodology and searching five major databases, the authors identified and analyzed over two hundred eligible studies published between early 2015 and early 2026. The field was found to be growing rapidly, though research was heavily concentrated on a narrow triad of diseases—COVID-19, malaria, and tuberculosis—while neglected tropical diseases were markedly underrepresented, and convolutional neural networks were the dominant artificial intelligence approach across diagnostic modalities. A critical finding was that the vast majority of studies lacked prospective field validation, with only a small fraction reporting this rigorous standard, and geographic coverage skewed toward East Africa and South Asia while West Africa and Latin America were underrepresented. The authors conclude that despite rapid growth, the field faces fundamental gaps in validation quality, disease equity, and geographic inclusivity, and they call for future work to prioritize real-world field validation, broaden disease focus, and meaningfully involve end-user communities from the earliest stages of research design.
items.venue: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
items.citation: Farquhar H. AI-Enhanced Point-of-Care Diagnostics for Infectious Diseases in Resource-Limited Settings: A Scoping Review.. Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH. 2026

items.title: Concordance Between Fingerprick and Venous Whole Blood CD4 Counts Using the Visitect CD4 Advanced disease platform.
items.summary: This study evaluated whether fingerprick blood samples could serve as a reliable alternative to venous whole blood samples for CD4 testing using the Visitect CD4 Advanced Disease platform, a rapid semi-quantitative assay that classifies CD4 counts as above or below a clinically important threshold. The researchers conducted a prospective validation study directly comparing results obtained from the two blood collection methods on the same platform. They found a very high level of agreement between fingerprick and venous whole blood results, supporting the conclusion that fingerprick sampling with this assay could function as a dependable point-of-care diagnostic tool in resource-limited settings where conventional venous blood collection is not readily accessible.
items.citation: Adzemovic T, Nalintya E, Onencan P et al.. Concordance Between Fingerprick and Venous Whole Blood CD4 Counts Using the Visitect CD4 Advanced disease platform.. The Journal of infectious diseases. 2026

items.title: An integrated centrifugal microfluidic CRISPR-based diagnostics platform for multiplexed point-of-care testing of respiratory pathogens.
items.summary: The paper developed and validated a centrifugal microfluidic diagnostic platform called iCARD for multiplexed point-of-care detection of respiratory pathogens. The system integrates CRISPR/Cas13a chemistry with lyophilized reagents pre-loaded onto a spinning disc, paired with a portable fluorescence analyzer, and uses a novel resin-based nucleic acid purification method for throat swab samples. The platform can simultaneously screen six respiratory pathogens across four independent samples in a single automated run. Analytical testing confirmed single-copy-level sensitivity with no cross-reactivity, and clinical validation using retrospective patient samples demonstrated very high diagnostic sensitivity and perfect specificity. The authors conclude that iCARD offers a robust, accurate, and high-throughput solution for decentralized molecular diagnostics and epidemiological surveillance.
items.citation: Li L, Wei H, Wei M et al.. An integrated centrifugal microfluidic CRISPR-based diagnostics platform for multiplexed point-of-care testing of respiratory pathogens.. Biosensors & bioelectronics. 2026

items.title: EULAR recommendations for the management of rheumatoid arthritis with synthetic and biologic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs: 2025 update
items.summary: This paper presents the updated clinical recommendations from a major European rheumatology alliance for managing rheumatoid arthritis using synthetic and biologic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs. An international task force conducted systematic literature reviews on drug safety and efficacy, then used a structured voting process to revise and consolidate guidance from the previous iteration. The updated framework distilled recommendations into a streamlined set of principles covering conventional synthetic agents, glucocorticoids, biologic drugs, and targeted synthetic drugs including Janus kinase inhibitors. The recommendations follow a treat-to-target strategy beginning with methotrexate plus short-term glucocorticoids, escalating to biologic agents after insufficient response, with Janus kinase inhibitors considered as an alternative after careful evaluation of cardiovascular, malignancy, and thromboembolic risks. The guidance also addresses sequencing after treatment failure, tapering strategies in sustained remission, and cost considerations, with high levels of evidence and agreement achieved for most recommendations.
items.citation: Josef S. Smolen, Christopher J. Edwards, Victoria Konzett et al.. EULAR recommendations for the management of rheumatoid arthritis with synthetic and biologic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs: 2025 update. Annals of the Rheumatic Diseases. 2026
