items.title: Antimicrobial Resistance in the Food Chain: Bridging Knowledge Gaps for Effective Detection and Control
items.summary: This review examines antimicrobial resistance within the food chain as a critical public health concern, adopting a One Health framework that connects animals, the environment, and humans. The authors analyze the major drivers of resistance spread across animal agriculture, aquaculture, and food processing, while evaluating both established and emerging detection methodologies. They contrast traditional culture-based phenotypic testing against rapid molecular approaches such as whole genome sequencing, metagenomics, and CRISPR-based diagnostics, identifying persistent challenges including matrix interference, the viable but non-culturable bacterial state, and disconnects between genotype and phenotype. The review also describes integrated mitigation strategies spanning antimicrobial stewardship on farms, biofilm control, and consumer hygiene practices. The authors conclude that bridging technical and regulatory gaps in surveillance is essential to developing effective interventions and securing a safer food system.
items.citation: Emílio Gomes, Tomás Gonçalves Mesquita, Patrícia Serra et al.. Antimicrobial Resistance in the Food Chain: Bridging Knowledge Gaps for Effective Detection and Control. Antibiotics. 2026

items.title: The analysis of natural gemstones and their synthetic counterparts using analytical spectroscopy methods
items.summary: This paper investigated the use of Raman spectroscopy to distinguish natural gemstones from their synthetic counterparts, focusing on ruby, sapphire, emerald, and spinel as major commercial gems. The researchers evaluated both a laboratory Raman spectrometer equipped with two different lasers and a portable Raman system, applying these tools to differentiate gems produced by various manufacturing methods and to determine geographic origin. The laboratory instrument demonstrated reliable and repeatable results, successfully distinguishing natural from synthetic gemstones and determining origin among stones of the same colour, while emerald analysis required a specific laser wavelength. The portable system could differentiate between broad stone types but lacked the sensitivity needed to separate natural from synthetic specimens. The study concludes that Raman spectroscopy offers a non-destructive, efficient analytical approach to address the growing challenge of identifying increasingly sophisticated laboratory-grown gemstones in the jewellery market.
items.citation: Raabell Shah. The analysis of natural gemstones and their synthetic counterparts using analytical spectroscopy methods. Research Output (Edinburgh Napier University). 2026

items.title: Varicella Zoster Virus Infection: Clinical Features, Molecular Pathogenesis, Treatment, and Prevention
items.summary: This review examines varicella zoster virus, a human herpesvirus that establishes lifelong latency and reactivates to cause herpes zoster, a condition whose burden grows substantially in aging and immunocompromised populations. The authors synthesize existing knowledge spanning viral epidemiology, structure, and life cycle alongside the clinical manifestations of herpes zoster, which extend beyond skin disease to include postherpetic neuralgia, neurological complications, and systemic involvement. Particular attention is given to the molecular mechanisms underlying latency, reactivation, and immune evasion, as well as the virus-induced neuronal injury that drives long-term sequelae. The review also surveys advances in diagnostic technologies and therapeutic strategies targeting viral replication and inflammatory complications, in addition to current preventive approaches. By integrating mechanistic insights with clinical management considerations, the authors identify key gaps and emerging directions aimed at translating fundamental discoveries into more comprehensive and effective interventions against herpes zoster.
items.citation: Lei Peng, Honghao Song, Tianying Li et al.. Varicella Zoster Virus Infection: Clinical Features, Molecular Pathogenesis, Treatment, and Prevention. MedComm. 2026

items.title: Invisible Agents, Uninformed Patients: Towards Responsible Deployment Of Autonomous AI Diagnostic Agents In Sub-Saharan Africa
items.summary: This paper examines the deployment of autonomous AI diagnostic agents across eHealth platforms in sub-Saharan Africa, focusing on the ethical and governance challenges that arise when such systems operate without adequate patient awareness or regulatory oversight. The authors identify a structural accountability gap rooted in the fact that existing frameworks for AI transparency and explainability in healthcare are largely clinician-centered and presuppose regulatory conditions absent in low-resource settings, leaving patients uninformed about the autonomous nature of the systems making decisions about their care. Drawing on documented real-world deployments involving tuberculosis detection, diabetic retinopathy screening, and mobile health chatbot triage in Tanzania, Zambia, and Ghana, the paper demonstrates that these governance deficiencies are already manifesting in active systems across the region. In response, the authors synthesize literature on informed consent, algorithmic accountability, and explainable AI to propose three foundational principles: agent-aware informed consent, human override as a structural requirement, and contextually adapted explainability. Together, these principles are presented as a practical minimum standard for developers, health administrators, and policymakers operating in contexts where formal AI regulation remains nascent.
items.citation: Percy Brown, Kweku Yamoah. Invisible Agents, Uninformed Patients: Towards Responsible Deployment Of Autonomous AI Diagnostic Agents In Sub-Saharan Africa. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Beyond Fault Localization: A Trajectory-Level Study of LLM Agents for Microservice Root Cause Analysis
items.summary: This paper investigates automated root cause analysis (RCA) for microservice systems, arguing that existing evaluations focused solely on whether an agent correctly identifies the responsible service are insufficient to capture diagnostic quality. The authors developed a trajectory-level evaluation framework that assesses agent diagnostic processes against manually curated fault-propagation paths, analyzing a large collection of diagnostic trajectories from a public benchmark to characterize how agents investigate faults and use retrieved telemetry. They found a fundamental disconnect between answer correctness and diagnostic quality, revealing that an agent can correctly localize a fault source while failing to reconstruct how the fault propagated through the system. Their analysis identified recurring failure modes including omission of decisive evidence, misinterpretation of retrieved evidence, and unsupported inference, which they organized into a taxonomy. Building on these findings, they developed DiagGuard, a two-stage architecture that grounds diagnoses in available observations before localization and then audits the result, demonstrating meaningful improvement in localization accuracy in an independent evaluation setting.
items.citation: Qisheng Lu, Aoyang Fang, Junjielong Xu et al.. Beyond Fault Localization: A Trajectory-Level Study of LLM Agents for Microservice Root Cause Analysis. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Fault Diagnosis of Dynamic Systems Under Unknown Operating Conditions: A Condition-Guided Selective Adaptation Approach
items.summary: The paper addresses the challenge of diagnosing faults in dynamic industrial systems when the operating conditions encountered during deployment differ from those seen during training, a problem that causes distribution shift and degrades model performance. The authors propose a condition-guided selective adaptation framework that combines an offline training phase, where continuous operating-condition adversarial learning with progressive training improves model generalization, with an online deployment phase that uses residual operating-condition responses to identify reliable unlabeled samples from streaming data for model updating. Experiments on real-world gearbox and motor datasets show that the proposed approach outperforms existing state-of-the-art fault diagnosis methods in accuracy while keeping test-time computational costs relatively low, suggesting practical viability for industrial deployment.
items.citation: Jiaming Liu, Zeyi Liu, Hongshuo Zhao et al.. Fault Diagnosis of Dynamic Systems Under Unknown Operating Conditions: A Condition-Guided Selective Adaptation Approach. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Event-Time Confounding Under Bursty Human Dynamics
items.summary: This paper investigates a systematic methodological flaw in studies of digital behavior that measure the effect of user-initiated events—such as opening an AI assistant or clicking a recommendation—by comparing activity before and after the event. The core problem identified is that because users choose when to initiate these events, the chosen moment tends to fall within an already-ongoing burst of activity, meaning post-event activity may simply reflect the continuation of that episode rather than any causal response to the event. Using web logs spanning multiple digital surfaces, the authors demonstrate that activity increases broadly before these events and peaks prior to the moment of alignment, consistent with episode-selection bias rather than a treatment effect. To quantify the bias, they exploit known-null timestamps that causally produce no effect, finding that these null events still reproduce a substantial fraction of the excess post-event activity observed for real events, with the confounding concentrated at detectably active moments and absent at quiet ones. The authors formalize the bias theoretically, show why common controls like user fixed effects and activity matching are insufficient because the confound is within-user and time-varying, and provide diagnostic tools and benchmarks to help researchers detect and account for this problem.
items.citation: Michael Iannelli, Alan Ai. Event-Time Confounding Under Bursty Human Dynamics. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Comprehensive Regression and Diagnostics for Non-Negative Data Using the BCSreg Package
items.summary: This paper introduces a software package for fitting flexible regression models to non-negative data that exhibit high skewness, heavy tails, or a mixture of zero and positive values, characteristics that standard regression approaches handle poorly. The authors developed the BCSreg package for R, which implements Box-Cox symmetric and log-symmetric regression models along with their zero-adjusted extensions for mixed discrete-continuous responses. The package allows simultaneous modelling of multiple distributional parameters, including a scale parameter tied to response quantiles, relative dispersion, and the probability of zero occurrences, all specified through a unified multi-part formula interface. A comprehensive suite of diagnostic tools is also provided, encompassing randomized quantile residuals, simulated envelopes, and influence diagnostics tailored to these model classes. The package's functionality is demonstrated through applications to real datasets.
items.citation: Francisco F. Queiroz, Rodrigo M. R. de Medeiros. Comprehensive Regression and Diagnostics for Non-Negative Data Using the BCSreg Package. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Oblique Bragg-Doppler scattering at relativistic grating created by backward Raman amplification in hydrogen
items.summary: This paper reports the first experimental observation of relativistic Bragg-Doppler reflection, a phenomenon in which light scatters off a rapidly moving phase grating. The grating was generated inside hydrogen-filled hollow-core fibre through seeded backward stimulated Raman scattering, producing a coherent molecular vibration wave travelling at a substantial fraction of the speed of light. When a probe beam was directed at the moving grating at the appropriate generalized Bragg angle, it reflected with a large frequency shift equal to the molecular vibration frequency. The effect was found to be unidirectional because phase-matching fails when the probe direction is reversed, making the system function as an extremely high-frequency optical shifter. The authors suggest this approach could enable frequency conversion across a broad spectral range, including difficult ultraviolet regions, and may have applications in quantum optics and the study of coherence wave dynamics.
items.citation: Wenhong Lai, Jiapeng Huang, Haozhe Guo et al.. Oblique Bragg-Doppler scattering at relativistic grating created by backward Raman amplification in hydrogen. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Mechanism-informed diagnostic accuracy of blood biomarkers for sepsis-associated encephalopathy: a systematic review and Bayesian diagnostic network meta-analysis.
items.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis investigated the diagnostic accuracy of blood biomarkers for sepsis-associated encephalopathy, a serious form of acute brain dysfunction occurring in sepsis patients. The researchers conducted a comprehensive literature search across multiple databases and applied a Bayesian diagnostic network meta-analysis to compare and rank biomarkers spanning the biological cascade from innate immune activation through blood-brain barrier disruption, glial response, and neuronal injury. Blood-brain barrier and glial markers such as GFAP and S100β demonstrated more balanced diagnostic discrimination than classic neuronal injury markers, while upstream immune and alarmin candidates ranked highest in Bayesian comparative analysis, though several top-ranked biomarkers were supported by only single studies. The authors identified that diagnostic performance varied substantially depending on how sepsis-associated encephalopathy was defined and when biomarker sampling occurred relative to clinical anchor events, and critically, few studies assessed whether biomarkers provided diagnostic value beyond established clinical predictors such as illness severity scores. The findings are considered hypothesis-generating, with the authors calling for prospective head-to-head validation of mechanism-staged biomarker panels under standardized phenotyping and sampling protocols to determine their incremental clinical utility.
items.citation: Zhang Q, Zhu R, Li Y et al.. Mechanism-informed diagnostic accuracy of blood biomarkers for sepsis-associated encephalopathy: a systematic review and Bayesian diagnostic network meta-analysis.. Frontiers in molecular neuroscience. 2026

items.title: Plasma and urinary sTREM-1 as biomarkers of sepsis-associated acute kidney injury in critically Ill children.
items.summary: This prospective observational study investigated whether plasma and urinary levels of soluble triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells-1 (sTREM-1) could serve as early biomarkers for sepsis-associated acute kidney injury in critically ill children admitted to a pediatric intensive care unit. Researchers measured sTREM-1 levels at the time of sepsis diagnosis and again at the point of acute kidney injury diagnosis in those who developed it, using established pediatric scoring criteria to define both conditions. Both plasma and urinary sTREM-1 concentrations were significantly elevated in children who subsequently developed sepsis-associated acute kidney injury compared to those who did not, and both markers rose further once acute kidney injury was established. Receiver operating characteristic analyses indicated moderate diagnostic accuracy for plasma sTREM-1 and somewhat lower accuracy for urinary sTREM-1, with urinary sTREM-1 additionally demonstrating prognostic value for mortality. The authors conclude that measuring sTREM-1 at sepsis onset may facilitate earlier risk stratification for acute kidney injury than conventional creatinine- and urine output-based criteria alone.
items.citation: Magdy SM, El-Gawaad TA, Hussein FA et al.. Plasma and urinary sTREM-1 as biomarkers of sepsis-associated acute kidney injury in critically Ill children.. European journal of pediatrics. 2026

items.title: Diagnostic value of cystatin C in acute kidney injury among patients with sepsis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of cystatin C (CysC) for the early detection of acute kidney injury in patients with sepsis. The authors systematically searched electronic databases, assessed study quality using a standardized diagnostic accuracy tool, and applied a random-effects model to pool sensitivity, specificity, and area under the summary receiver operating characteristic curve across included studies. Cystatin C demonstrated good overall diagnostic performance for sepsis-associated acute kidney injury, and subgroup analyses showed that studies applying Sepsis 3.0 diagnostic criteria achieved higher specificity and diagnostic odds ratios with less heterogeneity. Combining cystatin C with other biomarkers further enhanced diagnostic accuracy. The authors conclude that cystatin C is a promising early diagnostic biomarker for sepsis-associated acute kidney injury and has potential utility in clinical practice, though heterogeneity among included studies remains a limitation.
items.citation: Cheng L, Zhang B, Hu X et al.. Diagnostic value of cystatin C in acute kidney injury among patients with sepsis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.. Frontiers in medicine. 2026

items.title: Pancreatic Stone Protein as an Emerging Biomarker in Paediatric Nosocomial and Postoperative Sepsis: An Integrative Review of Diagnostic and Prognostic Performance.
items.summary: This integrative review examined the diagnostic and prognostic utility of pancreatic stone protein (PSP) as a biomarker for sepsis in paediatric patients, particularly in nosocomial and postoperative contexts where distinguishing infectious from sterile inflammation is clinically difficult. The authors conducted a structured narrative review of published literature, screening identified articles and ultimately synthesizing findings from those meeting inclusion criteria. Across the analyzed studies, PSP levels were found to rise significantly in children with sepsis compared to those with non-infectious systemic inflammation, and elevated PSP was associated with bacteraemia, organ dysfunction, and mortality. PSP demonstrated diagnostic performance comparable to or exceeding that of conventional markers such as C-reactive protein and procalcitonin, including in neonatal and other high-risk populations. The review concludes that PSP is a promising early biomarker for paediatric sepsis detection and risk stratification, but calls for larger multicentre prospective studies and integration of PSP into multimarker diagnostic frameworks to address variability across existing evidence.
items.citation: Ramírez Quintana A, Gaman EL, Badea M et al.. Pancreatic Stone Protein as an Emerging Biomarker in Paediatric Nosocomial and Postoperative Sepsis: An Integrative Review of Diagnostic and Prognostic Performance.. International journal of molecular sciences. 2026

items.title: Early diagnostic accuracy of immature platelet fraction for sepsis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis examined whether the immature platelet fraction, a measure of bone marrow thrombopoietic activity obtainable through routine blood analysis, could serve as an early diagnostic biomarker for sepsis. The authors searched major medical databases and identified studies meeting their inclusion criteria, then pooled data to calculate summary diagnostic performance metrics including sensitivity, specificity, and diagnostic odds ratio, with a subgroup analysis focused on adult populations. The meta-analysis found that the immature platelet fraction demonstrated only moderate diagnostic accuracy for sepsis, with pooled sensitivity and specificity both around seventy percent and moderate heterogeneity across the included studies. The authors conclude that while the immature platelet fraction may function as a complementary biomarker alongside other indicators, the small number of qualifying studies and methodological inconsistencies limit confidence in these estimates. They call for larger, prospective, and standardized studies before the measure can be recommended for routine clinical use in sepsis diagnosis.
items.citation: Wiranata S, Manuaba IBAP, Supadmanaba IGP et al.. Early diagnostic accuracy of immature platelet fraction for sepsis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.. Hematology, transfusion and cell therapy. 2026

items.title: Diagnostic performance of interleukin-27 and C-reactive protein in neonatal sepsis: an updated systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated and compared the diagnostic accuracy of interleukin-27 (IL-27) and C-reactive protein (CRP) as biomarkers for neonatal sepsis, a condition where consistent diagnostic evidence has been lacking. Following PRISMA guidelines, the authors searched major medical databases spanning nearly three decades and included controlled studies of acceptable methodological quality involving several hundred neonates. Pooled analysis using summary receiver operating characteristic curves demonstrated that IL-27 achieved higher sensitivity and specificity than CRP for identifying neonatal sepsis, with the area under the curve for IL-27 exceeding that of CRP. The authors conclude that IL-27 demonstrates superior diagnostic accuracy compared to CRP and may serve as a more reliable biomarker for the early and accurate clinical diagnosis of neonatal sepsis.
items.citation: Liu W, Zhang Y, Liu W et al.. Diagnostic performance of interleukin-27 and C-reactive protein in neonatal sepsis: an updated systematic review and meta-analysis.. Frontiers in pediatrics. 2026

items.title: Surviving Sepsis Campaign: International Guidelines for Management of Sepsis and Septic Shock 2026
items.summary: This paper presents the 2026 Surviving Sepsis Campaign international clinical practice guidelines for the management of sepsis and septic shock in adults. The guidelines were developed by a large, geographically diverse multidisciplinary committee, including patient and family advisors, using the GRADE methodology and an Evidence to Decision framework to evaluate and synthesize the available evidence across clinical domains including screening, infection management, hemodynamics, respiratory support, adjunctive therapies, and goals of care. The recommendations span the hospital, immediate prehospital, and post-hospital settings, and incorporate principles of antimicrobial stewardship to balance early treatment with responsible antibiotic use. The resulting statements range from strong recommendations where evidence was sufficient and consistent to conditional recommendations and best practice statements where certainty was lower or context-dependent, with explicit attention to applicability in low- and middle-income country settings. The guidelines aim to provide clinicians and health systems with actionable, evidence-based guidance to improve early identification and treatment of sepsis and thereby reduce its substantial global mortality and long-term morbidity burden.
items.citation: Hallie C. Prescott, Massimo Antonelli, Waleed Alhazzani et al.. Surviving Sepsis Campaign: International Guidelines for Management of Sepsis and Septic Shock 2026. Critical Care Medicine. 2026

items.title: The NLRP3 Inflammasome: Mechanisms of Activation, Regulation, and Therapeutic Opportunities
items.summary: This review paper examines the NLRP3 inflammasome, a key signaling platform of the innate immune system that detects a wide range of microbial, metabolic, and environmental danger signals. The authors synthesize current knowledge on the molecular mechanisms driving NLRP3 activation, including ion flux, mitochondrial damage, lysosomal rupture, reactive oxygen species, and post-translational modifications, as well as the negative regulatory pathways that maintain inflammasome homeostasis. Activation of this complex leads to caspase-1-dependent maturation of the pro-inflammatory cytokines IL-1β and IL-18 and triggers pyroptotic cell death, processes whose dysregulation has been linked to autoinflammatory syndromes, metabolic and cardiovascular diseases, neurodegeneration, and cancer. The review further surveys therapeutic strategies targeting NLRP3, encompassing direct inhibitors, allosteric modulators, biologics, and repurposed drugs, and evaluates their translational potential. The authors conclude that a deeper understanding of the balance between NLRP3 activation and inhibition opens promising avenues for treating a broad spectrum of inflammatory and immune-related diseases.
items.citation: Chan Zou, Shilong Jiang, Hui Li et al.. The NLRP3 Inflammasome: Mechanisms of Activation, Regulation, and Therapeutic Opportunities. MedComm. 2026

items.title: Exosomal bioactive molecules: molecular regulation, functional heterogeneity, and translational implications in disease diagnostics and therapeutics
items.summary: This review examines exosomes, nanoscale extracellular vesicles that mediate intercellular communication by carrying diverse bioactive cargo including proteins, lipids, and nucleic acids. The authors synthesize current understanding of the molecular machinery governing exosome biogenesis and cargo loading, with particular attention to how ESCRT complexes, lipid domains, RNA-binding proteins, and post-translational modifications collectively drive selective cargo enrichment and functional heterogeneity. The review surveys state-of-the-art omics platforms and machine learning–based tools used to decode exosomal content, and evaluates their diagnostic utility as liquid biopsies across cancer, metabolic, and neurodegenerative diseases. Therapeutic applications of both native and engineered exosomes are discussed, encompassing targeted drug delivery, wound healing, and neuroregeneration, alongside an overview of ongoing clinical trials. The authors also identify persistent translational barriers—including isolation protocol variability, cargo inconsistency, and regulatory constraints—and propose that emerging strategies such as synthetic exosome mimetics and AI-driven diagnostics will advance exosome-based precision medicine.
items.citation: Victor U. Chigozie. Exosomal bioactive molecules: molecular regulation, functional heterogeneity, and translational implications in disease diagnostics and therapeutics. Clinical and Experimental Medicine. 2026

items.title: A systematic literature review on the effects of exercise on human Toll-like receptor expression
items.summary: This systematic review examined how different forms of exercise affect the expression of Toll-like receptors (TLRs), immune cell proteins that trigger inflammatory signalling cascades and have been implicated in chronic low-grade inflammation associated with sedentary behaviour and non-communicable diseases. The authors searched multiple databases for human studies using exercise as an isolated intervention, ultimately including dozens of articles spanning acute and chronic resistance, aerobic, and combined exercise modalities. They found that acute resistance exercise tended to upregulate TLR expression, while acute aerobic exercise was more likely to produce neutral or downregulatory effects, particularly in healthy individuals. Chronic resistance and combined training programs predominantly left TLR levels unchanged or reduced them, whereas chronic aerobic exercise produced mixed results with most measurements showing no significant change. The authors conclude that an exercise–TLR relationship exists and appears to depend on exercise type and context, but caution that substantial heterogeneity in study designs limits firm conclusions and that further research is needed to clarify the underlying mechanisms and clinical implications.
items.citation: Kasper Favere, Matthias Bosman, Peter Delputte et al.. A systematic literature review on the effects of exercise on human Toll-like receptor expression. PubMed. 2026

items.title: Natural-Language Workflows Are Not Software Yet: Artifact-Driven Compilation for Reliable Agent Execution
items.summary: This paper investigates the unreliability of natural-language workflows when used to guide AI agent execution, identifying that implicit data dependencies and complex control logic cause agents to fail under context pressure. The authors propose Artic, a compiler that transforms natural-language workflows into structured, artifact-driven representations where each step explicitly declares the data it reads and writes, with constraints and control transfers made explicit. The compiler identifies problematic steps with excessive state dependencies or difficult branching logic and refines them through constrained optimization, while validating the transformation using faithfulness checking decomposed into local obligations and scenario-based dry runs. Evaluated across a large set of problem instances drawn from real-world domain workflows, Artic substantially improves task resolution rates compared to executing original text workflows, and also produces markedly more consistent behavior across different language models and repeated executions.
items.citation: Xiangzhe Xu, Hanxi Guo, Guangyu Shen et al.. Natural-Language Workflows Are Not Software Yet: Artifact-Driven Compilation for Reliable Agent Execution. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Anatomy-Informed Neural Networks: Encoding Anatomic Priors in Loss and Architecture, with an SE(3) Formulation of Guidewire-Induced Aortoiliac Deformation
items.summary: This paper introduces Anatomy-Informed Neural Networks (AINN), a framework that encodes anatomical knowledge into deep learning models either as soft penalty terms in the loss function or as hard constraints built directly into the network architecture, analogous to how physics-informed neural networks incorporate physical laws. The approach is developed and demonstrated on a clinically relevant problem: predicting how the aortoiliac arterial tree deforms when a stiff guidewire is inserted endoluminally, which is important for aortic surgery and autonomous endovascular navigation. The vessel centerline and wire path are represented as curves of frames in the SE(3) Lie group, and a Cosserat-rod wire model is coupled to an anatomically anchored vessel through a contact inequality constraint, with the predicted deformation found as a constrained minimizer of coupled elastic energy. Supervision uses a Wasserstein-2 optimal-transport loss between predicted angiographic projections and observed two-dimensional angiograms, enabling three-dimensional predictions to be trained from two-dimensional images. Importantly, no network is actually trained in this work; the paper establishes and verifies the mechanical and geometric framework in silico, with future work planned to transfer the model to real CT data and assess whether anatomical priors improve accuracy and reduce data requirements.
items.citation: David P. Stonko. Anatomy-Informed Neural Networks: Encoding Anatomic Priors in Loss and Architecture, with an SE(3) Formulation of Guidewire-Induced Aortoiliac Deformation. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Invisible Agents, Uninformed Patients: Towards Responsible Deployment Of Autonomous AI Diagnostic Agents In Sub-Saharan Africa
items.summary: This paper examines the ethical and governance challenges arising from the deployment of autonomous AI diagnostic agents across eHealth platforms in sub-Saharan Africa, where regulatory infrastructure has not kept pace with technological adoption. The authors argue that existing frameworks for AI accountability, transparency, and explainability are predominantly clinician-centered and assume regulatory conditions that do not apply in low-resource settings, leaving a structural accountability gap rooted in patients being largely unaware that autonomous systems are involved in their care. Drawing on documented cases of AI deployment for tuberculosis detection, diabetic retinopathy screening, and mobile health chatbot triage across Tanzania, Zambia, and Ghana, the paper demonstrates that these gaps are already manifest in active systems. In response, the authors synthesize literature on informed consent, algorithmic accountability, and explainable AI to propose three foundational principles: agent-aware informed consent, human override as a structural requirement, and contextually adapted explainability. Together, these principles are offered as a practical minimum standard for developers, health administrators, and policymakers operating in contexts where formal AI regulation remains nascent.
items.citation: Percy Brown, Kweku Yamoah. Invisible Agents, Uninformed Patients: Towards Responsible Deployment Of Autonomous AI Diagnostic Agents In Sub-Saharan Africa. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Hypothesis testing between quantum ensembles
items.summary: This paper studies the problem of distinguishing between quantum state ensembles, which are collections of quantum states paired with classical labels that carry richer operational information than their average density operators alone. The authors formulate binary hypothesis testing for finite quantum ensembles and derive fundamental limits on the achievable error probability. By analyzing the joint sampled state conditioned on an observed label pattern, they show it can be characterized through power-weighted ensemble moments, which enables derivation of the Bayes-optimal measurement and exact finite-sample error, demonstrating that discrimination depends on the full moment hierarchy up to the number of samples taken. In the many-sample regime, they derive Chernoff-type bounds and exact error exponents, finding that for finite uniform pure-state designs with large design order, the maximal discrimination exponent decays inversely as the square of the design order, while achieving fixed-error discrimination requires a number of samples that grows as the square of the design order. These results are applied to optical communication and the theory of quantum designs, providing operational benchmarks for how well such structured ensembles can be distinguished.
items.citation: Jian Yao, Quntao Zhuang. Hypothesis testing between quantum ensembles. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Beyond Fault Localization: A Trajectory-Level Study of LLM Agents for Microservice Root Cause Analysis
items.summary: This paper investigates automated root cause analysis (RCA) for microservice systems, arguing that conventional evaluations focused solely on whether an agent correctly identifies the responsible service are insufficient because they obscure the quality of the diagnostic reasoning and fault-propagation reconstruction. The authors developed a trajectory-level evaluation framework that assesses agent diagnostic processes against manually curated fault-propagation paths, applying it to analyze thousands of diagnostic trajectories from a public benchmark to characterize investigative behavior and telemetry usage. They found a systematic disconnect between answer correctness and diagnostic quality, where agents can identify the correct fault source while failing to trace how the fault propagated, and identified recurring failure modes including omission of decisive evidence, misinterpretation of retrieved telemetry, and unsupported inference. Building on this taxonomy, they proposed DiagGuard, a two-stage architecture that grounds diagnosis in available observations before localization and then audits the result against retrieved evidence. Applied in an independent setting with a different model and benchmark, DiagGuard meaningfully improved top-one accuracy, demonstrating that trajectory-level evaluation reveals limitations hidden by endpoint metrics and offers practical guidance for improving automated RCA systems.
items.citation: Qisheng Lu, Aoyang Fang, Junjielong Xu et al.. Beyond Fault Localization: A Trajectory-Level Study of LLM Agents for Microservice Root Cause Analysis. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Rethinking Expressivity and Efficiency in Test-Time Training
items.summary: This paper addresses a fundamental tension in Test-Time Training approaches to long-context sequence modeling, where per-token weight updates during inference offer expressive temporal dynamics but are computationally expensive, while chunk-wise approximations are efficient but discard important update structure. The authors propose a method that derives a closed-form state transition under standard chunk-start gradient approximations, allowing exact reproduction of per-token fast-weight and momentum states at chunk boundaries without sacrificing parallelism. Models trained from scratch using this approach were evaluated on language modeling benchmarks and in-context retrieval tasks, where the method performed comparably to or better than existing Test-Time Training and hybrid attention baselines. The most striking gains appeared in length extrapolation, where the method maintained high accuracy on a passkey retrieval benchmark at context lengths far beyond those seen during training. The approach achieves training throughput comparable to efficient chunk-wise methods, demonstrating that expressivity and hardware efficiency need not be in conflict.
items.citation: Zeyun Zhong, Joya Chen, Manuel Martin et al.. Rethinking Expressivity and Efficiency in Test-Time Training. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Executive Summary: Surviving Sepsis Campaign: International Guidelines for Management of Sepsis and Septic Shock 2026
items.summary: The 2026 Surviving Sepsis Campaign guidelines represent a comprehensive update to international evidence-based recommendations for the identification and management of sepsis and septic shock in adult patients, building on prior iterations published since 2004. Developed using GRADE methodology with input from a broad multidisciplinary panel and patient representatives, the guidelines synthesized evidence through mid-2025 and produced a total of statements covering domains ranging from screening and early management to long-term outcomes. Notable new recommendations include the use of prehospital sepsis screening tools and prehospital antibiotic administration for patients with septic shock when transport times are prolonged, selective digestive tract decontamination in low-resistance settings, and active fluid removal following the acute resuscitation phase. Key changes from the 2021 guidelines include a shift toward recommending crystalloids alone over supplemental albumin for fluid resuscitation, a consolidated recommendation against routine empiric antifungal therapy, and updated guidance permitting either invasive or noninvasive blood pressure monitoring in septic shock. Several prior conditional recommendations were upgraded to strong recommendations, including prolonged beta-lactam infusion and antimicrobial de-escalation, while the recommendation for norepinephrine as first-line vasopressor was downgraded from strong to conditional relative to vasopressin and angiotensin II comparators.
items.citation: Hallie C. Prescott, Massimo Antonelli, Waleed Alhazzani et al.. Executive Summary: Surviving Sepsis Campaign: International Guidelines for Management of Sepsis and Septic Shock 2026. Critical Care Medicine. 2026

items.title: Accelerating scientific discovery with Co-Scientist
items.summary: Co-Scientist is a multi-agent AI system built on the Gemini platform, designed to augment scientific discovery by generating, critiquing, and refining novel research hypotheses conditioned on a scientist's research objectives and existing evidence. The system employs an asynchronous task execution framework for flexible compute scaling and a tournament evolution process for iterative hypothesis improvement, with automated evaluations confirming that increasing test-time compute continues to improve hypothesis quality. Although designed as a general-purpose tool, the system was validated in three biomedical domains: drug repurposing, novel target discovery, and elucidating mechanisms of antimicrobial resistance. Notably, Co-Scientist identified new drug-repurposing candidates and synergistic combination therapies for acute myeloid leukaemia that were subsequently confirmed through in vitro experiments. These real-world validations support the claim that such AI systems have meaningful potential to accelerate scientific discovery across complex research domains.
items.citation: Juraj Gottweis, Wei‐Hung Weng, Alexander Daryin et al.. Accelerating scientific discovery with Co-Scientist. Nature. 2026

items.title: A comprehensive review of green synthesis methods and applications of nanoparticles derived from plant extracts and microorganisms
items.summary: This review examines the field of green synthesis, in which biological entities such as plants, bacteria, fungi, algae, and yeast serve as natural reducing and stabilizing agents to produce nanoparticles without relying on toxic chemicals or harsh reaction conditions. The authors surveyed literature from multiple major scientific databases to critically assess advances in both plant-mediated and microorganism-assisted fabrication strategies, covering the underlying mechanisms of nanoparticle formation and how biological constituents influence particle size, morphology, and stability. The review evaluates the performance and limitations of green-synthesized nanoparticles across biomedical, agricultural, catalytic, and environmental applications, with particular attention to their photocatalytic and pollutant degradation potential for environmental remediation. The authors identify reproducibility, standardization, and scalability as key challenges currently hindering the translation of green nanotechnology from laboratory-scale research to practical industrial use. The review is intended to provide a structured critical foundation to guide future efforts aimed at overcoming these barriers and realizing the broader potential of biologically mediated nanomaterial production.
items.citation: Shoaeb Mohammad Syed, Shivam Kulkarni, Mayur Patil et al.. A comprehensive review of green synthesis methods and applications of nanoparticles derived from plant extracts and microorganisms. Discover Green Chemistry. 2026

items.title: Smart wearable and implantable biosensors for continuous health monitoring: materials, biocompatibility, and AI integration
items.summary: This review examines the current landscape of smart wearable and implantable biosensors designed for continuous, real-time monitoring of biophysical and biochemical signals in the context of personalized and preventive healthcare. The paper surveys advances in flexible, stretchable, and biocompatible materials that enable long-term comfort and seamless integration with the body, alongside multimodal and multi-analyte sensing approaches intended to improve measurement robustness. The role of artificial intelligence in enhancing signal processing and generating predictive health insights is also assessed. Despite notable progress, the review identifies persistent challenges including motion artifacts, energy autonomy, data privacy, and the clinical interpretability of sensor outputs. The authors synthesize findings across materials science, device architecture, and AI-assisted strategies to provide a comprehensive overview of the field's current state and remaining obstacles.
items.citation: Thirumalaisamy Suryaprabha, Chunghyeon Choi, Yanfang Wu et al.. Smart wearable and implantable biosensors for continuous health monitoring: materials, biocompatibility, and AI integration. npj Flexible Electronics. 2026

The authors identify a patient-centered accountability problem largely absent from existing literature: current frameworks for AI transparency and explainability in healthcare are clinician-centered and assume regulatory conditions that do not exist in low-resource settings, leaving patients unaware that autonomous systems are making or informing diagnostic decisions about them. Drawing on documented deployment cases involving tuberculosis detection, diabetic retinopathy screening, and mobile health chatbot triage in Tanzania, Zambia, and Ghana respectively, the paper demonstrates that these structural gaps are already manifest in active real-world deployments. In response, the authors synthesize literature on informed consent, algorithmic accountability, and explainable AI to propose three foundational principles: agent-aware informed consent, mandatory human override mechanisms, and contextually adapted explainability. Together, these principles are offered as a practical minimum governance standard for developers, health administrators, and policymakers operating in contexts where formal AI regulation remains nascent.
