items.title: Time-Aware Tranformer-Based Prediction Model for AECOPD
items.summary: The paper addresses the challenge of predicting acute exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD) in a timely manner, noting that conventional machine learning approaches relying on clinical and laboratory data introduce problematic delays. To overcome this limitation, the authors developed a Time-Aware transformer-based model designed for home monitoring scenarios, using only respiratory data collected from patients' daily-use ventilators. The model generates patient representations that capture both symptom characteristics and their temporal progression within the ventilator data stream. Experimental results show that this approach outperforms traditional methods across multiple classification tasks, suggesting it can improve both the speed and accuracy of AECOPD prediction.
items.citation: Weihao Qu, Ling Zheng, Dongyang Wang et al.. Time-Aware Tranformer-Based Prediction Model for AECOPD. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Prompt-Model Interaction Reaches the Fixed Points: A deterministic, task-free structural readout -- and the factorizations of it that failed
items.summary: This paper investigates whether the interaction between a prompt and a language model is a fundamental property of the model pair rather than an artifact of task-specific evaluation. Rather than using task accuracy as a readout, the authors study the fixed-point structure of a deterministic, short-window argmax map, censused from many starting points across six models, which removes any confound from stochastic generation or task machinery. They find that just nine tokens of conditioning can shift fixed-point fractions across most of their range and change structural classifications entirely, while instruction tuning worth substantial benchmark gains moves these structural classes not at all, demonstrating that prompt-model interaction reaches even this task-free readout at full magnitude. Attempts to explain the effect through interpretable factors—such as prefix length, prose versus markup content, a universal direction, or attention-sink mechanisms—each failed when tested more broadly, with the attention-sink account predicting the correct sign at no better than chance and breaking down on randomly constructed inputs. The authors conclude that on this readout the prompt-model pair is the irreducible unit of explanation, and they identify a recurring analytical error they call applying a criterion with a shape to a quantity with no room to vary.
items.citation: Nicolás Vera Zúñiga. Prompt-Model Interaction Reaches the Fixed Points: A deterministic, task-free structural readout -- and the factorizations of it that failed. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Beyond Fault Localization: A Trajectory-Level Study of LLM Agents for Microservice Root Cause Analysis
items.summary: This paper investigates automated root cause analysis (RCA) for microservice systems, arguing that conventional evaluations focused solely on whether an agent correctly identifies the responsible service are insufficient because they obscure the quality of the diagnostic reasoning and fault-propagation paths. To address this, the authors developed a trajectory-level evaluation framework that assesses agent diagnostic processes against manually curated fault-propagation paths, analyzing thousands of diagnostic trajectories to characterize how agents investigate faults and use retrieved telemetry. They found a systematic disconnect between answer correctness and diagnostic quality, where an agent can localize a fault source while failing to reconstruct how it propagated, and identified recurring failure modes including omission of decisive evidence, misinterpretation of retrieved evidence, and unsupported inference. Based on this taxonomy, the authors developed DiagGuard, a two-stage architecture that grounds diagnoses in available observations before localization and then audits them against retrieved evidence. Applied in an independent evaluation setting, DiagGuard substantially improved localization accuracy, demonstrating that trajectory-level evaluation reveals limitations hidden by final-answer metrics and offers actionable paths to improving automated RCA systems.
items.citation: Qisheng Lu, Aoyang Fang, Junjielong Xu et al.. Beyond Fault Localization: A Trajectory-Level Study of LLM Agents for Microservice Root Cause Analysis. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Fault Diagnosis of Dynamic Systems Under Unknown Operating Conditions: A Condition-Guided Selective Adaptation Approach
items.summary: The paper addresses the challenge of diagnosing faults in dynamic industrial systems when operating conditions are unknown or changing, a scenario that causes distribution shifts that degrade conventional diagnostic models. The authors propose a condition-guided selective adaptation framework that combines two stages: an offline phase using a continuous operating-condition adversarial learning strategy with progressive training to improve model generalization, and an online phase that exploits residual operating-condition responses to identify reliable unlabeled samples from streaming data for model updating. The approach was evaluated on real-world gearbox and motor datasets, where it outperformed existing state-of-the-art methods in diagnostic accuracy while keeping test-time computationally efficient, suggesting practical viability for industrial deployment.
items.citation: Jiaming Liu, Zeyi Liu, Hongshuo Zhao et al.. Fault Diagnosis of Dynamic Systems Under Unknown Operating Conditions: A Condition-Guided Selective Adaptation Approach. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Event-Time Confounding Under Bursty Human Dynamics
items.summary: This paper investigates a systematic bias in studies of digital behavior that measure user activity following self-initiated events, such as opening an AI assistant or clicking a recommendation. The authors argue that because users initiate these events during ongoing task episodes, the elevated activity observed afterward may simply reflect the natural continuation of those episodes rather than any causal effect of the event itself. Using cross-surface web logs spanning AI, shopping, news, coding, and reference interactions, they demonstrate that activity rises broadly before these events and peaks prior to the moment of event occurrence, a signature inconsistent with a causal interpretation. Critically, they validate this bias using known-null timestamps that have no causal effect, showing these null events still reproduce a substantial fraction of the post-event activity excess seen for real events, with the confounding concentrated at active moments and absent during quiet ones. The authors formalize this episode-selection bias theoretically, show why standard controls like user fixed effects and activity matching fail because the confound is within-user and time-varying, and release a diagnostic protocol and audit tool, concluding that post-event activity volume alone cannot identify genuine effects without comparing similar episodes that differ only in whether the event occurred.
items.citation: Michael Iannelli, Alan Ai. Event-Time Confounding Under Bursty Human Dynamics. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Biosensing technologies for foodborne pathogen detection and healthcare: principles, emerging materials, and intelligent platforms
items.summary: This review examines the current landscape of biosensing technologies designed to detect priority foodborne pathogens, including *Escherichia coli*, *Salmonella*, and *Listeria monocytogenes*, which continue to threaten global public health. The authors survey electrochemical, optical, and microfluidic sensing platforms, with particular attention to how advances in functional nanomaterials, aptamers, nanozymes, and surface engineering strategies have improved sensor sensitivity, specificity, and performance in complex food matrices. A central focus is the integration of artificial intelligence and machine learning into biosensor systems, enabling intelligent pattern recognition, real-time analytics, and high-throughput multiplexing that transform conventional detection tools into smart diagnostic devices. The review critically evaluates biosensor design principles, signal transduction mechanisms, and performance validation, while identifying persistent challenges such as matrix interference, bioreceptor instability, manufacturing scalability, and the absence of regulatory standardization, alongside mitigation strategies including ratiometric sensing, microfluidic pre-treatment, and explainable AI. Looking forward, the authors outline a vision for self-powered biosensors, modular pathogen detection panels, blockchain-integrated traceability, and standardized validation pipelines as pathways toward regulation-ready platforms for next-generation food safety monitoring.
items.citation: Purshottam J. Assudani, Balakrishnan . P., Anny Leema A et al.. Biosensing technologies for foodborne pathogen detection and healthcare: principles, emerging materials, and intelligent platforms. Microchimica Acta. 2026

items.title: Machine learning–empowered smartphone platforms for sustainable point-of-care bacterial detection
items.citation: Rzgar Sirwan Raza, Shilan Arif Fatah, Sameera Sh. Mohammed Ameen et al.. Machine learning–empowered smartphone platforms for sustainable point-of-care bacterial detection. Talanta. 2026

items.title: From bench to bedside: the promise and roadblocks of extracellular vesicle therapeutics
items.summary: This review examines the current state of extracellular vesicle-based therapeutics, focusing on the gap between their promising biological properties and their limited clinical translation. The authors systematically identify the core barriers preventing EV therapies from advancing beyond the preclinical stage, including difficulties in isolation, storage stability, characterization, biosafety evaluation, and quality control. They then survey emerging technologies intended to overcome these bottlenecks, such as advanced bioreactors for scalable production, microfluidic platforms for high-purity separation, single-vesicle analysis methods to address population heterogeneity, and machine learning tools to improve standardization and clinical decision-making. The review concludes by discussing future priorities around standardizing manufacturing processes, strengthening safety assessment frameworks, and achieving regulatory compliance. Overall, the authors argue that systematically addressing these translational challenges is essential to realizing the therapeutic potential of extracellular vesicles in clinical settings.
items.citation: Jing Zhang, Yuanwei Pan, Peng She et al.. From bench to bedside: the promise and roadblocks of extracellular vesicle therapeutics. Theranostics. 2026

items.title: Zinc finger protein arrays in an epoxy-functionalized, pump-free microfluidic device for amplification-free, colorimetric detection of double-stranded DNA.
items.summary: This study developed a microfluidic platform for detecting pathogen-specific double-stranded DNA without requiring amplification, denaturation, or labeling. The researchers engineered zinc finger proteins targeting the *stx2* gene of *E. coli* O157 and covalently attached them to epoxy-functionalized surfaces within a pump-free, capillary-driven microfluidic device, coupling detection to sequence-enabled reassembly of β-lactamase for a colorimetric readout. The device operates via capillary wicking consistent with Lucas-Washburn behavior, produces a visible yellow-to-red color shift upon target binding, and completes detection at ambient temperature in approximately ten minutes. The platform achieved low picomolar sensitivity and demonstrated strong specificity, generating significantly higher signals only for the cognate target sequence compared to non-target and irrelevant DNA. This work presents a low-cost, instrument-free approach to point-of-care pathogen detection by translating programmable protein-DNA recognition into a practical microfluidic format.
items.citation: Bhuiyan SAM, Shumway R, Trinkle C et al.. Zinc finger protein arrays in an epoxy-functionalized, pump-free microfluidic device for amplification-free, colorimetric detection of double-stranded DNA.. The Analyst. 2026

items.title: Artificial Intelligence-Empowered Single-Cell Phenotyping for Rapid, Automated Pathogen Diagnostics.
items.summary: This paper developed an integrated diagnostic platform combining microfluidic single-cell bacterial detection with artificial intelligence to accelerate bacterial identification and antimicrobial susceptibility testing, addressing the clinical problem that conventional diagnostics require one to two days and contribute to inappropriate antibiotic use. The platform uses a microfluidic device to expose individual bacterial cells to controlled antibiotic concentrations under time-lapse phase-contrast microscopy, with a U-Net-based deep learning model automatically segmenting and quantifying drug responses at the single-cell level. The AI model demonstrated high accuracy in identifying individual Escherichia coli cells with negligible false-positive detections on bacteria-free images. Applied to susceptibility testing, the system quantified dose-dependent growth inhibition and determined minimum inhibitory concentrations for two antibiotics within two hours, with results consistent with standard broth microdilution methods. The platform was additionally shown to distinguish bacterial species including Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus in blood matrices, demonstrating its potential for rapid, automated, and clinically relevant pathogen diagnostics.
items.citation: Khadka S, Raahat B, Tragoudas S et al.. Artificial Intelligence-Empowered Single-Cell Phenotyping for Rapid, Automated Pathogen Diagnostics.. Advanced science (Weinheim, Baden-Wurttemberg, Germany). 2026

items.title: Microfluidic and Paper-Based Recombinase Polymerase Amplification Systems for Decentralized Diagnostics and Biosurveillance.
items.summary: This review examines the integration of recombinase polymerase amplification with microfluidic and paper-based platforms for decentralized molecular diagnostics. Because RPA operates rapidly at mild temperatures without the extensive thermal cycling required by PCR, it is well suited to compact, low-power, field-deployable formats when combined with centrifugal chips, capillary-driven systems, paper-based analytical devices, electrochemical biosensors, CRISPR-assisted detection, and sample-to-answer cartridges. The authors survey recent advances across biomedical diagnostics, food safety testing, environmental monitoring, and One Health biosurveillance, encompassing applications ranging from respiratory viruses and parasitic diseases to antimicrobial-resistance tracking and airborne pathogen screening. A notable trend identified is the incorporation of smartphone imaging, artificial intelligence-assisted interpretation, digital partitioning, and cloud connectivity into rapid testing workflows to enhance portability, consistency, and diagnostic decision-making. The review concludes that while practical barriers such as sample preparation, multiplex stability, reagent storage, and regulatory validation remain, continued convergence of RPA chemistry with these emerging detection and data technologies is expected to yield more robust and accessible molecular diagnostic systems.
items.citation: Wang HM, Lee SZ, Fu LM. Microfluidic and Paper-Based Recombinase Polymerase Amplification Systems for Decentralized Diagnostics and Biosurveillance.. Micromachines. 2026

items.title: Smart wearable and implantable biosensors for continuous health monitoring: materials, biocompatibility, and AI integration
items.summary: This review examines smart wearable and implantable biosensors designed for continuous, real-time monitoring of biophysical and biochemical signals in the context of personalized and preventive healthcare. The authors survey advances in flexible, stretchable, and biocompatible materials that enable long-term device comfort and seamless integration with the body, alongside multimodal and multi-analyte sensing approaches that improve measurement robustness. The review also covers the integration of artificial intelligence for enhanced signal processing and predictive health insights. Despite these advances, the paper identifies persistent challenges including motion artifacts, energy autonomy, data privacy, and the clinical interpretability of sensor outputs. The work synthesizes current knowledge across materials science, device architecture, and AI-assisted strategies to outline the state of the field.
items.citation: Thirumalaisamy Suryaprabha, Chunghyeon Choi, Yanfang Wu et al.. Smart wearable and implantable biosensors for continuous health monitoring: materials, biocompatibility, and AI integration. npj Flexible Electronics. 2026

items.title: Exosomal bioactive molecules: molecular regulation, functional heterogeneity, and translational implications in disease diagnostics and therapeutics
items.summary: This review paper examines exosomes, nanoscale extracellular vesicles that mediate intercellular communication by carrying bioactive cargo including proteins, lipids, and nucleic acids, with a focus on understanding their molecular regulation and clinical utility. The authors synthesize current knowledge of the molecular machinery governing exosome biogenesis and cargo loading, including the roles of endosomal sorting complexes, lipid domains, RNA-binding proteins, and post-translational modifications that collectively determine cargo heterogeneity. The review also surveys modern analytical technologies and omics platforms used to characterize exosomal content for diagnostic applications, particularly in liquid biopsies for cancer, metabolic disorders, and neurodegenerative diseases. On the therapeutic side, the paper explores the potential of both native and engineered exosomes for drug delivery, wound healing, and neuroregeneration, and discusses ongoing clinical translation efforts. The authors identify persistent translational barriers such as isolation standardization and targeting specificity, while highlighting emerging approaches including synthetic exosome mimetics and artificial intelligence-driven diagnostics as strategies to advance exosome-based precision medicine.
items.citation: Victor U. Chigozie. Exosomal bioactive molecules: molecular regulation, functional heterogeneity, and translational implications in disease diagnostics and therapeutics. Clinical and Experimental Medicine. 2026

items.title: Comprehensive Review on Candidemia: Epidemiology, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Future Directions
items.summary: This review examines candidemia, a serious bloodstream infection caused by Candida species that represents a major source of hospital-acquired illness with high mortality and significant healthcare burden. The authors conducted a comprehensive literature synthesis covering the epidemiology, species distribution, and origins of candidemia, alongside an evaluation of both conventional and emerging diagnostic technologies. The review critically assesses current antifungal therapeutic strategies, including empiric and targeted regimens, management of mixed infections, host-drug interactions, and the growing problem of antifungal resistance, with particular attention to the potential role of combination therapy. Novel agents currently in clinical trials and compounds directed at new fungal targets are highlighted as part of the evolving treatment landscape. Looking ahead, the authors identify artificial intelligence-assisted diagnostics, vaccine-based prophylaxis, and synergistic treatment approaches as promising future directions for improving candidemia management.
items.citation: Haojie Dong, Minghui Song, Jingfang Sun et al.. Comprehensive Review on Candidemia: Epidemiology, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Future Directions. iFungi. 2026

items.title: Efficient Event Generation for High-Multiplicity LHC Processes: An End-to-End GPU Workflow with Normalizing Flows
items.summary: This paper addresses the computational challenge of generating large samples of unweighted events for high-multiplicity particle collision processes at the LHC, where standard approaches are bottlenecked by costly matrix-element evaluations and poor unweighting efficiencies. The authors developed the first fully GPU-resident end-to-end event-generation workflow, combining normalizing flow models as phase-space proposals with the parton-level generator Pepper, keeping all data exchange between the control layer and the matrix-element evaluator directly in device memory to minimize overhead. The normalizing flows are trained using online updates with sample replay and deployed across multiple partonic subprocesses, with the study comparing subprocess-specific flows against grouped conditional flows that share parameters among related subprocesses. The workflow was benchmarked on several high-multiplicity processes including multi-jet and top-quark pair production, demonstrating end-to-end speedups of up to two orders of magnitude over standalone Pepper on four high-end GPUs, reducing what would otherwise be a multi-week computation to less than a single day. The authors conclude that this approach makes billion-event production practical and offers a viable path toward relieving the Monte Carlo statistics bottleneck in high-multiplicity collider physics analyses.
items.citation: Enrico Bothmann, Joshua Isaacson, Claudius Krause et al.. Efficient Event Generation for High-Multiplicity LHC Processes: An End-to-End GPU Workflow with Normalizing Flows. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Maxwell's Demon in Markov Chain Monte Carlo: Cooling Information Flow and Entropy Balance
items.summary: This paper examines Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithms through the lens of thermodynamic analogies, specifically by drawing a formal parallel between the accept/reject mechanism and Maxwell's Demon. The authors identify the acceptance module as the demon, which measures proposed moves, stores outcomes in a single decision bit, and uses that information to guide probability currents toward the target distribution. They show that the decision bit carries genuine Shannon mutual information about the proposal, but only its directional component contributes to what the authors term a cooling information flow. The central result is a decomposition of the relative-entropy relaxation rate into two distinct contributions: a useful cooling term and a housekeeping circulation term arising from nonreversibility. This framework provides a principled way to separate productive convergence toward the target distribution from irreducible entropy production associated with nonequilibrium steady-state circulation in non-reversible chains.
items.citation: Masayuki Ohzeki. Maxwell's Demon in Markov Chain Monte Carlo: Cooling Information Flow and Entropy Balance. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Dirac Surface States and Nonlocal Quantum Tunneling in Topological Semiconductor Mo$_2$SeTe$_3$ for High-Performance Tunnel FETs
items.summary: This study investigates the quasi-two-dimensional transition-metal chalcogenide Mo₂SeTe₃ as a candidate material for low-power quantum electronic devices using first-principles calculations combined with device-level simulations. The material is identified as a weak topological semiconductor, exhibiting spin-orbit coupling-driven band inversion, an indirect bulk bandgap, and symmetry-protected Dirac surface states confirmed through Wannier charge-center evolution and Z₂ invariant analysis with weak topological indices. Beyond its topological properties, Mo₂SeTe₃ demonstrates dynamical and mechanical stability, strong optical anisotropy, broad infrared-to-visible absorption, and favorable thermoelectric transport characteristics including enhanced carrier mobility under n-type doping. A dual-source tunnel field-effect transistor implemented via TCAD simulations with nonlocal band-to-band tunneling achieves subthreshold switching below the thermionic limit, a high ON/OFF current ratio, and improved tunneling efficiency attributed to SOC-induced orbital hybridization and topologically enhanced interband coupling. The authors conclude that Mo₂SeTe₃ represents a multifunctional quantum material platform suitable for both topological applications and next-generation energy-efficient nanoelectronics.
items.citation: Zafar Sadik Mehrub, Suvodip Kundu Arnob, Md. Tareq Mahmud et al.. Dirac Surface States and Nonlocal Quantum Tunneling in Topological Semiconductor Mo$_2$SeTe$_3$ for High-Performance Tunnel FETs. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Dynamics of localized solutions in three core coupled waveguides with quasi-periodic nonlinearity
items.summary: The paper investigates how solitons behave in a system of three coupled waveguides where the nonlinearity governing inter-waveguide interactions is spatially modulated in a quasi-periodic fashion. By varying the modulation parameters, the authors analyze the evolution of soliton profiles and their mutual interactions within this coupled system. They find that the interplay between quasi-periodic nonlinearity and waveguide parameters gives rise to complex dynamics, including regimes of soliton attraction and repulsion. The results advance understanding of how quasi-periodic nonlinear modulation shapes localized wave behavior in multi-core waveguide systems, with suggested relevance for nonlinear optics and photonic device applications.
items.citation: Bruno M. Miranda, Ardiley T. Avelar, Wesley B. Cardoso et al.. Dynamics of localized solutions in three core coupled waveguides with quasi-periodic nonlinearity. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Invisible Agents, Uninformed Patients: Towards Responsible Deployment Of Autonomous AI Diagnostic Agents In Sub-Saharan Africa
items.summary: This paper examines the deployment of autonomous AI diagnostic agents across eHealth platforms in sub-Saharan Africa, focusing on the governance and ethical gaps that have emerged as these systems outpace regulatory infrastructure. The authors identify a critical patient-centered problem: existing frameworks for AI accountability and transparency in healthcare are largely clinician-focused and assume regulatory conditions that do not exist in low-resource settings, leaving patients largely unaware that autonomous systems are making or informing decisions about their care. Drawing on documented real-world deployments in Tanzania, Zambia, and Ghana involving tuberculosis detection, diabetic retinopathy screening, and mobile health chatbot triage, the paper demonstrates that structural accountability gaps are already present in active use. In response, the authors synthesize literature on informed consent, algorithmic accountability, and explainable AI to propose three foundational principles: agent-aware informed consent, human override as a structural requirement, and contextually adapted explainability. These principles are offered as a practical minimum standard for developers, health administrators, and policymakers operating in contexts where formal AI regulation remains nascent.
items.citation: Percy Brown, Kweku Yamoah. Invisible Agents, Uninformed Patients: Towards Responsible Deployment Of Autonomous AI Diagnostic Agents In Sub-Saharan Africa. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Beyond Fault Localization: A Trajectory-Level Study of LLM Agents for Microservice Root Cause Analysis
items.summary: This paper investigates automated root cause analysis for microservice systems, arguing that existing evaluations are too narrow because they only measure whether an agent correctly identifies the faulty service without examining the reasoning process or fault-propagation path leading to that conclusion. The authors developed a trajectory-level evaluation framework that assesses agent diagnostic processes against manually curated fault-propagation paths, applying it to analyze thousands of diagnostic trajectories from a public benchmark. They found a fundamental disconnect between answer correctness and diagnostic quality, where agents can pinpoint a fault source while failing to reconstruct how it propagated, and identified recurring failure modes including omission of decisive evidence, misinterpretation of retrieved telemetry, and unsupported inference. Based on this taxonomy, they designed DiagGuard, a two-stage architecture that grounds the diagnosis in available observations before localization and then audits the result against retrieved evidence. Testing in an independent setting demonstrated that DiagGuard meaningfully improved fault localization accuracy, supporting the claim that trajectory-level evaluation reveals hidden limitations and offers actionable improvements over final-answer metrics alone.
items.citation: Qisheng Lu, Aoyang Fang, Junjielong Xu et al.. Beyond Fault Localization: A Trajectory-Level Study of LLM Agents for Microservice Root Cause Analysis. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Biosensing technologies for foodborne pathogen detection and healthcare: principles, emerging materials, and intelligent platforms
items.summary: This review examines advanced biosensing technologies designed for the rapid and accurate detection of priority foodborne pathogens, specifically Escherichia coli, Salmonella, and Listeria monocytogenes, with implications for both food safety and clinical healthcare. The authors survey electrochemical, optical, and microfluidic sensing platforms, emphasizing how innovations in functional nanomaterials, aptamers, nanozymes, and surface engineering strategies have substantially improved sensor sensitivity, specificity, and performance in complex food matrices. A central theme is the integration of artificial intelligence and machine learning into these biosensing systems, enabling intelligent pattern recognition, real-time analytics, and high-throughput multiplexed detection that transforms conventional sensors into smart diagnostic tools. The review critically addresses persistent challenges including matrix interference, bioreceptor instability, manufacturing scalability, and the absence of regulatory standardization, while proposing mitigation approaches such as ratiometric sensing, microfluidic sample pre-treatment, explainable AI, and printable electronics. Looking ahead, the authors outline a vision for self-powered biosensors, modular pathogen detection panels, blockchain-integrated data management, and standardized validation pipelines to facilitate the deployment of robust, regulation-ready platforms for next-generation food safety monitoring.
items.citation: Purshottam J. Assudani, Balakrishnan . P., Anny Leema A et al.. Biosensing technologies for foodborne pathogen detection and healthcare: principles, emerging materials, and intelligent platforms. Microchimica Acta. 2026

items.title: Graphene oxide as smart sustainable nanomaterial: a versatile multifunctional material with transformative potential in advanced materials science research
items.summary: This review paper examines graphene oxide, a two-dimensional carbon-based nanomaterial, as a versatile and sustainable platform for addressing challenges across energy, environmental, and healthcare domains. The authors survey the synthesis chemistry and property modification strategies that underpin graphene oxide's distinctive characteristics, including its tunable band gap, high surface area, structural flexibility, and capacity for surface functionalization spanning zero- to three-dimensional architectures. The review covers a broad range of applications, including adsorption and photocatalytic degradation of pollutants and microplastics, photocatalytic hydrogen production and carbon dioxide reduction, battery technologies, ultra-sensitive molecular detection via surface-enhanced Raman scattering, and biomedical uses. The authors highlight that graphene oxide can perform effectively as a standalone material across these diverse fields, underscoring its multifunctional and transformative potential. However, the review also acknowledges persistent challenges such as scalability limitations, long-term stability concerns, and reproducibility issues, and proposes potential solutions to support sustainable and industrially viable future applications.
items.citation: S.N. Thakur, Ayush Badoni, Rupam Sharma et al.. Graphene oxide as smart sustainable nanomaterial: a versatile multifunctional material with transformative potential in advanced materials science research. npj Materials Sustainability. 2026

items.title: Comprehensive Review on Candidemia: Epidemiology, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Future Directions
items.summary: This review paper examines candidemia, a serious bloodstream infection caused by Candida species that represents a major source of hospital-acquired infections with high mortality and substantial healthcare burden. The authors synthesize current knowledge spanning the epidemiology, species distribution, and origins of candidemia, alongside a critical evaluation of existing diagnostic methods and their limitations. The review assesses emerging diagnostic technologies with potential to improve detection performance, and thoroughly examines therapeutic strategies including empiric and targeted antifungal regimens, management of mixed infections, host-drug interactions, and the growing challenge of antifungal resistance. The paper also highlights advances in drug development, including agents in clinical trials and compounds targeting novel fungal pathways. Looking forward, the authors explore future directions such as artificial intelligence applications in diagnostics, vaccine-based prophylaxis, and combination treatment strategies, aiming to guide clinicians and researchers in addressing evolving challenges in candidemia management.
items.citation: Haojie Dong, Minghui Song, Jingfang Sun et al.. Comprehensive Review on Candidemia: Epidemiology, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Future Directions. iFungi. 2026

items.title: Self-Cleaning Electrochemical Biosensor Based on MCOF@Ag for Simultaneous Pathogen Detection and Photocatalytic Inactivation.
items.summary: This paper developed a dual-function electrochemical biosensor capable of both detecting and destroying bacterial pathogens using a single electrode material. The researchers synthesized silver nanoparticle-decorated metal-covalent organic framework composites that formed a nanoflower-like structure, then functionalized the resulting electrode with aptamers specific to Staphylococcus aureus. The biosensor achieved highly sensitive detection of the target bacterium across a broad concentration range with a limit of detection of a single colony-forming unit per milliliter. Beyond detection, the material's photocatalytic activity enabled near-complete inactivation of captured bacteria through reactive oxygen species generation under visible light within minutes, after which the electrode could be regenerated and reused. The work demonstrates that metal-covalent organic framework composites can serve as a unified platform for simultaneous pathogen sensing and antibacterial action, with implications for infectious disease surveillance and control.
items.citation: Bai Y, Xiao L, Cai L et al.. Self-Cleaning Electrochemical Biosensor Based on MCOF@Ag for Simultaneous Pathogen Detection and Photocatalytic Inactivation.. Analytical chemistry. 2026

items.title: A Modular APEX Biosensor Enables Sensitive and Visualized Monitoring of Viral Protease Activity.
items.summary: The paper developed modular biosensors designed to detect viral protease activity within living cells and to screen antiviral drug candidates under physiologically relevant conditions. Traditional approaches such as fluorescent protein assays and FRET-based methods suffer from non-specific conformational interference and fail to accurately capture intracellular inhibitory effects, motivating the need for a new platform. The researchers engineered two biosensors based on split ascorbate peroxidase fragments that reassemble upon protease-mediated cleavage of a specific recognition sequence, restoring enzymatic activity and generating amplified fluorescent signals. Using the coronavirus main protease as a model, one sensor achieved an exceptionally high signal-to-noise ratio for enzymatic detection, while the other accurately identified potent inhibitors and avoided the false positives common to conventional methods. By simply swapping the protease recognition sequence, the platform can be adapted to monitor proteases from a range of viruses, offering a flexible and reliable intracellular tool to accelerate broad-spectrum antiviral drug discovery.
items.citation: Li B, Dong B, Chen Y et al.. A Modular APEX Biosensor Enables Sensitive and Visualized Monitoring of Viral Protease Activity.. Virologica Sinica. 2026

items.title: Multiple cross displacement amplification coupled with a lateral flow biosensor for ultra-rapid and highly sensitive detection of <i>Escherichia coli</i> in neonatal sepsis.
items.summary: The study addressed the need for rapid and sensitive detection of *Escherichia coli* in neonatal sepsis, where conventional blood culture is slow and often insufficiently sensitive. Researchers developed a multiple cross-displacement amplification assay paired with a lateral flow biosensor targeting the *uidA* gene, using a ten-primer design optimized to run at a single temperature for forty minutes. The assay achieved femtogram-level sensitivity with no cross-reactivity against non-*E. coli* strains, and the complete workflow from nucleic acid extraction to visual result was completed within approximately one hour. Clinical validation using blood and cerebrospinal fluid specimens from neonates with suspected *E. coli* infection showed the assay achieved complete concordance with quantitative PCR while detecting a substantially higher proportion of positive cases than conventional culture. The authors conclude that this method offers a rapid, sensitive, and operationally simple approach well suited to point-of-care and resource-limited settings for early diagnosis of neonatal *E. coli* infection.
items.citation: Xiao R, Zou P, Zhou J et al.. Multiple cross displacement amplification coupled with a lateral flow biosensor for ultra-rapid and highly sensitive detection of <i>Escherichia coli</i> in neonatal sepsis.. Microbiology spectrum. 2026

items.title: Target-to-signal conversion and spatial enrichment cascade boost CRISPR/Cas12a biosensing for trace-level pathogen detection.
items.summary: This study developed a biosensor for detecting *Salmonella typhimurium*, a major cause of foodborne illness, at extremely low concentrations. The system integrates DNAzyme-catalysed amplification with hybridization chain reaction to convert pathogen-specific signals into branched DNA nanowires bearing protospacer adjacent motif sequences, which then activate CRISPR/Cas12a to cleave the nanowires and restore a quenched fluorescent signal. This cascade of target-to-signal conversion and spatial enrichment steps enables ultrasensitive detection across a broad linear range, achieving a very low limit of detection. The biosensor operates rapidly, requires straightforward handling, and demonstrated high sensitivity and selectivity under optimized conditions. The authors also propose that the platform is adaptable to other foodborne pathogens by substituting the recognition and primer sequences, suggesting broad applicability in food safety monitoring.
items.venue: Analytical methods : advancing methods and applications
items.citation: Liu Y, Yue X, Li B et al.. Target-to-signal conversion and spatial enrichment cascade boost CRISPR/Cas12a biosensing for trace-level pathogen detection.. Analytical methods : advancing methods and applications. 2026

items.title: Simultaneous Dual-Gene Detection of <i>Escherichia coli</i> O157:H7 Based on a CRISPR/Cas13-Mediated Biosensor.
items.summary: This study addressed the need for rapid, accurate detection of *Escherichia coli* O157:H7, a significant foodborne pathogen, by developing a one-pot CRISPR/Cas13-based biosensor capable of simultaneously targeting two key genetic markers that define the pathogen's serotype. The system exploited the distinct collateral cleavage preferences of two different Cas13 proteins to create dual fluorescence channels, allowing serotype-specific identification while reducing false positives, and integrated gene amplification via recombinase polymerase amplification, transcription, and CRISPR-mediated sensing into a single reaction tube. The biosensor achieved high sensitivity at a low detection limit and was validated using a mouse infection model, with results from fecal samples consistent with standard PCR methods. Compared to conventional CRISPR diagnostics, this dual-channel approach improves specificity and serotype discrimination while remaining simple, rapid, and suitable for field deployment, offering potential utility in clinical diagnostics, food safety monitoring, and infectious disease surveillance.
items.citation: He Y, Lin X, Zhang X et al.. Simultaneous Dual-Gene Detection of <i>Escherichia coli</i> O157:H7 Based on a CRISPR/Cas13-Mediated Biosensor.. JACS Au. 2026

items.title: Graphene foam biosensors for molecular diagnostics of antimicrobial resistance and emerging pathogen threats.
items.summary: This paper developed an electrochemical biosensor designed for rapid, point-of-care detection of antimicrobial resistance genes and emerging pathogen targets. The platform uses disposable graphene foam electrodes functionalized with pyrene-modified peptide nucleic acid probes, which are attached via π-π stacking to preserve the material's electronic properties and high surface area, enabling amplification-free and label-free nucleic acid detection. A key innovation is a heat-assisted functionalization protocol that reduces preparation time from hours to minutes while maintaining sensor performance. The biosensor demonstrated sensitive and selective detection of the colistin resistance gene, discriminating the true target from non-complementary sequences, and was readily retargeted to a second resistance gene simply by swapping the probe. The authors conclude that the platform offers a reproducible, scalable approach to decentralized molecular diagnostics for antimicrobial resistance and pandemic preparedness.
items.citation: Wang KY, Schulze H, Lozano Sanchez P et al.. Graphene foam biosensors for molecular diagnostics of antimicrobial resistance and emerging pathogen threats.. Biosensors & bioelectronics. 2026

items.title: From bench to bedside: the promise and roadblocks of extracellular vesicle therapeutics
items.summary: This review examines the current state and translational obstacles of extracellular vesicle-based therapeutics, which have gained attention for their biocompatibility, ability to carry biomolecules, and capacity to cross biological barriers. The authors systematically catalogue the core impediments preventing most EV products from advancing beyond preclinical stages, including difficulties in isolation, storage stability, characterization, biosafety evaluation, and quality control. They then survey emerging technologies proposed to address these bottlenecks, such as advanced bioreactors for scalable production, microfluidic platforms for high-purity separation, single-vesicle analysis to manage heterogeneity, and machine learning tools to support standardization and clinical decision-making. The review concludes by outlining future priorities around standardizing production processes, improving safety assessment frameworks, and achieving regulatory compliance. Overall, the authors argue that resolving these intertwined technical and regulatory challenges is essential to accelerating the translation of EV therapies into clinical practice.
items.citation: Jing Zhang, Yuanwei Pan, Peng She et al.. From bench to bedside: the promise and roadblocks of extracellular vesicle therapeutics. Theranostics. 2026

items.title: Oxidative Stress in Health and Disease: Mechanisms and Therapeutic Perspectives
items.summary: This review examines the dual role of reactive oxygen species in biological systems, where they serve both as essential signaling molecules at physiological levels and as drivers of cellular damage when produced in excess. The paper synthesizes current knowledge on the major types, cellular sources, and molecular mechanisms by which ROS regulate normal physiology and contribute to oxidative stress-related pathology. The authors survey contemporary and emerging methodologies for detecting and quantifying ROS in clinical and preclinical settings, including biochemical assays, fluorescent probes, biosensors, and advanced imaging approaches. The review connects oxidative stress mechanisms to the pathophysiology of major diseases such as cancer, diabetes, cardiovascular conditions, neurodegeneration, and inflammatory disorders. The authors conclude by advocating for precision redox medicine strategies that integrate improved ROS detection technologies with targeted antioxidant-based diagnostics and therapeutics.
items.citation: Shehwaz Anwar, Hajed Obaid A. Alharbi, Ali Yousif Babiker et al.. Oxidative Stress in Health and Disease: Mechanisms and Therapeutic Perspectives. International Journal of Molecular Sciences. 2026

items.title: A review of applications of machine learning in quantum dots research
items.summary: This review examines how machine learning has been applied across the breadth of quantum dot research, spanning experimental device control, materials synthesis, sensing, photonic applications, and computational modeling of quantum systems. The authors surveyed recent data-driven approaches with particular attention to how these methods are embedded within established physical workflows rather than deployed independently. They found that machine learning most commonly serves to replace time-consuming fitting procedures, guide experimental sampling, or approximate computationally intensive simulations, with recurring methodological patterns including supervised learning on limited datasets, transfer learning across device instances, and hybrid approaches that incorporate physical constraints. The review also identifies persistent limitations such as dataset bias, poor cross-laboratory transferability, absence of standardized benchmarks, and inadequate treatment of uncertainty. The authors conclude that machine learning is best understood as a complementary tool whose reliability depends critically on integration with physical insight, sound experimental design, and rigorous validation.
items.citation: Ivan Malashin, Dmitry Martysyuk, Vladimir Nelyub et al.. A review of applications of machine learning in quantum dots research. Discover Nano. 2026

items.title: Classical versus non-classical photon states for detecting vacuum non-linearity
items.summary: The paper investigates whether the detectability of quantum electrodynamic vacuum nonlinearity can be enhanced by modifying the initial quantum state of light used in experimental schemes designed to verify this fundamental prediction. Quantum electrodynamics predicts that the vacuum itself behaves as a nonlinear optical medium, and many verification schemes look for photons appearing in modes that would otherwise be empty. The authors consider replacing the vacuum state in those signal modes with either classical or non-classical photon states, such as squeezed light, and analyze the resulting effect on measurement sensitivity. They find that injecting such modified photon states into the relevant modes can significantly improve the detectability of the vacuum nonlinearity signal compared to standard approaches.
items.citation: N. Ahmadiniaz, C. Kohlfürst, R. Shaisultanov et al.. Classical versus non-classical photon states for detecting vacuum non-linearity. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Mining beyond Earth with Space Robots: Exploration, Sampling, and Extraction
items.summary: This paper provides a comprehensive review of space mining robotics, covering the technologies and systems needed to extract resources such as helium-3, water, minerals, and asteroid deposits for sustained human space exploration and commercial purposes. The authors propose a systematic six-stage architecture that organizes space mining activities into three broad phases: exploration via remote sensing and in situ robotic detection, sampling through single- and multi-robot excavation, and extraction culminating in resource integration for in situ construction or transport back to Earth. The review also catalogs available research resources including real-world mission data, terrestrial analog datasets, and simulation environments to support the field. The paper identifies key open challenges posed by harsh space environments, communication delays, and high launch costs, and outlines a strategic research roadmap aimed at advancing autonomous robotic systems to close existing technological gaps. Ultimately, the authors frame these developments as essential steps toward establishing a sustainable off-world economy.
items.citation: Dong Li, Dujun Nie, Xiaotong Zhang et al.. Mining beyond Earth with Space Robots: Exploration, Sampling, and Extraction. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Invisible Agents, Uninformed Patients: Towards Responsible Deployment Of Autonomous AI Diagnostic Agents In Sub-Saharan Africa
items.summary: This paper examines the ethical and governance challenges that arise when autonomous AI diagnostic agents are deployed in sub-Saharan African healthcare settings, where patients often remain unaware that non-human systems are making or influencing clinical decisions about them. The authors argue that existing frameworks for AI accountability and transparency in healthcare are predominantly clinician-centered and assume robust regulatory environments that do not reflect the realities of low-resource contexts, leaving a structural accountability gap from a patient perspective. Drawing on documented cases of AI deployment in Tanzania, Zambia, and Ghana, the paper demonstrates that problems around inadequate informed consent, limited human oversight, and poorly adapted explainability are already manifesting in active systems. In response, the authors synthesize literature on informed consent, algorithmic accountability, and explainable AI to propose three foundational principles: agent-aware informed consent, mandatory human override mechanisms, and contextually adapted explainability. These principles are presented as a practical minimum standard intended to guide developers, health system administrators, and policymakers in regions where formal AI regulation has yet to mature.
items.citation: Percy Brown, Kweku Yamoah. Invisible Agents, Uninformed Patients: Towards Responsible Deployment Of Autonomous AI Diagnostic Agents In Sub-Saharan Africa. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Time-Aware Tranformer-Based Prediction Model for AECOPD
items.summary: The paper addresses the challenge of predicting acute exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD) in a timely manner, noting that conventional machine learning approaches relying on clinical and laboratory data introduce problematic delays. To overcome this, the authors developed a Time-Aware transformer-based model that operates exclusively on respiratory data collected from home ventilators, enabling a low-latency monitoring scenario. The model generates patient representations that capture both symptom patterns and their temporal progression within the ventilator data stream. Experimental results showed that this approach outperformed traditional methods across multiple classification tasks, suggesting it could meaningfully improve the speed and accuracy of AECOPD prediction in real-world home settings.
items.citation: Weihao Qu, Ling Zheng, Dongyang Wang et al.. Time-Aware Tranformer-Based Prediction Model for AECOPD. arXiv. 2026

items.title: VLASS Discovery of a Luminous Galactic Radio Transient Evolving on Decade Timescales
items.summary: This paper presents a detailed multiwavelength study of a newly discovered Galactic radio transient, VT J1906+0849, identified in the Very Large Array Sky Survey after more than two decades of non-detection in prior surveys. Radio observations trace the source's evolution from its first detection in 2005 through a peak flux and subsequent decline, with a late rebrightening, while its low Galactic latitude and optical-infrared counterpart confirm a Galactic origin at a distance placing it among the most radio-luminous known Galactic transients. Despite spectral signatures consistent with synchrotron self-absorption, interferometric observations reveal that the radio-emitting region has undergone little to no expansion over several years, and the source is unexpectedly faint in X-rays compared to known X-ray binaries. Near-infrared spectroscopy identifies a broad emission line interpreted as blueshifted hydrogen recombination emission tracing a persistent, asymmetric outflow of roughly two thousand kilometers per second. The authors propose that VT J1906+0849 may represent a young analog of the microquasar SS 433, in which a dense disk wind confines a continuously powered synchrotron jet, simultaneously explaining the compact radio structure and the suppression of bright X-ray emission.
items.citation: Jessie M. Miller, Gregg Hallinan, Dillon Dong et al.. VLASS Discovery of a Luminous Galactic Radio Transient Evolving on Decade Timescales. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Human-AI Collaboration in Requirements Engineering: Evidence of the Negative Effect of LLMs on Requirements Inspection
items.summary: This paper investigated whether large language model assistance improves human performance on requirements inspection, a software engineering practice aimed at identifying defects in requirements documents early in development. Using a controlled crossover experiment, participants inspected textual specifications both with and without LLM support, identifying and classifying requirements smells by type and severity while their task duration was recorded, with Bayesian regression models used to analyze outcomes. Contrary to optimistic expectations, LLM support was found to negatively affect smell detection accuracy while having no meaningful impact on severity classification or inspection time. The study also identified a learning effect across experimental periods, whereby skill development was attenuated when participants began the task with LLM assistance rather than without it. These findings suggest that LLM support not only fails to enhance novice inspectors' performance but may also impede the natural acquisition of requirements inspection skills when introduced from the outset.
items.citation: Giovanna Broccia, Julian Frattini, Chetan Arora et al.. Human-AI Collaboration in Requirements Engineering: Evidence of the Negative Effect of LLMs on Requirements Inspection. arXiv. 2026
